The mostly intact, empty ship has been slumbering here for eons without someone to pilot it. Shall we take it out for a spin?

items.name: Surface Piercers
items.desc: The surface expedition down to the seas of [From.Planet.GetName] has come across something strange. Great spikes of organic material pierce the surface of the water, made from some kind of fossilized coral or bone, stretching hundreds of meters towards the sky.\n\nThe spikes are found in claw-like clusters of up to a few dozen, and formations like these are commonplace everywhere except the very coldest polar seas. The spikes are porous, covered with perforations ranging in size up to that of a strike craft. Perhaps they are related to how these bio-structures propagate themselves?

items.name: Current Makers
items.desc: The expedition has finally managed to reach a set of long and evenly shaped bio-formations on the bottom of the planetary sea. Made of the same material as the surface-piercing spikes, these underwater formations appear to be some kind of organic pumping mechanism. The living network "breathes", and its exhalations cycle the current of the seas.\n\nThe size of these formations, as well as the sheer number of them across the ocean floor, hints that they are responsible for the unexplained underwater currents of [From.Planet.GetName].

items.name: The Hive Coral
items.desc: Another deep sea expedition has returned, and revealed the truth of the churning seas of [FromFrom.Planet.GetName]. All the strange organic formations on the planet are actually connected in a single, vast coral reef. This coral, as it turned out, is partly aware, although with an utterly alien mindset compared to our conception of sentient life. Through pheromones excreted in the water, it has more or less enslaved the rest of all the organisms in the sea, controlling their behavior and reproduction cycles to fit its own needs.\n\nIt seems to be completely benign, but it is a puppet master nonetheless. Is it simply the apex life form on this world? An intrusive alien parasite? Communicating with it seems impossible, so we may never know.

items.name: Bio-Savior
items.desc: After sequencing the alien DNA, a startling revelation was made: the global sea coral network is not only not native to this world, but it is in fact a bio-engineered construct rather than a natural formation. Beneath the thick carpet of alien coral is a fossilized extinction layer of the entire previous ecosystem of this world. It seems the coral, once introduced, gradually choked out all the native life and replaced it with an ecosystem tailored specifically for itself.\n\nThere are two main theories as to why this might have been done: either the artificial coral was introduced for benign reasons, and then it massively out-competed the local wildlife in an unexpected way, or it was deliberately constructed to be some sort of terrifying biological weapon to cleanse ocean worlds of native life.

items.name: Welcoming Committee
items.desc: It's all one giant bio-machine! Subsurface analysis indicates that the planet's oceans were once dead - no current or oxygen to sustain underwater life. This bio-engineered machine was introduced to the planet with the purpose of artificially jump starting the basic prerequisites of organic existence.\n\nApparently it worked, as underwater flora and fauna now thrives on the world. No trace was found of why such a colossal undertaking was carried out, nor by whom - was it perhaps some terraforming project by an unknown aquatic species with advanced biotechnology, seeking to create for themselves a new home?

items.name: Wounds on the Ocean Floor
items.desc: Closer inspection of [From.Planet.GetName] reveals that the bottom of the vast oceans look exceptionally strange - more like the surface of a moon or an asteroid - completely covered in impact craters. Craters like that tend to not appear on celestial bodies with atmosphere, and especially not on the ones with oceans.\n\nFurther studies must be made.

items.name: Otherworldly Waters
items.desc: The answer to the mysterious craters in the ocean floor was finally found in an analysis of the water itself. Traces of certain minerals and chemical compositions proved that the water did in fact not belong to the same planet. It was transported here in the form of gargantuan blocks of ice that were hurled down on the planet. The ice blocks crashed, cracked into splinters and melted, eventually covering almost the entire surface with water.\n\nIt was an absolutely monumental undertaking, but there is nothing that hints to why it was carried out.

items.name: Current Events
items.desc: The Science Ship in orbit of [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] picked up some unidentified energy readings from deep beneath the waves, and upon inspection the expedition discovered an ancient construction. A structure many kilometers long with a single purpose; to artificially create underwater currents.\n\nUnderwater circulation is vital for much aquatic life, and the current theory is that this planet was set up to be habitable for some aquatic, spacefaring species. It appears as if they never showed up.

items.name: Submerged Storage
items.desc: By following a strange energy signature our expedition managed to locate an alien communications array buried deep in the seabed. It contained information fragments, and once translated they told of the water-introduction project.\n\nAccording to the translation the entire ocean-making venture was done to create an immense submerged storage, but it does not specify what needed to be stored. Certainly not what requires an entire planet covered in water.

items.name: Climate Control
items.desc: Thanks to serendipitous sensory scan the Science Ship managed to isolate ancient building buried deep under the ocean floor. Getting the expedition there turned out to be very difficult, but the finding was grand.\n\nThe building was once a climate control center. It directed giant climate-altering machines in orbit. This was a terraforming project that was interrupted, but apparently the project had gotten far enough. Even without directed input, nature managed to thrive and eventually create the ecosystem that can be seen today.

items.name: Island Tunnels
items.desc: The surface expedition sent down to [From.Planet.GetName] started to investigate one of the round islands, and soon made a remarkable discovery. The island had a complex tunnel network running beneath it, winding through the strange, oily rock. These tunnels were remarkably even and round, and laced the entire island. They seem to be natural formations, not intentionally excavated, but they have certainly not been shaped in a conventional, geological manner.

items.name: Tunnels Everywhere
items.desc: As the surface expedition delved deeper into the round islands, two more discoveries were made: First, that every island seem to have a duplicate internal layout of tunnels beneath them. They vary slightly in size, but not in how they are laid out. The second discovery was even more astonishing: the islands aren't parts of the planet crust - they actually float! Their lower levels are filled with pockets of gas, which combined with the fairly brittle and porous island rock makes then buoyant.

items.name: Frozen Jelly
items.desc: The answer to the mystery of the floating islands was not found in the field of geology, but in biology. The islands are in fact enormous fossilized jellyfish creatures. Millions of years ago an ice age froze them all to death, after which their carcasses were fossilized into the islands seen bobbing around in the water today. Ages of debris accretion gave their exposed surface the look of natural islands, but beneath that they are entirely organic.

items.name: Natural Slumber
items.desc: They are not islands at all, but jellyfish! Each of these floating circles is in fact a giant invertebrate organism. And they aren't dead, either: the seemingly fossilized state is just a natural part of their life cycle. Over the course of thousands of years, these stony islands release sediment until they finally dissolve completely. The sediment contains microscopic polyps that eventually germinate in the water until they enter the next stage of their life cycle.

items.name: Big Ones Couldn't Cope
items.desc: They aren't islands at all. They are all alien organisms: jellyfish creatures that for some reason were artificially introduced to the ecosystem. It seems their introduction did not go exactly as planned, however. Most of the big ones died and fossilized - becoming the floating island archipelago - but the smaller jellyfish creatures assimilated and are now thriving in the oceans across the planet. Whether they will eventually share the fate of their bigger ancestors remains to be seen.

items.name: Hello/Goodbye
items.desc: By tracing weak energy trails - most likely left by space-faring vessels - one particular asteroid in the cluster was singled out. Closer inspection of the asteroid's surface confirmed the theory of prior space traffic as multiple signs of landing and takeoff were found on the rocky exterior.\n\nSensors also indicate cavities and tunnels within the asteroid, which may be excavated.

items.name: Stepping Stone
items.desc: Following small and narrow tunnels, the expedition team finally stumbled into the innermost sanctum; a vast and exquisitely crafted chamber adorned by sculptures carved directly into the rock. Translation of spiritual texts carved into the walls called the place "The Ninth Step", and it was apparently one of many destinations on a religious journey taken by the creating species.\n\nIf this was the ninth step, where are the preceding eight? And how many steps followed?

items.name: Deep Space Depot
items.desc: The reasons behind this well-visited asteroid became clear as the surface expedition encountered vast storage areas and silos dug into the asteroid. The dead rock served as a depot for some space-faring species, offering refueling and maintenance before sending ships even deeper into space. This would indicate an alien society devoid of FTL drive, but with an abundance of motivation to explore space.\n\nWhy the asteroid depot was abandoned remains unclear, but we managed to salvage a small yield of materials. Finders keepers!

items.name: Rise and Shine
items.desc: Getting inside the asteroid, the expedition made quite a fascinating discovery. Abandoned cryo-pods - hundreds of thousands of them - lined vast, dug out chambers. Each pod was opened and inactive, giving the impression that they had already fulfilled their purpose.\n\nThe current theory is that the asteroid served as some kind of colonization shuttle, hurled through space toward some prosperous habitat. When in proximity to its destination, automated systems woke up the slumbering cargo, and they left the asteroid in short-distance spacecraft to get to their new home.

items.name: Signs of Resistance
items.desc: The disturbances caused by the orbiting Science Ship's sensors are nothing compared to the complications being encountered down on the surface of [From.Planet.GetName]. Extreme magnetic fluctuations from some unknown source are making equipment go haywire.\n\nIt will be quite an ordeal to research this electromagnetic bedlam - but given enough time, answers will emerge.

items.name: That's So Metal
items.desc: Once the surface expedition managed to solve the problems with the malfunctioning equipment, the nature of the wild magnetic fluctuations started to reveal itself.\n\nThe raging oceans and rivers of lava down on [From.Planet.GetName] are in fact not made up of conventional magma - it's molten metal! Metals of this temperature tend not to have particularly strong magnetic properties; not even the sheer volume of molten metal on [From.Planet.GetName] should create electromagnetism on this scale. So what is causing it?

items.name: Wake of the Neutron Star
items.desc:
The Science Ship orbiting [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] has finally cracked the enigma of the magnetic fluctuations down on the planet.

Millions of years ago, the planet came into close proximity with a special kind of neutron star. The magnetism of this neutron star effectively boiled the metals inside [FromFrom.Planet.GetName], turning them into the molten oceans we see today. The electromagnetism we've encountered is but a lingering echo of the original, cataclysmic event.

Where the neutron star is now remains a mystery - a quite disturbing mystery.

items.name: Zapped!
items.desc:
The blatant disregard for conventional laws of physics has our science department considering "external forces" as an explanation for the strange properties of [FromFrom.Planet.GetName].

An impact crater - in combination with fusion drive particle traces found in orbit - suggests that the planet was fired upon by some kind of electric super-weapon at some point. The severity of the strike was such that all metals on the planet melted, and the planet is still crackling with residual electricity.

What warranted such tremendous attack? We'll never know.

items.name: For Science!
items.desc:
Once the sensors had been re-calibrated to compensate for the interference, a new discovery was made: an abandoned research station, located on a nearby moon. Fragments of data were salvaged from the almost entirely burned-out records, detailing an experiment involving a giant, artificial magnet on the planet's surface.

The experiment was a bit too successful. It turned the planet's entire, metal crust into molten pools with an electromagnetic charge so intense that it fried the research station in an instant.

Well... No progress without sacrifice.

items.name: Arcane Deciphering
items.desc: Study of the artifacts has advanced some of our research.

items.name: Arcane Deciphering
items.desc: While the artifacts we are researching have not yielded an immediate breakthrough, they are accelerating research in all fields.

items.name: Arcane Deciphering
items.desc: Study of the artifacts has yielded an unexpected breakthrough!

items.name: Find Military Applications
items.desc: What aspect shall we focus on?

items.name: Find Peaceful Applications
items.desc: What aspect shall we focus on?

items.name: Mega Art Installation: Perfection
items.desc: The greatness of the [From.Owner.GetName] is such that we can line the Exhibition Stations of our Mega Art Installation with priceless artifacts.\n\nLet the xenos look upon our works and despair.

items.name: Secrets of the Irassians
items.desc: Though it clearly did not save them, the Irassians were admittedly experts in the field of biology. Our scientists have adapted what was worthwhile from their findings.

items.name: Special Project Unlocked
items.desc: Our scientists have begun a special project to study the deeper secrets of the precursors.

items.name: Secrets of the Yuht
items.desc: The Yuht had efficient processes for removing hostile xeno presences from their hatchery worlds. We have successfully recreated this cleansing process.\n\nIt does have some concerning short term effects on the biosphere, but once it recovers, the planet should be more suitable to our needs.

items.name: Secrets of the First League
items.desc: The First League proves that reliance on other races is folly that leads to weakness and self-destruction. Some of their advanced construction methods may, however, be of possible use.

items.name: Secrets of the Cybrex
items.desc: The tale of the Cybrex is proof that our decision to outlaw artificial intelligence is a wise one.  Some of their findings related to megastructure engineering have the potential to be beneficial to our cause.

items.name: Secrets of the Vultaum
items.desc: The Vultaum appear to have accepted some fundamentally illogical concepts in their research. Their research into computing and virtual worlds had some advances that we shall incorporate into our own processes.

items.name: Secrets of the Vultaum
items.desc:
It seems that the Vultaum may have been correct after all.

We have replicated their experiments and come to similar conclusions. There is a moderate chance that we are, in fact, existing within a simulated world.

We do not have enough data to hypothesize why someone would create such a thing. Surely no one would create a universe as cruel and cold as this one for simple enjoyment.

The implications of this are profound, and we yield to your discretion as to our next steps.

items.name: Unfortunate News
items.desc: We regret to inform you that [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName] did not take the decision to end the research into the Vultaum well.\n\nThe notes they left behind drift off into mad ramblings before coming to the decision to 'continue the research', shortly before committing suicide.
items.trigger: exists = event_target:leading_vultaum_research_scientist

items.name: Stress Relief
items.desc: Reports indicate that the stress of leading the research into the Vultaum has affected [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName].\n\nThey have begun to make incredible leaps of logic that are greatly aiding our research, but have also begun self-medicating as a coping mechanism.
items.trigger: exists = event_target:leading_vultaum_research_scientist

items.name: Breakthrough
items.desc: Reports indicate that [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName] has benefited greatly the research project, and has begun to make incredible leaps of logic that are greatly aiding our research.
items.trigger: exists = event_target:leading_vultaum_research_scientist

items.name: Secrets of the Baol
items.desc: Studying the Baol has given us new insights into the spread of plant life and improved our terraforming processes.\n\nBy carefully tracking the changes that the Baol underwent during their loss of sentience we also learned much about the uplifting process, but have already mastered that technology.

items.name: Secrets of the Zroni
items.desc: We have successfully managed to integrate the Zroni artifacts into our research process. Their insights into psionic study will greatly aid our own research.

items.name: The First Layer
items.desc: The ruins seem to be centuries, if not millennia, old. At first it seems to be only a large open-air dome, but as we are excavating the outermost parts we quickly find ourselves in what appears to be the derelict slums of a city. As a large gate blocks our progress deeper into the city, our scientists speculate that it is split into a hierarchy, each layer holding one class of the people of the city.\n\nIt does not take long before one of our scientists finds alien remains in subterranean ruins under the broken concrete floor. After the first corpse is found, however, we start finding remains all over the slums, be it in the streets, in what would have been their homes, or hanging from the most remote parts of the ceiling. It is unclear what killed them, but it is a grisly sight.

items.name: The Second Layer
items.desc:
Whereas the first circle seemingly consisted of the ramshackle dwellings of the outcast and destitute, this second circle has more in common with the [Root.GetAdj] notion of proper urban planning.

We find several open squares our scientists assume used to be marketplaces, though anything from back then has long since decayed to the point where it is impossible to make out what it might have been.

It does not take long before we start finding unusual remains in this part of the dome too. They seem to have perished in much the same way as their poorer neighbors, and we find the dead strewn all over.

items.name: The Third Layer
items.desc:
When the gate into the third layer finally opens, our scientists - curious about what they will find next - flood into what is soon identified as a yet wealthier region of the old dome. At this point we can make confident assumptions about what to expect from this city.

Shortly after we enter the layer, one of our people suddenly turns around and savagely attacks a colleague. The victim is already dead on the ground by the time the unexpected assailant is restrained. In the aftermath we are completely unable to get anything sensible out of the crazed scientist, and get no better understanding of what happened to them.

This layer is significantly smaller than either of the previous two, and it is most likely the final one before we reach the center of the dome. Only one gate remains.

items.name: The Final Layer
items.desc:
As soon as the final gate opens up, waves of intense psionic energy wash upon our scientists. Most of them collapse in apparent agony, leaving only a few to make their way into the actual layer itself.

It seems to be a large temple, with a massive dais or altar in the middle of it. All across the walls there are huge diagrams of different star systems, and a repeated one seems to center on [Root.System.GetName] itself.

Making their way closer to the middle, the few scientists that remain find that it is in fact an imposing machine fashioned in the form of an old altar.

items.name: The Elder One
items.desc: As they start tinkering with the machine, they are suddenly beset by a shared auditory hallucination - a screaming command by something to be unearthed, unshackled. Visions of a creature ripping apart the [From.System.GetName] system plays repeatedly in their heads as the creature's demands grow shriller. Several scientists fall unconscious, unable to deal with the unabating torrents of pain that rack their bodies.

items.name: Incoming Transmission
items.desc:
FINALLY...

BOW DOWN MORTALS, GROVEL BEFORE ME, AND I SHALL GRANT YOU PROTECTION AND WISDOM.

OPPOSE ME, AND I SHALL BE YOUR END!

items.name: Incoming Transmission
items.desc: SO YOU HAVE CHOSEN THE PATH OF WISDOM.\nEVERYTHING IS AS IT SHOULD BE.

items.name: Incoming Transmission
items.desc: SO YOU HAVE CHOSEN DEATH.

items.name: Lost Fleet in [eldritch_location.GetName]
items.desc: We have lost all contact with our fleet as it was traveling through the [eldritch_location.GetName] system. Shortly afterwards, we receive news about the collapse of the star and the destruction of everything around it.

items.name: Experimental Weaponry
items.desc: [Root.Leader.GetName] has boarded the station with a team of researchers and managed to restore power to some sections. It appears that it was inhabited mere centuries before [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] took to space. At first sight, it appears to have been a weapons station, as evidenced by the exceptionally large cannon that takes up the majority of its volume. However, most of the remaining sections seem to have been dedicated to research facilities, indicating that the weapon was likely highly experimental.

items.name: System Failures
items.desc: [Root.Leader.GetName] can't help but notice that an abnormally large number of apparently undamaged systems in the station seem to be failing with excessive frequency, even allowing for their age.\n\nUpon reactivating them for the umpteenth time, agonized screams are heard from the team's comp tech: "What? Why? How?!" The stream of distressed and incredulous noises continues unabated for some time before [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] shakes [Root.Leader.GetHerHis] head, defeated. "It seems this entire facility was cobbled together with duct tape," [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] says. "I'm surprised it ever worked."

items.name: The Rudari Gambit
items.desc: Despite the frequent outages, [Root.Leader.GetName] has been able to make significant progress in deciphering the purpose of the station. Logs indicate that its creators, the "Rudari," had been engaged in a long struggle with a genocidal race known as the "Pogg-Mory" - a war they were losing. In a desperate last-ditch effort to turn the tide, a radical group of Rudari politicians concluded that the only way to guarantee their survival was through the total annihilation of the enemy. Unable to defeat the Pogg-Mory fleet by conventional means, they funded a top secret project to build a laser weapon capable of firing across interstellar space by harnessing the power of a star. However, it appears that while they could throw considerable resources at the problem, the project was hastily set up and in constant danger of discovery - either by the enemy or by factions within their own government unwilling to stoop to such measures.

items.name: The Failure of a Dream
items.desc:
[Root.Leader.GetName] has uncovered the Rudari Chief Science Officer's personal logs, which read as a litany of complaints about the seemingly impossible demands of the project and their rapidly falling quality and safety standards. "There is no time to test anything," reads one of the last entries. "This is the last gambit of my people, and the enemy has our scent. We must hope that this is enough. They are coming."

The logs indicate that the weapon was due to be tested soon after, at which point all records cease. Evidence suggests that the superweapon succeeded only in destroying the station. The Rudari seemingly took the secret of its location to their graves - allowing us to find its remains undisturbed.

Neither the programming nor the general condition of the station are good enough for us to risk trying to reactivate it and complete the project. However, some of the innovative concepts used in the "Death Laser" have provided our own weapons specialists with valuable insights.

items.name: Ruins Long Forgotten
items.desc: We have discovered clear signs that [From.Planet.GetName] was once densely populated. However, whatever destroyed their civilization did a very thorough job of it: very few useful remains have been found.\n\nOur scanners have detected several large cavities deep below the surface that may once have supported life. Perhaps we will have more luck there.

items.name: The Library
items.desc: Our excavation of the cave systems on [From.Planet.GetName] has found well-preserved remnants of an underground, high technology society built on a vast scale. Many of the ruins are in surprisingly good condition, and we have managed to find what our [Owner.GetResearchers] are describing as a "library" of encrypted data crystals. Hopefully, these can shed some light on what happened here.

items.name: Lurking in the Shadows
items.desc: A [Owner.GetTeamMember] exploring the ruins on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] recently disappeared. After a short search, we found a [Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName] that seems to have belonged to a [Root.Owner.Species.GetName]. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled about how the body decayed quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.

items.name: Troubles in Paradise
items.desc: As we interpret the data crystals from the caves on [From.Planet.GetName], we begin piecing together a picture of a troubled planet.\n\nThe planet was once the center of a prosperous civilization known as the Ilanii Foundation. During that civilization's latter years, the Ilanii turned more and more to the hoarding of knowledge instead of more material matters such as procreation. As a result, their population fell rapidly. Alarmed by their dwindling numbers, their leaders attempted to find a technological solution for immortality. Records become scarcer around this point - though it appears to predate whatever cataclysm forced them underground - and it is not clear yet what results their efforts yielded.

items.name: Civilization's End
items.desc:
We can now piece together what became of the Ilanii's attempt at immortality. It appears that, far from bringing them everlasting life, they created a terrible menace - a swarm of microorganisms capable of multiplying rapidly and almost instantly devouring any organic matter... as must have happened to our team's lost member.

The resulting cataclysm wiped out much of the population. The survivors splintered into two groups: one, unwilling to give up [From.Planet.GetName], took to the depths, recreating their civilization in air-tight pockets such as the one we found. However, this solution proved unsustainable in the long run, and eventually the microorganism found its way into their habitats; the caves became their tombs.

The other group instead went into exile, enforcing a planetary quarantine by utterly obliterating the surface, rendering it uninhabitable. They would henceforth live in small enclaves and dedicate themselves to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization, eventually morphing into one of the ancestors of the modern §H[curator_enclave_country.GetName]§!.

items.name: The [From.GetName] System
items.desc: An eerie glow lies over the [From.GetName] system. The [Root.GetName] has emerged in a sector of the galaxy surely not visited by any galactic civilization for generations - for millennia... if ever.\n\nBut wait - our sensors are reporting energy signatures! Most are concentrated on the first planet of the system, an unlikely candidate for life, considering its proximity to a neutron star. But there are others, mobile ones. They are careening towards the [Root.GetName], weapons charged!

items.name: Victory in [fromfrom.System.GetName]
items.desc: We have defeated the defenders of [fromfrom.System.GetName]. The system is a curious sight: there is very little solid matter remaining in it - even its asteroid belts have a bedraggled look, as if they have been extensively mined. A series of large installations placed at regular intervals around the star, and there is a single planet that our readings suggest may be artificial in origin. Intense energy signals have been detected emanating from it. If answers are to be found, they will be there.

items.name: Teeming with Artificial Life
items.desc: As far as our [Owner.GetResearchers] can tell, there has never been life on the planet they have ominously dubbed the "§YObservation Terminal§!". But there is no shortage of activity. The surface is densely built up, massive artificial structures placed upon the bare bedrock in neat, orderly rows that cover almost three quarters of the planet. Billions of mechanical drones maintain them, performing tasks ranging from menial clean-up to running highly-complex assembly lines.\n\nTheir exact purpose remains, however, unclear. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are preparing to send a team to the surface to investigate further.

items.name: Investigating the Drones
items.desc: As our [Owner.GetResearchers] pass amongst them, the drones on the planet ignore their presence and continue going about their tasks. All efforts to communicate with the drones have failed, and even attempts to disrupt them produced no reactions - the drones simply rode roughshod over the interfering [Owner.GetResearchers], causing serious injury.\n\nSince then, our [Owner.GetResearchers] have shifted their focus to the programs steering the drones. Analysis of intercepted signals suggests there is an overarching system steering them. However, the encryption it uses is extremely sophisticated, and it has proven hard to find out more.

items.name: Systemic Exploration
items.desc: While our [Owner.GetResearchers] have been unable to make further progress investigating the planet, a team has been investigating the array of objects spread across the system. There are over ten thousand of them, all told. Most of them are long and cylindrical devices that still seem to be operating - they are transmitting a signal towards the planet. Given their shape and the fact that they seem to be without exception pointed towards various points in our galaxy, we cannot escape the conclusion that this is an absurdly huge sensor array. But who could have built it?

items.name: Time to Phish
items.desc: In a daring move, our [Owner.GetResearchers] managed to implant spyware into an access terminal to the drones' mainframe in a moment while no drones were nearby. The intrusion does not appear to have been detected yet. Our impression is of a highly sophisticated system - beyond even our own networks, probably - but one which did not anticipate the need to protect itself. No doubt the physical deterrence of the defense fleet was deemed sufficient. Nevertheless, the systems we are infiltrating are vast - a term which seems a gross understatement for this planetary system - so it will take some time to find out more.

items.name: The Surveillance Supercomputer
items.desc:
It seems the automated systems in Ultima Vigilis are older than we can imagine. The data systems we have hacked do not give us any clues as to the identity or ultimate intentions of its creators, but the one thing we have managed to ascertain is that they arrived no less than 1.2 billion years ago, and departed soon after setting up the system as an observation post to surveil our entire galaxy.

Remarkably, the system is still operating even after all these years: the array of installations spread across the system are, it turns out, highly sophisticated sensors. They send a live feed to the planet, where the central operating system processes it into information the drones can save and store. Spurred on by shortages of space and matter, it appears that they have improved their data compression techniques with determination: the massive structures on the planet purport to contain the sum of all observations ever recorded. However, we cannot test this assertion, since the data is compressed well beyond our ability to decompress it.

Disturbingly, a reduced stream of "highlights" is still being broadcast into empty space. But surely no one is still listening, after all this time? Regardless, our programs are poised to take control of the drones. We may now shape the system to our imagination - if we dare.

items.name: Incoming Transmission
items.desc:
"You inconsiderate-"

§BThe transmission feed is garbled for a time, and no sense can be made of the noises heard.§!

"Did you never consider that someone might be watching that signal feed you so carelessly cut off? Well, since you have proven yourselves to be dangerously aggressive vermin... it's time to call the §RPEST CONTROL§!. Prepare to face your doom."

items.name: Incoming Transmission
items.desc:
"You inconsiderate-"

§BThe transmission feed is garbled for a time, and no sense can be made of the noises heard.§!

"Did you never consider that someone might be watching that signal feed you so carelessly cut off? Well, since you have proven yourselves to be dangerously aggressive vermin... it's time to call the §RPEST CONTROL§!. Prepare to face your doom."

items.name: A Cool Reception
items.desc: After the last of the aggressors in Polaris fell, our ships completed a final scan of the system before heading back to port and discovered something curious. On the world of Polaris II, heavy metals are arranged in artificial structures on our sensors. Interestingly only one of these formations appears to be floating on the planetary ocean while the rest are below the surface. We suspect this is the work of alien life.

items.name: Iceberg
items.desc: Built into the floating iceberg itself is a hulking black cuboid made out of the same alloys as the wreckage of the space fleet above. Our glacial specialists state that analysis of the iceberg dates its formation to least a thousand years ago, though it's supposedly "hard to tell with alien atmospheres". Scans of the interior of the structure show quite a few biological readings, therefore using disruptive tools is inadvisable.\n\nThe team will have to traverse the frozen cliffs to what appears to be an entrance into the building.

items.name: Frost Gate
items.desc: We have set up base camp at the supposed entrance to the facility here on [From.Planet.GetName]. Already we have discovered something that looks like writing inscribed on the walls of the building. Now we will begin the long and arduous process of opening this door without damaging whatever is inside. At the same time, our xeno-linguists attempt to translate the dead alien language of the inscriptions.

items.name: Grave Robbing
items.desc: The time was upon us, and we stood ready to unseal the black structure, dubbed "The Vault" according to preliminary translations of the wall inscriptions. The creators of this vault, the Polarians, made it as a last resort to keep their treasures safe. As we opened the doors, we were greeted by - according to our sensors - a controlled atmosphere similar to the air outside, just with quite a bit less carbon dioxide.

items.name: Treasure
items.desc: Ancient seeds! Plant embryos - that was the treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the plant matter they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.\n\nBack then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole plant ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our scientists in researching future biological matters.

items.name: Treasure
items.desc: Microorganisms! Every harmful and helpful bacterium. Every eukaryote and prokaryote. All in an advanced storage facility labeled and cataloged: this was the great treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed, the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the microbial life they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.\n\nBack then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole microbial ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our [Root.Owner.getscientistplural] develop new and improved colonies for new worlds.

items.name: Water Hoarders
items.desc: The discovery on [From.Planet.GetName] of vast canyons filled with mushrooms provided us with the beginning of an answer. The water is inside the mushrooms. They seem to span a large part of the surface of the world, all connected to the same mycelium, which technically makes it a single organism, and one of the biggest we've ever seen. Some of the members of the team dubbed this humongous fungus the 'Fumongus'.\n\nIt looks like the mushrooms have been genetically altered and have completely taken over the ecosystem that once existed here. Their unbridled and accelerated growth was such that they absorbed most of the water that was present here. They subsequently entered a sort of dried-up dormant state in which most of the fungus is still alive, with water spread out across the whole organism.

items.name: Overrun Bunker
items.desc: Deep in the heart of the mycelial forests nestled in the canyons of [From.Planet.GetName] we discovered some sort of bunker, long overrun by mushrooms. The team believes that it was built by the same species that genetically altered the mushrooms here. \n\nLarge sections of the bunker have collapsed and a lot of the equipment within it is likely broken beyond repair, but we have identified some sealed rooms that might hold exploitable material. Notably, no alien remains have been found here. Maybe they abandoned the place, or else didn't leave behind any body parts that weren't absorbed by the local wildlife.

items.name: Fungal Tamperers
items.desc: The bunker on [From.Planet.GetName] was used to protect computing equipment, some of which appears to be directly connected to the mycelium. Thankfully, we managed to reactivate several terminals and databanks.\n\nBreaking the encryption and deciphering the language used will take time, and the team has requested that several of our top [Root.Owner.GetLinguists] be sent here to help.

items.name: From Shroom to Code
items.desc: We have recovered valuable information from the databanks found in the bunker on [From.Planet.GetName]. The databanks tell us that this was a sort of listening post. Apparently, the aliens found a way to interpret the signals coursing through the mycelium and convert them into actionable intel.\n\nWe do not understand how this might have been possible, but the team will now try to bring water from nearby ice asteroids to 'awaken' the Fumongus again and see what kind of data it transmits, if any.

items.name: Dry No More
items.desc: The mushrooms on [From.Planet.GetName] are starting to flourish again. With the help of several other ships, we had to tow several icy asteroids into orbit before bringing down chunks of them to various places on the planet to melt. It has been long process, but it is finally beginning to bear fruit.\n\nWith this, the computers began to spit out small bits of data that seemed pretty random until we recognized activity from our home. In cooperation with teams on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName], a series of experiments has been conducted and the only possible conclusion is that the mushroom has some limited awareness of what happens on other planets. While the data we have retrieved is not exploitable just yet, continued efforts to restore the mushrooms are expected to give us more results.

items.name: The Fumongus Listens Again
items.desc:
The Mycelium Listening Array is finally operational. A significant supply of water has been brought from orbit to sate the ever-thirsty mushroom, and major upgrades have been made to the computing resources.

Some mysteries remain, as we are still not sure how the mushroom manages to collect that much data from the rest of the galaxy. The number of signals traversing the network proved surprisingly low, considering the quantity of information conveyed. The most prominent theory posits that the Fumongus exists across dimensions where distances are not what we are used to.
In any case, the Fumongus is in contact with its offspring across the galaxy, and these smaller colonies are able to relay data, which we can then interpret.

With the network working again, the only decision left to make is whether to use it for surveillance, or not.

items.name: Fear the Old Shroom
items.desc:
The Mycelium Listening Array is finally operational. A significant supply of water has been brought from orbit to sate the ever-thirsty mushroom, and major upgrades have been made to the computing resources.

And yet, there is still so much we don't know about the mycelial network.  The number of signals traversing the network proved surprisingly low, considering the quantity of information conveyed. The most prominent theory posits that the Fumongus exists across dimensions where distances are not what we are used to.
In any case, the Fumongus is in contact with its offspring across the galaxy, and these smaller colonies are able to relay data, which we can then interpret. But who else may have access to this network? There is a lot of data that we were not able to correlate to systems in this galaxy. Our more pessimistic [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] argue we might not be the only ones listening, and that by reactivating the network we just revealed ourselves to anyone using it.

Given all we still don't know about the Fumongus, or about the previous species that tapped into it, it might be best to just leave it alone..

items.name: Rage in a Cage
items.desc: When we opened the airlock of the alien starship, putrefaction and decay awaited us on the other side. Our preliminary investigation has uncovered a scene of carnage. After examining the mutilated bodies of the crew, we are certain they tore each other limb from limb. We could just leave... but then we'd never know why this tragedy happened.

items.name: Elaborate Laboratory
items.desc: Digging deeper, we have uncovered the ship's science lab. Minimal power saturates the scene in ultraviolent illumination. A riot of purple shrubbery is releasing thick clouds of spores. The ship's doctor used a laboratory and ventilation shafts to flood the ship with an intoxicating mist.

items.name: Throw the Switch!
items.desc: We think we are immune to the full effects of the intoxicating mist. If we can get the ship's engines online, we can launch the ship and send it back home for study. This will take time, but the elaborate pharmaceutical laboratory may provide useful biochemical augmentation for our empire's soldiers.

items.name: Bliss Outbreak
items.desc: We foolishly thought we were immune to the mist, but our engineers are experiencing a state of rapturous bliss. They dance in the ship's corridors, singing atonally. We will need to clear the atmosphere and capture our engineers before we can launch the ship. This delay will cost us time.

items.name: Rage Outbreak
items.desc: We foolishly thought that we were immune to the mist, but our scientists are experiencing fits of psychotic rage. Fighting has broken out shipwide. We will need to clear the atmosphere and subdue the mist's victims before we can launch the ship. This delay will cost us time.

items.name: Temptations of Technology
items.desc: We have liftoff! Though dangerous, the alien ship's intoxicating mist could augment the effectiveness and loyalty of our empire's soldiers. However, the question remains: should we subject our own soldiers to this hazardous substance? Or should we say no and learn from their tragic mistakes?

items.name: Meatball
items.desc: It's hard to determine if [From.Planet.GetName] is even a planet: preliminary drilling has only revealed strata upon strata of biological tissue. According to estimations, it would take 2,435,463 Tiyanki bodies to produce a planetary mass of this size (with a margin of error equal to 5.3%). Even assuming the existence of a rocky core upon which the corpses are layered, the number of specimens involved is still significant.\n\nDid someone or something bring the Tiyanki here to die, or are they naturally drawn to this place as their final hour draws near?

items.name: Three Parts Dead
items.desc:
The unusual... liveliness of the dead Tiyanki covering the surface of [From.Planet.GetName] seems to be a byproduct of their regenerative capabilities: even if technically dead, the bodies are still reassembling themselves. This system is unusually rich in nourishing substances typically found in the gas giants where Tiyanki graze. Perhaps that explains why this behavior hasn't been observed before.

This discovery does not explain why the dead seem to move as if controlled by a single mind, extending their tentacles to encroach upon the new carcasses falling on the planet.

Further excavations will hopefully reveal new insights on the inner workings of this... place. Or being. Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] are still divided on the exact nomenclature.

items.name: Flesh Labyrinth
items.desc: Our excavations unearthed a complex network of tunnels extending under the surface of [From.Planet.GetName]. Chemical analysis confirms the walls are entirely composed of highly compressed Tiyanki tissue, the flesh still warm and hardly decomposed despite rivaling the age of our empire. It's as if the corpses were fused together, reshaped and modified to form this place... But why?

items.name: Haunted Tunnels
items.desc: After mapping the extensive underground network of [From.Planet.GetName], our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] realized the tunnels closely match the structure of the Tiyanki vascular system - but on a planetary scale.\n\nThe pulsating walls emanate a soft warmth, the temperature slowly increasing as the expedition approached the planet core - where our scanners have picked up a faint life signal.

items.name: Mother Brain
items.desc: In a vast underground chamber, a Tiyanki stands upright, bell-shaped head swaying lightly, its wiry tentacles spread across the floor to connect with the outer walls of the chamber. It appears to be some sort of command unit, controlling and directing the growth of this planet-sized graveyard.\n\nOur [Owner.GetScientistPlural] are unable to determine what kind of creature will arise from this grim process, and when it will awaken, but one thing is for sure: it will be something far, far more vast and terrible than an ordinary Tiyanki.

items.name: Mother Brain
items.desc: In a vast underground chamber, a Tiyanki stands upright, bell swaying lightly, its wiry tentacles spread on the floor to connect with the outer walls of the chamber. It appeared to be some sort of control unit, controlling and directing the growth of the grave mound. But the creature is now dead, destroyed by the mining equipment we used to get access to this same place. The shells around the core are pallid and brittle; soon, this whole place will die a second death.

items.name: Environmental Contamination
items.desc:
A member of our expedition team disappeared while exploring a tunnel. The retrieval squad spent days trying to locate the [Owner.GetScientist], only to find them partly encased in a wall, body tightly wrapped in tentacles.

Freeing the [Owner.GetScientist] took considerable time and effort. The [Owner.GetScientist] was not simply tied: the wall was trying to fuse with the [Owner.GetScientist] at a molecular level, turning them into a part of the surface.

The [Owner.GetScientist] is now in stable condition, but refuses to leave our science ship - and even there, they keep watching the walls with extreme suspicion as though fearing another attack.

items.name: Message in the Canopy
items.desc: Our scientists have discovered something unusual on [From.Planet.GetName]. A tropical world, much of the planet's surface is covered with dense jungle: massive, thousand year old trees erupt from the canopy, their leafy crowns towering over the landscape.\n\nAt first glance, the distribution of these giants appears random. However, further analysis indicates that the trees are arranged with mathematical precision, and it seems likely they were planted by some long-vanished civilization. What's more, the team leader believes the distribution pattern may comprise a set of coordinates, one that points to an unexplored location deep within the jungle.

items.name: Welcome to the Jungle
items.desc: Given the impenetrable canopy on [From.Planet.GetName], aerial surveys have proven useless in determining a convenient route through the jungle. Below, the undergrowth teems with life: limbless predators; droop-faced primates; swarms of hematophagous insects. The forest floor is loamy, and pools of fetid water have caused the team significant delays. What's more, something - either the density of the foliage or an as yet undefined electrical interference - has prevented much of their equipment from functioning properly.\n\nThe project's lead believes they should still be able to forge a path through the trees, though progress is likely to be slow.

items.name: Psionic Metamorphosis
items.desc: A soil analysis reveals that [From.Planet.GetName] has undergone a startling climatological transformation within its last 100 cycles. Far from the lush jungle world that exists today, the planet was once rocky and barren. The project lead believes the great trees themselves are responsible: a resonance imaging scan detected the presence of psionic energy within their sap. Pulled from groundwater by the trees' vast root systems, this energy is eventually diffused throughout the planet's atmosphere in a process akin to photosynthesis. It is highly likely that this is the cause of the team's malfunctioning equipment.\n\nInterestingly, the presence of moonlight appears to accelerate the psionic diffusion. On clear nights, the air itself seems to vibrate, a phenomenon that has only grown in intensity as the team nears its destination. This is unlike anything we've ever seen before.

items.name: The Cave
items.desc:
At last reaching their tracked coordinates, the archaeology team discovered a winding river valley hidden beneath the canopy. Rushing forth from a circular cave-mouth, the river apparently stems from some massive, underground spring. A precarious stairway, carved from the rocks several thousand years ago, delivered the team to a subterranean tunnel.

The cave's walls and ceiling are covered in a compact scrawl of ideographs, the most prominent of which is a round, humanoid face. Our translation algorithms have succeeded in decoding much of the symbology, and this particular image likely represents the planet's moon.

Within the cave, the presence of psionic energy is off the charts. Unfortunately, the path ahead was blocked by a cave-in several centuries ago, but given time, the expedition should be able to find a way through.

items.name: The Pillar
items.desc: A note of triumph from our science team on [From.Planet.GetName]! After successfully reaching the lower levels of the cave, they at last arrived in a wide, hemispherical chamber. There, the river parts around a small island, at the center of which is a stalagmite of rare crystals. Formed drop-by-drop over the course of several millennia, the pillar appears to be the source of the planet's strange, psionic energy. The team has discovered evidence of religious ritual, as well as several small artifacts of ceremonial significance scattered around the pillar. What's more, a multiphasic scan revealed a round object embedded in the pillar's base. Hopes are high that, once removed, this artifact will shed some light on the true nature of this mysterious place.

items.name: Shattered!
items.desc: Frustration on [From.Planet.GetName] as our science team has failed to remove the artifact from the crystal stalagmite. Perhaps working with too much vigor, the team's efforts caused the pillar to shatter. Worse, the artifact within was damaged beyond recognition, and all traces of psionic energy have vanished from the chamber.\n\nOne minor consolation is that the crystal itself could prove extremely valuable. While we may never fully understand the intentions of the precursor civilization that built this place, at least our efforts have not entirely been in vain.

items.name: The Mask of Transformation
items.desc: A breakthrough from the science team on [From.Planet.GetName]! Their careful excavation of the crystal pillar is complete. Preserved within was an ancient, humanoid mask. Ideographs on the reverse side refer to the artifact as The Mask of Transformation. This is likely a reference to the transformative power of the planet's moon, controlling the tides as it transitions from one phase to the next.\n\nThe Mask itself possesses incredible psionic properties, and is likely responsible for the rapid climatological transformation of the planet. Whoever fostered the crystal pillar and planted the elaborate map of trees in the forest above clearly intended to honor and protect this artifact. The team theorizes that, if properly used, the Mask may enable our empire to transform entire worlds.

items.name: Message in a Bottle
items.desc:
As we expected, the interior of this 'solar sailer' is appropriately archaic. The bridge resembles the deck of an old planetbound sailing ship designed to sail on watery seas.

The deck plating appears to be metal, but most surfaces are covered with carved wood, a contrast to the glass-like substance on viewports and datascreens.

Powering up the ship's computers, we have found a datafile with an old-fashioned seafarers' song. According to our archaeologist, this melody was once known as a 'sea chanty' or 'space shanty.' We are attempting to transcribe the lyrics.

items.name: Space Shanty
items.desc:
Immediately after we completed the restoration and reactivation of the datafiles, a thrumming musical cadence surged throughout the ship, accompanied by the auto-tuned voices of ancient mariners. Transcription follows:

'Come all you young spacefarers, listen to me!
I'll sing you a song of our fish from the sea!

And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes.

Up come the solar winds
Taking us far
All through the space lanes
And out to the stars!

And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes!

items.name: Cosmic Beasties
items.desc:
As we explored the ship, further attempts to power it up and recover its datafiles unlocked more stanzas of the ancient space shanty. The ship's holographic display vibrantly projected images of sailors and spacefarers singing and dancing in accompaniment:

'Up comes the Great Dragon
In search of our home
Through space to a place that's
Beneath waves and foam!

'And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes.

'Up comes the Tiyanki
The king of deep space
Racing our ships
In a hyperspace chase!

(chorus repeats)

'Up comes Leviathan
Tentacles grasp
Choking our ship
As we shiver and gasp!

(chorus repeats)

items.name: Potent Potables
items.desc:
Our archaeologists have unearthed of a stash of potent potables. Were the sailors consuming these foul fluids? We will not ingest these strange liquids. Our exploration of the ship is already sufficiently intoxicating!

'Up come the Lithoids
All hewn from their stone
These boulders are bolder
When they're not alone!

(chorus)

'Up come the Necroids
All fearsome and great
You can't kill them, mateys,
They'll reanimate!

(chorus)

'Up come swarms of robots
Get ready to run
Fight one, ten, a dozen,
1101!

(chorus)

items.name: Cast Off the Hawser!
items.desc:
Our exploration has revealed a glance of ancient history, displaying the zeal and courage of ancient explorers. Clearly the captain used this 'space shanty' to motivate and coordinate the crew. Perhaps they even sang along! Our archaeologists are suggesting this performance should be preserved in a museum installation.

As for the ancient melody, we've transcribed all the lyrics we could find and added them to our databanks. Our own 'sailors' now have a habit of singing versions of their own space shanties, which should improve their morale and efficiency.

'We rose from the ocean
And reached for the sky
We're building an empire
That never will die!

'And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes!'

It's time to untether from this ancient vessel, 'casting off the hawser' as we set sail on solar winds. Steady as she goes!

items.name: Laser Grid Triggered
items.desc: During the excavations of the archaeology site on [From.Planet.GetName], an ancient but still functional laser grid was inadvertently triggered.\n\nThe rapidly moving laser beams sliced §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! and several other [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] into tiny pieces.

items.name: Laser Grid Triggered
items.desc: During the excavations of the archaeology site on [From.Planet.GetName], an ancient but still functional laser grid was inadvertently triggered.\n\nSeveral [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were sliced into tiny pieces by the fast moving beams. Although §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! survived unscathed, these losses have had a negative impact on the project.

items.name: Laser Grid Triggered
items.desc: During the excavations of the archaeology site on [From.Planet.GetName], an ancient but still functional laser grid was inadvertently triggered.\n\nFortunately, thanks to the quick actions of §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! the lasers were disabled before they could cause any harm. The project is moving forwards, ahead of schedule.

items.name: Laser Grid Triggered
items.desc: During the excavations of the archaeology site on [From.Planet.GetName], an ancient but still functional laser grid was inadvertently triggered.\n\nThe lasers are blocking the only path forward. Disabling them will be expensive, but finding an alternative route around the laser grid would take a lot of time.

items.desc: Our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] working on [From.Planet.GetName] accidentally triggered an array of ancient but still functional sentry guns.\n\nThe automated guns rapidly mowed down §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! and several other [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] before they could be disabled.

items.name: Sentry Guns Triggered

If they can't be disabled, our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] will have to find an alternate route.

items.name: Rampaging Crusher-Droid
items.desc: A roving crusher-droid, set up to ambush unwary explorers, was encountered by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName].\n\nThe ancient and semi-sentient robot ground §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! into tiny pieces before its rampage could be stopped.

items.name: Rampaging Crusher-Droid
items.desc: A roving crusher-droid, set up to ambush unwary explorers, was encountered by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName].\n\n§H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! managed to flee its rampage, but several other [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were not so lucky.

items.name: Rampaging Crusher-Droid
items.desc: A roving crusher-droid, set up to ambush unwary explorers, was encountered by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName].\n\nWith skill and a fair bit of luck, §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! managed to halt the rampaging robot before anyone was injured.

items.name: Rampaging Crusher-Droid
items.desc: A roving crusher-droid, set up to ambush unwary explorers, was encountered by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName].\n\nEveryone managed to escape the rampaging robot, but it is now tirelessly patrolling the only way forward. Unless it can be disabled, our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] will have to look for another path.

items.name: Sentinel Droids
items.desc: The excavations carried out by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName] have somehow activated several ancient sentinel droids.\n\nThe hostile robots made short work of §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! before they could be permanently deactivated with weapons fire.

items.name: Sentinel Droids
items.desc: The excavations carried out by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName] have somehow activated several ancient sentinel droids.\n\nThe hostile robots managed to kill several [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] before they could be stopped by §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§!.

items.name: Sentinel Droids
items.desc: The excavations carried out by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName] have somehow activated several ancient sentinel droids.\n\nLuckily, §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! and the nearby security escort managed to neutralize the hostile robots before they could seriously injure anyone.

Unless they can be neutralized, an alternate route will have to be found.

items.name: Resource Cache
items.desc: §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! discovered an ancient cache of resources among the ruins on [From.Planet.GetName]. They are even now in the process of being shipped off to our central stores.

items.name: Hidden Passage
items.desc: §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! recently found a hidden passage while excavating the ruins on [From.Planet.GetName]! This unexpected discovery has accelerated progress at the dig site.

items.name: Lost Expedition
items.desc: Your [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] have stumbled upon an ill-fated previous expedition on [From.Planet.GetName] that perished long ago. Several minor artifacts were recovered from their desiccated remains.

items.name: Bickering Archaeologists
items.desc: Tempers are running high at the archaeology site on [From.Planet.GetName], and several [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] are openly disagreeing with §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! about how best to proceed. Progress at the site has been slowed to a crawl.

items.name: Treasure Chamber
items.desc: A small hidden treasure chamber was recently uncovered by §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! at the archaeological dig site on [From.Planet.GetName]. Although most of the found trinkets are of little practical use, they have a substantial energy credit value.

items.name: Spreading Illness
items.desc: [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that a strange sickness has been spreading among the [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName]. The first confirmed cases appeared shortly after a sealed chamber was opened for the first time. With a large part of the team incapacitated, progress has been delayed.

items.name: Equipment Malfunction
items.desc: The archaeological expedition on [From.Planet.GetName] has reported delays caused by an unlikely series of equipment malfunctions. Work has been halted momentarily until replacements can be acquired.

items.name: Without a Trace
items.desc: While excavating the ruins on [From.Planet.GetName], §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! recently vanished without a trace. An extensive search by the other [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] turned up nothing. We have to assume the worst.

items.name: Minor Artifacts Discovered
items.desc: Our continued excavations on [From.Planet.GetName] have unearthed a small cache of antique objects. [Root.GetLeaderName] has identified several minor artifacts among them.

items.name: Hostile Wildlife
items.desc: A group of large predators indigenous to [From.Planet.GetName] were recently discovered to have made a lair in the ruins being excavated.\n\nBefore our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] could make their escape, the vicious animals were upon them. §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! was lost along with the others.

items.name: Hostile Wildlife
items.desc: A group of large predators indigenous to [From.Planet.GetName] were recently discovered to have made a lair in the ruins being excavated.\n\nMany [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were lost before §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! could lead the survivors to safety.

items.name: Hostile Wildlife
items.desc: A group of large predators indigenous to [From.Planet.GetName] were recently discovered to have made a lair in the ruins being excavated.\n\nFortunately, the animals were hibernating and they were not disturbed by the passage of our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural]. The project is rapidly moving ahead.

items.name: Hostile Wildlife
items.desc: A group of large predators indigenous to [From.Planet.GetName] were recently discovered to have made a lair in the ruins being excavated.\n\nDealing with these vicious animals will not be easy, but they are blocking the only route forwards. Our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] can look for an alternate path, but it will take time.

items.name: Unstable Ruins
items.desc: Our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] working on [From.Planet.GetName] have reached a highly unstable section of the ruins.\n\nUnfortunately, an entire ceiling collapsed on several [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural], killing them instantly. §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! was among them.

items.name: Unstable Ruins
items.desc: Our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] working on [From.Planet.GetName] have reached a highly unstable section of the ruins.\n\nSeveral [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were recently killed when a ceiling collapsed on them. §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! emerged unscathed from the debris, but work at the site has been momentarily halted.

items.name: Unstable Ruins
items.desc: Our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] working on [From.Planet.GetName] have reached a highly unstable section of the ruins.\n\nFortunately, §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! managed to devise an unorthodox and brilliant way of providing structural support with a complex array of directed energy fields. We can now safely access new areas of the ruins.

items.name: Unstable Ruins
items.desc: Our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] working on [From.Planet.GetName] have reached a highly unstable section of the ruins.\n\nSupports will have to be carefully added to the floors and ceilings before we can proceed. It will be difficult work, but finding an alternate route would delay the project.

items.name: Ancient Records
items.desc: Ancient, partially translated records have been discovered amongst the ruins being excavated on [From.Planet.GetName]. §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! reports that the records contain several technical specifications that may be of value to our scientists.

items.name: Disturbing Vision
items.desc: Three nights ago, chief archaeologist [From.Leader.GetName] reported having a disturbing vision and has been shut away in their quarters until now. They believed the source to be whatever is down here with us...

items.name: Fungal Zombies
items.desc: The expedition carried out by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName] has disturbed the decaying husks of some local wildlife, which seem now to be under the sway of parasitic fungi. These fungal zombies immediately began assaulting us, apparently drawn to sources of water in our camp and inside our very bodies.\n\nThe zombies made short work of §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! before they could be burned down by our security team. Their desiccated remains are all that is left of them.

These fungal zombies immediately began assaulting us, apparently drawn to sources of water in our camp and inside our very bodies.\n\nThe zombies managed to kill several [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] before they could be stopped by §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! Their desiccated corpses fell to pieces when we tried to recover them.

These fungal zombies immediately began assaulting us, apparently drawn to sources of water in our camp and inside our very bodies.\n\nLuckily, §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! and the nearby security escort managed to neutralize the zombies before they could seriously injure anyone.

These fungal zombies immediately began assaulting us, apparently drawn to sources of water in our camp and inside our very bodies.\n\nThe zombies have been contained for now, but there is no way past them. Perhaps we can lure them out with a sufficiently vast amount of water.

items.name: Bushwhacked!
items.desc:
Emergency transmission from the science team on [From.Planet.GetName]! Their rough foray into the jungle appears to have badly angered some of the local fauna.

Over the course of several nights, the team sighted fleeting shadows, half-glimpsed between the underbrush. Then, on the eve of the full moon, a troop of simian-like creatures descended on the expedition, howling and brandishing sticks. Given our technological advantage, these raiders were quickly driven back into the trees, but not before they had made off with several members of the team. We are told the dense foliage did little to muffle the screams.

Despite the danger, scientist [Root.GetLeaderName] has vowed to continue the expedition.

items.name: Lost and Found
items.desc: We have received an update from the expedition on [From.Planet.GetName]. Navigating the labyrinthine jungle has proven more challenging than initially hoped. As the team struggled to push forward, stymied by unexpected marshes and thick, creeping vines, they were approached by an unusually intelligent simian. Picking its way through the foliage on the back of a tamed ungulate, the creature led the team through the worst of the jungle. It also made sure to point out caches of edible insectoid larvae buried in the roots of the great trees. Given the creature's excited gestures, these must be something of a local delicacy. More importantly, the tip resulted in further evidence of the planet's precursor civilization, as the team quickly unearthed several artifacts from the forest floor.

items.name: Bush Party
items.desc: Hard times for the science team on [From.Planet.GetName]. Progress through the jungle ground to a near halt with the unexpected discovery of a river valley winding beneath the trees. The raging waters are stuttered with sharp rocks, and have proven impassable along the team's chosen course. The resulting detour has had surprising consequences: the arrival of a gregarious troop of local simians. These slope-browed creatures have delighted in entertaining the expedition, arriving each night laden with an extremely potent variety of fermented berry. Although morale is higher than ever, progress continues to slow, and the project lead reports an alarming lack of initiative among the team.

items.name: Explosive Decompression
items.desc: During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.\n\nThere was nothing anyone could have done - within moments, §H[dead_scientist.GetName]§! and several other [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were swept through the breach to their deaths.

items.name: Explosive Decompression
items.desc: During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.\n\nWithin moments, several [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were swept through the breach to their deaths. Fortunately, §H[Root.GetLeaderName]§! was in a different section of the station at the time, but this is nevertheless a significant setback for the investigation effort.

items.name: Explosive Decompression
items.desc: During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.\n\nFortunately, no lives were lost in the incident, as our team was able to escape to unaffected areas of the station. It seems no vital equipment was damaged either, so the investigation will not face any undue setbacks as a result.

items.name: Explosive Decompression
items.desc: During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.\n\nFortunately, no lives were lost in the incident, as our team was able to escape to unaffected areas of the station. However, the force of the decompression damaged several of the consoles they had been working on, and will cost a considerable amount to be repaired.

items.name: Minor Artifacts Discovered
items.desc: Our continued study of the remnants of the station in the [fromfrom.planet.system.GetName] system has unearthed a small cache of antique objects. Chief archaeologist [root.leader.GetName] has identified several minor artifacts among them.

items.name: System Lockout
items.desc: As they were poking through the station's electronics, one of our [Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] accidentally triggered some still-functional security measures left by its creators. As a result, our team were locked out from the station's systems for a considerable time before the right countermeasures could be deployed.

items.name: Coprolite Asteroid
items.desc: Although it is difficult to accept, all indications point towards asteroid [From.GetName] being a coprolite - a piece of fossilized feces from some kind of massive life form. It appears to be almost a billion years old, and much of the fossil's original organic composition has been replaced by mineral deposits. Our scientists are baffled as to what kind of creature could have produced something like this.

items.name: Pirate Treasure
items.desc: This asteroid appears to have been used intermittently as a base by a band of alien pirates roughly one thousand years ago. By entering the base, we managed to recover their abandoned treasure hoard. It consisted largely of stolen trinkets and artifacts, but some of it still appears to be of value.

items.name: Asteroid Fauna
items.desc: Amazingly, while conducting their survey of [From.GetName], the crew of the [Root.GetName] picked up several life signs coming from within the asteroid. There appears to be a colony of large burrowing worm-like lithovores within the rock, which has been riddled with tunnels. These unique life forms have somehow adapted to a life in the coldness of space.

items.name: Asteroid Fossils
items.desc: Fossils from what appears to be several species of aquatic animals have been found on the barren and airless surface of [From.GetName]. There are indications that the surrounding asteroid belt was created from the remains of a shattered planet, and these findings seem to confirm that theory. Judging by the fossils, the planet supported life and was at least partially covered by water.

items.name: Derelict Shipyard
items.desc: A large portion of asteroid [From.GetName] has been hollowed out to allow for the construction of some kind of shipyard. It has been abandoned and exposed to the vacuum of space for centuries - if anything useful remained, it has already been looted by previous explorers. The design of the shipyard itself is unique, however, and much could potentially be learned by its study.

items.name: Junkyard
items.desc: This asteroid was evidently used as a junkyard by someone at some point in the distant past. All manner of discarded machinery and metallic refuse has been deposited inside the asteroid's weak gravity well, being slowly pulled into the jumble of debris that now covers the surface. There is nothing of particular value to be found here, but a lot of the metal could be salvaged by a mining station.

items.name: Crashed Scout Craft
items.desc: A small scout craft of some kind plowed into the surface of this asteroid millennia ago, creating a shallow canyon. There is no visible cockpit on the ship, leading us to believe it was either piloted by remote or through some kind of primitive artificial intelligence. Although it is too damaged to be salvaged, the ship hasn't been picked clean by looters yet.

items.name: Automated Mining Base
items.desc: We have detected an automated mining base built in close orbit around asteroid [From.GetName]. There is scorching on the hull indicative of light weapons damage, and the facility appeared to be stuck in some kind of feedback loop. We have managed to reprogram the base systems and the facility is now fully under our control.

items.name: Weapons Target Range
items.desc: Asteroid [From.GetName] is pockmarked with craters from weapon blasts, and appears to have been used as a target range by someone roughly two millennia ago. Residual energy readings suggest they tested increasingly exotic weaponry, including subspace bombs and some kind of singularity generator. Our scientists would be interested in studying the unusual energy echoes that remain.

items.name: Asteroid Collision
items.desc: Upon closer examination, we have discovered that a smaller asteroid consisting almost entirely of precious metals recently collided with [From.GetName]. This small but dense cache of metals was hidden just beneath the asteroid's surface, but now that it has been discovered it should be accessible to mining.

items.name: Exotic Radiation
items.desc: This particular asteroid is an extrasolar capture, and appears to have been washed by some kind of exotic radiation as it plummeted through interstellar space before finally settling in the [From.GetStarName] system. The original source of this radiation remains unknown, but the [Root.GetName] has been able to pick up a wealth of physics data by studying the asteroid's energy emissions.

items.name: Crashed Ore Freighter
