items.name: Veiled in Debris
items.desc: There has been an accident.\n\nDue to a critical error, several trash pods orbiting [planet.GetName] collided, causing large amounts of debris to enter the lower atmosphere. This has already limited the planet's spacefaring capabilities, and according to estimates, the situation could further worsen as the space trash continues to break down. However, launching an operation to collect the debris might prove long and costly.
items.trigger: has_deposit = d_sprawling_landfill_blocker

items.name: Orbital Clean-Up Complete
items.desc: A momentous day on [planet.GetName] as the astrogarbage collectors have completed their final shift. As of this day, the trash rings surrounding [planet.GetName] have been reduced by such a scale that they no longer pose a major threat to passing ships.\n\nIn the coming days, the work will continue on a smaller scale. It might be impossible to clean the orbit entirely, but at least the worst is over.

items.name: Ground Locked
items.desc: After dismissing concerns over some runaway space garbage in orbit around [Planet.GetName], the situation has drastically escalated.\n\nAs the colonial scientists suggested, individual pieces of space trash have collided to create a halo of microtrash around the planet. This has made it extremely hard to transport resources and people in or out of the colony without risking collateral damage.

items.name: Shooting Stars
items.desc: After dismissing concerns over some runaway space garbage in orbit around [Planet.GetName], the issue seems to have resolved itself.\n\nThousands of 'shooting stars' have begun to fall en masse as the planet's strong gravitational pull brings the trash close enough to burn in the atmosphere. Nightly gatherings have become commonplace as people arrive to witness the unique display.

items.name: Clear Skies
items.desc: A historic celebration has erupted on [planet.GetName] as the astrogarbage collectors' final shift has ended.\n\nAs of this day, the trash rings that once surrounded the planet are no longer detectable. Due to this success, the collectors have received resounding support to continue their operation, ensuring clear skies for generations to come.

items.name: Myrmeku Activity
items.desc: Since settling on §Y[Root.GetName]§!, we have noted increased arthropod activity. Specifically, tiny colony-building insects designated "Myrmeku" have become unexpectedly productive.\n\nTheir underground colonies are spread across the continent in great numbers, but until now they have never caused an issue. It is unknown if they are searching for something above ground or fleeing from something beneath.

items.name: [Owner.GetColonistPluralCapital] Attacked
items.desc:
Our [Owner.GetColonistPlural] on §Y[Root.GetName]§! have been viscously attacked! Venturing too close to a Myrmeku colony, they were swarmed. As the tiny insects entered openings in the [Owner.GetColonistPlural]' frames, the victims were quickly overwhelmed.

The fallen [Owner.GetColonistPlural] were immediately disassembled, but no conclusive data was collected as to the insects' purpose. The craggy surface of the Myrmeku's magnetic exoskeletons damage our internal circuitry, and when two Myrmeku touch, they create a tiny electrical spark; both of which may cause catastrophic failure.

Losing [Owner.GetColonistPlural] this way has slowed down the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s development rate. Something must be done.

items.name: Memory Eaters
items.desc:
With astounding speed, the Myrmeku have built several sprawling structures close to our settlement. Their attacks are no longer limited to the perimeter, but have also begun inside housing structures.

The large number of subjects available for autopsy has revealed the disturbing reason why the Myrmeku are interested in us: The insects consume the insulation material of our §Ymemory chips§!.

This is only fatal for the victim in the short term, as memory circuits can be replaced and backups restored. However, replacing the parts means delays for the construction of new [Owner.GetColonistPlural].

items.name: Pest Control
items.desc: The colony buildings on §Y[Root.GetName]§! were completely sealed off to keep the Myrmeku insects out.\n\nThe entrances of both new and existing buildings were outfitted with metallic strips that can be magnetized to trap the Myrmeku, but [Owner.GetColonistPlural] are still being lost to attacks in the field.

items.name: Nuclear Option
items.desc: Everything has been prepared for the cleansing of biological life on §Y[Root.GetName]§!.\n\nObserving the [Root.GetPlanetMoon] from orbit during the event will give us an opportunity to appreciate the reduction in organic complexity on the surface.

items.name: Analysis Subroutine Proposal
items.desc:
Efforts so far have not put an end to the Myrmeku problem. The insects still crawl across [Root.GetName] in immense numbers, making travel and off-colony operations difficult. Our analysis subroutine has concluded its simulation of potential futures with the following approaches.

Approach A: Distract the Myrmeku by airdropping memory insulation material far off from our colony and recycle the fallen [Owner.GetColonistPlural].

Approach B: Study the Myrmeku to see if we can find a way to turn their vigorous activity into something useful.

items.name: Powerful Results
items.desc: Our study of the Myrmeku has concluded. When calibrated magnets were placed around the entrances of their colonies, the magnetism in the insect exoskeletons generated electricity that we could harness.\n\nThe study also showed that the Myrmeku move according to local magnetic fields, so installing a demagnetized protective shell around our memory chips should be enough to protect them.

items.name: A Dimension of Static
items.desc: The Dimensional Portal on [Root.GetName] shut itself. When we stabilized the portal, we saw that it led to a dimension consisting solely of a white, formless void interrupted only by random streaks of black noise. The strange phenomenon instantly started to seep into our universe and consumed our dimensional stabilizers, collapsing the gateway.\n\nThe portal, static, and dimensional stabilizers have all winked out of existence simultaneously. Nothing was left behind; not even trace particles. If the portal hadn't been unstable, who knows what kind of disaster might have occurred here.

items.name: Disruptions
items.desc: Recently our [Root.GetScientistPlural] working in our primary physics lab on §Y[Root.GetHomeWorldName]§! have noticed strange fluctuations in their work. Our hyperdrive-related tests suffered most from these interferences, yet these interruptions only went on for about a week before stopping entirely. At the same time [From.GetName] noticed fluctuations from the now closed dimensional portal, thankfully the impossible static did not return. Hopefully, nothing will come of this.

items.name: Negative Mass
items.desc:
A new report from lead physics unit [cloned_physicist.GetName] was received today. The report included recent findings of the spontaneously appearing negative mass particles close to §Y[Root.Capital.GetStarName]§!.

"These findings could advance the [Root.GetName] understanding of artificial wormholes immensely as well as related subjects," reports science unit [cloned_physicist.GetName].

Threat analysis subroutines suggest bringing fleets home until the source of this new and untested material can be determined.

items.name: The Night the Sky Split
items.desc: Additional science units had been deployed to study [cloned_physicist.GetName]'s latest findings and the use of the negative mass particles only to be interrupted. Emergency sirens screeched in every observatory and space station across the system as §Y[Root.GetHomeWorldName]§! got a new fixture in the night sky. A rip in space the size of our star stretches over the sky as a small fleet of fighters pours out of the tear.

items.name: An Old Code
items.desc: As the last corvette is rendered inoperable, observation analysis subroutines report something abnormal. The invader ships are similar to outdated vessels that the [Root.GetName] stopped producing years ago. Additionally, the ships lack FTL drives and are equipped with obsolete weaponry. While the report is coming in, a communication request originating from the strange tear reverberates throughout the system. It's using our most complex handshaking protocols... from 10 years ago.

items.name: A Trans-Dimensional Call
items.desc: As the comms screen flickers on, an identification code is sent through. §RChecksum error:§! This is [cloned_physicist.GetName]s unique ID! \n§B"Greetings [Root.GetName]-Alpha and apologies: Previous hostile action was caused by a redundant and deprecated military branch of [Root.GetName]-Beta systems. It has since been dealt with and deleted. Statement: We intend no further hostile interactions."§!

items.name: A Trans-Dimensional Call
items.desc: §BTransportation ships have been built. Request to send over [Root.GetName]-Beta units to preserve resources and databanks. We do not wish to end our exploration of the universe here.§!

items.name: The Summit
items.desc:
Every supercomputer under the control of [Root.GetName] was put on calculating the most optimal solution to the current dilemma regarding [Root.GetName]-Beta. In the end, 4 potential options were declared viable.

1: Study collapse of Beta universe.
2: Enter gateway and acquire all relevant stockpiles of minerals and energy.
3: Allow science unit: [cloned_physicist.GetName]-Beta's proposal.
4: Attempt to use highly experimental Beta science and technology to bring [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta into Alpha reality.

items.name: Elation!
items.desc: A formless static covers a large swath of §B[Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta's§! sky and is closing in rapidly as [cloned_physicist.GetName]-Alpha and Beta and all other available science units work side by side. The negative mass stabilizers activate, and the tear between worlds moves over [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta just as the static would smother it. The rift winks out moments later, and negative mass stops being produced at its former location.\n\nIt is done. After months of study and research accounting for new gravitational wells and habitable zones, [Root.Capital.GetStarName] now has a new inhabited planet orbiting it.

items.name: Static
items.desc: Probes left in the Beta universe record the final moments of reality, as a formless static wall absorbs first [Root.Capital.GetStarName]-Beta and then §B[Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta§!. The feed is abruptly cut off shortly before the rift winks out of existence. The negative mass particles it was producing are likewise gone.\n\nAnyone left on that side is no more.

items.name: Crossing the Dimensional Border
items.desc: A common issue has started occurring ever since the rift appeared. Families in our dimension are reaching out to their Beta counterparts and smuggling them into our stable universe. This is often done by the border guards assigned to keeping the universes separate, as basically everyone in the [Owner.GetName] has family on the other side. A few groups doing this wouldn't matter, but we would quickly have a stampede on our hands if the practice spreads. If §B[Owner.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta§! loses too many inhabitants, their infrastructure will collapse, and it will be even harder to get the world through.

items.name: Mission: Dimensional
items.desc: One of the great things about having a mirror world so near is that [Owner.GetSpeciesName] cultural pillars that might have been destroyed or lost in the last few years might still exist on the other planet, so everyone can enjoy them again. Yet unsavory characters have taken this as an opportunity to infiltrate §B[Target.GetName]-Beta§! and secure these great works for themselves. We now possess not one but two masterworks made by a great inventor from our past. [Target.GetName]-Beta's government has already sent an angry yet formal request for us to return the plunder.

items.name: One Last Plea
items.desc: The situation in the Beta-Universe is dire, and it's only getting worse. A unified cry for salvation was heard from the portal earlier this morning. Even with our best efforts, it seems like our kin will become one with the nothingness haunting their universe. If we want to save our alter selves, the time is now.

items.name: Offloading Optimization
items.desc: Having a second [Owner.GetGovernmentName] which is so similar provides us with an unprecedented opportunity. The calculations required to keep our consciousness organized every day take up many [Owner.GetTeamMemberPlural], but this task can now be offloaded to the second [Root.GetName]. The value of this is apparent, and while it might slow down the recovery effort of §B[Target.GetName]-Beta§!, we are sure we will still manage.

items.name: Desperate Drones
items.desc: In their continued distress, the other [Owner.GetGovernmentName] has lashed out and manically taken a hold of the Soldiers on [Target.GetName]! We must organize our defense drones before we are overrun.

items.name: A Trans-Dimensional Call
items.desc: The final divergent drone has been defeated. Our communication drones are once again detecting the presence of the other Overmind, but it's acting a lot submissively this time, waiting for us to initiate communication.\n\n"§BThis Mind apologises - instinctive reactions are getting harder to suppress as §RThe Static§! nears. We will ensure that we restrain ourselves in the future.§!"

items.name: Demands
items.desc: [FromFrom.GetName] has fallen to our Beta variants. They are now demanding the immediate transferal of some of their drones as well as the establishment of a sub-consciousness on our world to ensure the survival of their knowledge and existence.

items.name: Missed The Morning Check-in
items.desc: Recently, numerous [Owner.GetColonistPlural] have gone missing on [Root.GetName]. The only discernible pattern is that each was alone at the time of their disappearance. As news began to spread, a collective fear of going unescorted has gripped the colony. This state of unrest is causing considerable problems for our day-to-day operations.

items.name: Lucky Scan
items.desc:
Thanks to the implementation of the tracking system on [Root.GetName] we have a substantial lead.

As the most recent of our [Owner.GetColonistPlural] disappeared, and we quickly followed up with a scan of their last location ping. A decaying residue of charged particles was found in each instance.

We've established a special project to determine the true nature of the particles and their involvement in our missing [Owner.GetColonistPlural].

items.name: Holding Pattern
items.desc:
Using the residue as a reference, a system-wide scan found evidence of the particles within [Root.GetName]'s moon.

A search of the lunar surface revealed a few small airlocks buried under centuries of dust. Inside was an abandoned complex of admin offices, long-range matter transporters, and field manipulation systems connected to a network of highly advanced stasis pods.

Frozen in the pods were many individuals, including our missing colonists. There is little doubt that this facility functioned as a prison. We have yet to determine why they were taken and how we can free them.

items.name: Escape From The Moon
items.desc:
Far from a conspiracy, our missing [Owner.GetColonistPlural] were imprisoned because of a glitch.

A computer error reactivated the prison's aging transporter system and randomly identified our [Owner.GetColonistPlural] as guilty. The facility's architects used the pods for both prisoner storage and re-education. Freeing our people was relatively easy, but many original prisoners are still stuck in stasis fields. It should be possible to release them, although the lack of prison records means we cannot know the full extent of their criminal pasts.

Alternatively, we could restore the prison, giving special wardens control of its transporter system.

items.name: Bad Neighbors
items.desc: Most of the released prisoners on [Root.GetName] were hardened criminals. Having the group of them suddenly released has been causing issues for the colony.

items.name: Mixed Bag
items.desc: The prisoners released on [Root.GetName] were a mix of hardened criminals and political dissidents: artists, writers, and musicians.\n\nWhile the cultural prisoners are happy to share their knowledge with us, lacking any other option, many of the criminals have reverted to their old ways.

items.name: Good Neighbors
items.desc: Almost all of the prisoners released on [Root.GetName] were political dissidents: artists, writers, and musicians.\n\nThey're happily sharing their culture and knowledge with us now that they have been given their freedom.

items.name: Stratospheric Vents
items.desc:
Now that crucial colonization efforts of §Y[planet.GetName]§! have been completed, [Root.Owner.GetName] [Owner.GetScientistPlural] have turned their attention towards its lofty spires.

These mineral formations appear to be entirely hollow, transporting gaseous substances from beneath the planet's crust all the way to the thermosphere. For an as yet unknown reason, these gases also attract Tiyanki and other spaceborne fauna to travel across great distances to this planet.

A more thorough research project would allow us to study this planetary wonder and expand our understanding of these incredible creatures, or perhaps to devise a method of claiming these precious gases for ourselves.

items.name: Stratospheric Vents Studied
items.desc: We have determined that the vents on §Y[planet.GetName]§! have formed over millions of years as superheated gas and sediments cool down and solidify. The remaining fumes in the lower thermosphere form clouds that the Tiyanki feed on, plowing through with unexpected grace.\n\nThis affords us a rare opportunity not only to observe the creatures in close proximity, but also increase the colony's appeal to extraplanetary visitors. Alternatively, the vents could be harnessed for exotic gas refining at the expense of driving away the fauna from their ancient feeding grounds.

items.name: Stratospheric Vent Platforms
items.desc: The unique tourism opportunities on §Y[planet.GetName]§! could be enhanced greatly by building luxurious viewing platforms near the most active vents. This would allow visitors to get up close and personal with Tiyanki as our on-site researchers guide them through this one of a kind experience.\n\nThe more affluent patrons could join scientific sampling expeditions or even experience the thrill of setting foot on a live Tiyanki!

items.name: Stratospheric Vent Expansion
items.desc: Our engineers suggest that the underground gas reserves on §Y[Planet.GetName]§! could be fully harnessed by expanding the vents with mining charges. The dangers of the vents collapsing should be negligible, but the local populace should be notified just in case.

items.name: Vent Expansion Success
items.desc: The vent expansion project was a resounding success and our engineers are reporting increased gas production across the planet. As an unfortunate side-effect, some of the more fragile vents crashed spectacularly, causing minor damage to our facilities.\n\nDespite this minor setback, we have managed to harness the unique conditions of §Y[planet.GetName]§! to great advantage.

items.name: Vent Expansion Failure
items.desc: Miscalculations with the mining charges caused several vents to fracture and eventually topple to the ground, resulting in considerable damage to our facilities. While some refineries are now producing more gas than before, the total yield has decreased. The silver lining is that the collapsed structures have revealed unexpected sources of minerals.\n\nThese events act as a reminder that galaxy-spanning civilizations cannot be built without cracking a few vents.

items.name: Glacial Crisis
items.desc: The latest climate report from [planet.GetName] has come to a concerning conclusion. Inexplicably, the surface temperature on the frozen planet has been rising at an alarming rate.\n\nIf we fail to identify the reason for the ecosystem's rapid deterioration, the situation could lead to catastrophic melting of the planet's vast glaciers.

items.name: Cracks in the Ice
items.desc: The escalation of temperatures on [flooding_planet.GetName] is accelerating dramatically. This has caused substantial fractures within the icy surface layers, unveiling a vast subsurface ocean.\n\nFortunately, our investigations have identified a potential cause for this phenomenon. Due to our presence, the unique atmospheric shield safeguarding the planet has begun to exhibit critical fragility and could potentially collapse. Implementing stringent measures to curb our production would minimize our ecological impact. It might be enough to solve the issue.

items.name: Core Meltdown
items.desc: Our attempt to limit our emissions on [flooding_planet.GetName] has not yielded promising results. We have been only marginally successful in addressing the ongoing ecological crisis, and geographical lowlands are coming under threat due to the rising sea levels.\n\nAt present, our population centers remain shielded from immediate impact, but it is almost certain planet-wide meltdown cannot be avoided.

items.name: Vast Floodplains
items.desc: In the wake of our neglect to address the rapidly deteriorating ecological state of [flooding_planet.GetName], the situation has spiraled into an unprecedented cataclysm.\n\nThe disintegration of vast ice sheets has given rise to sprawling oceans, leaving behind immense devastation and upheaval. By building flood barriers we can protect our remaining cities, but more unforeseeable consequences still linger on the horizon.

items.name: Secrets of the Permafrost
items.desc: As the meltdown of the planet [flooding_planet.GetName] continues, a fascinating discovery was made beneath the permafrost. An astonishingly abundant polar reservoir of minerals and rare resources lies waiting, beckoning us with untold wealth and untapped potential.

items.name: Unfrozen Pathogen
items.desc: A disconcerting development has unfolded at our polar mining station on [flooding_planet.GetName]. Workers have succumbed to sudden bouts of unconsciousness, necessitating the implementation of a stringent no-pass zone for their safety.\n\nInitial investigations suggest the emergence of a dormant virus, awoken as its icy confines were disturbed. The true nature and characteristics of this awakened pathogen remain uncertain, leaving us grappling with a multitude of unanswered questions. The extent of its transmissibility and the potential danger it poses to the people remains undetermined.

items.name: Polar Riches
items.desc: In the hollowed depths of the polar regions of [flooding_planet.GetName], a mining team has made a discovery of monumental proportions. Veiled beneath layers of ice and snow, colossal crystals reminiscent of majestic glaciers were found.\n\nThese extraordinary formations, forged under immense pressure over untold ages, stand as a testament to the unlimited potential we have yet to uncover.

items.name: Climate Stabilized
items.desc:
We have reached an environmental breakthrough.

The innocuous byproducts generated through the combustion of our fuels harbor an insidious side-effect when coming to contact with [flooding_planet.GetName]'s bacterial clouds. We now know that these clouds play a vital role in retaining the planet's natural biorhythm by working as a solar shield. As the bacteria slowly begun to diminish, we inadvertently exacerbated the effect of our emissions.

Armed with this newfound knowledge, resolute measures have been swiftly enacted to restore the equilibrium.

items.name: End of an Ice Age
items.desc: A new climatic era begins as the last vestiges of [flooding_planet.GetName]'s glaciers sink into the ocean. The disappearance of the permafrost has uncovered an expansive underwater realm, filled with untapped resources.

items.name: National Treasures
items.desc: When we opened our colonies to the desertlings, no one could have anticipated the results. The critters have adapted seamlessly into our way of life, becoming beloved companions in households all across our territory.\n\nTheir rapid integration has led to speculation that these creatures must at once time have been domesticated. Whatever the cause of their innate friendliness, the rumor only adds to the fascination surrounding these extraordinary creatures.

items.name: Troublesome Critters
items.desc: Dire news has reached us. A few desertlings have broken free during transportation, forming a rapidly expanding community in the wild. The situation must be handled swiftly to avoid an environmental collapse.

items.name: Troublesome Critters
items.desc: Dire news has reached us. A few desertlings have broken free during transportation, forming a rapidly expanding community in the wild. The situation must be handled swiftly to avoid an environmental collapse.

items.name: Mammalian Population Stabilized
items.desc: We have been moderately successful in curbing the rampant desertling infestation. Regrettably, we have been unable to eradicate the elusive beasts. It is crucial to continue monitoring the situation, as it could reach a tipping point at any moment.

items.name: Uncontrollable Infestation
items.desc: Our attempt to control the infestation of desertlings has been rendered futile. The voracious creatures have already burrowed deep, expanding their large colonies faster than we can exterminate them. The battle is lost unless we allow our military to use their vast arsenal of explosives and noxious gases, a course of action which would risk the well-being of everyone on the surface.

items.name: Eruption!
items.desc: Tectonic events on [Root.GetName] have caused the Obsidian sheets on one of the giant plates to shatter. Lava pours across the surface to ruinous effect. Reports from the colony are dire.

items.name: Eruption Damage Report
items.desc: The recent eruption on the Obsidian Fields that shook our colony on [Root.GetName] has turned into an active volcano! Anything that once existed there is now buried under molten rock.

items.name: Eruption Damage Report
items.desc: The recent eruption on the Obsidian Fields that shook our colony on [Root.GetName] miraculously caused no damage. In a fortunate twist, it has also shattered the Obsidian for easy gathering!

items.name: Eruption Damage Report
items.desc: The recent eruption on the Obsidian Fields that shook our colony on [Root.GetName] miraculously caused no damage!

items.name: Strange Footprints
items.desc: Reports have come in from our outlying agricultural stations on [Root.GetName]. Several Farmers have vanished without a trace, their homesteads eerily undisturbed, save for the appearance of immense footprints in the surrounding soil.\n\nThe tracks are unlike anything examined in the planetary survey, quadrupedal, broad-toed with claws, and deep enough to suggest a creature of considerable mass. The colonists worry that we may be dealing with some unknown predator.
