items.name: A Dead Monster
items.desc: The expedition into the wilderness proved taxing, but ultimately fruitful. After days of following the creature's trail, our team arrived at a site of devastation: the corpse of the beast displays a heavily chitinous exoskeleton, thorned spinal ridges, and a segmented tail ending in a single curved stinger. The body is perforated by multiple punctures. \n\nBeyond it, concealed beneath a highly effective cloaking canopy of bioluminescent vines, our instruments detect an ancient garden. Marble columns entwined with ivy, smooth obsidian paths. Our team approached carefully until we caught a glimpse of the garden's caretakers: a humanoid species, elegant in bearing, their skin subtly luminous. Despite the harmonious appearance, the flowers and vines offered an effective veil. We would need to penetrate this glinting cover in order to approach the ones who lived beyond.

items.name: Continued Disappearances
items.desc: The frequency of the incidents has escalated. This time, the footprints did not merely pass by the homesteads; they tore straight through them. Entire structures have been ripped apart with alarming force. Traces of struggle suggest the victims were taken alive and did not go quietly.\n\nThe colonists are no longer merely unsettled; they are terrified. Several families have already abandoned their holdings for the colony center.

items.name: A Court of Blossoms
items.desc: I welcome you, travelers, in the name of the Court of Blossoms. I am King Tamperion, or as my kinship calls me, the 'Goldenhearted', sovereign not by rule of force, but by legacy and ritual. I serve as custodian of the this world and shepherd of my people, the Anathari. Are you alarmed to hear your own language? Never fear. We have been studying you ever since you decided to call [Root.GetName] your home. You must be a powerful people indeed, if you have managed to penetrate our cloak. We are honored to meet you.

items.name: A Court of Blossoms
items.desc: On behalf of the entire Court of Blossoms, I extend our sincere gratitude for your cooperation. Rest assured, the one you send to us will be welcomed as one of our own, and there shall be nothing they want for.

items.name: A Court of Blossoms
items.desc: So be it. Your decision is made, and so is ours. I have offered my counsel, yet now you must bear the fruits of your choice.

items.name: A Swift Attack
items.desc:
There was no warning. King Tamperion emerged from the heart of the gardens, draped in ceremonial armor spun from living vines and bioluminescent blossoms. With each deliberate step along the colony's edge, the world itself awakened. Vines slithered from the soil, while petals unfurled like blades. The air grew thick with a golden pollen, fine and luminescent. It seeped into vents and lungs. Within hours, it had claimed the life of many, inducing seizures, madness, and finally, death.

Only the intervention of automated colony defenses eventually brought him down. King Tamperion fell without a word; witnesses say his final gaze held not hatred, but a deep and solemn disappointment.

Where the Court of Blossoms once was, our scouts found only forest. It is as though the kingdom had folded itself back into the soil, taking its secrets and its sorrow with it.

items.name: One of Them
items.desc: We immersed ourselves in the ways of the Anathari. As we participated in ceremonial rites and attuned with their peculiar rituals, patterns emerged while meaning took root.\n\nDuring shared nocturnal ceremonies focused on longevity cycles and fertility, the Anathari began to reveal fragments of suppressed history. The folk spoke of an ancient and enduring blight that once blanketed the planet and still has control over the Anathari now.

items.name: King Tamperion
items.desc: There was a time, long before your kind set foot upon this soil, when we, the Anathari, served as noble stewards. We shaped this world in rhythm with its breath, guiding ecosystems, balancing currents, tending to the living world as one tends to a garden with infinite patience. Yet balance does not persist unchallenged for long.

items.name: A Seedling of Doubt
items.desc: What began as a peaceful exchange has taken on a subtler, more troubling dimensions. Participation in Anathari rites has resulted in delayed reports, fragmented memories, and altered sleep. King Tamperion remains courteous, but increasingly evasive when asked about the deeper purpose of these rites. His explanations, though poetic, often deflect direct inquiry. Even his title, 'Goldenhearted', appears in no recorded Anathari doctrine. Some now suggest the rituals serve not just as cultural bonding, but as tools of psychological calibration.\n\nWhatever the method, the result is unmistakable: we are becoming aligned with Tamperion and his kin. When he speaks of the Dark Immortal, it feels less like foreign entreaty and more like a sacred duty to help our dearest allies, the Anathari.

items.name: What Lies Beyond Death
items.desc: Our action was swift. A militia strike team infiltrated the Court of Blossoms. King Tamperion was meditating in the garden when we struck. But the king did not fall easily. Witnesses describe a terrifying display of botanical wrath, vines erupting from stone, floral constructs clawing through steel. By the time the king was brought down, the garden was soaked in luminous blood and ash.\n\nWhat remained beneath the garden astonished us, as it was a vault of biological treasures: ancient knowledge, botanical engineering, and stores of genetic stock from countless harvest cycles. The soil, now unbound from its ancient caretakers, was more fertile than any yet found on the planet. We may be entering a golden age of abundance.

items.name: The Dark Immortal
items.desc:
The scientists deciphered the essence successfully and located the Dark Immortal at a forlorn mountain top. Soon after, an expedition team arrived at the mountain's plateau, finding the site occupied.

At the epicenter loomed the architect of the trials: The Dark Immortal. An entity of incomprehensible origin, its form an unstable fusion of plasma, smoke, bone, and psionically active matter. Its voice bypassed sound, manifesting directly in the neural architecture of every team member present.

'Have you come to subordinate yourselves, little [Owner.GetSpeciesNamePluralInsult]?' it intoned slowly, its thought-voice laced with mockery. 'The Anathari are my dearest possession. But I offer you a chance. Enter the trials and prove yourself worthy of my regard.'

items.name: Trial of Bravery
items.desc: A single colonist was transported to a cave deep within the mountain, The Dark Immortal leading the way. A monstrous beast awaited in the darkest corner. The entity resembled a crustacean of impossible scale, its shell glittering with strange minerals and ancient alloys. It acted like it was guarding its turf, moving with an eerie coordination that hinted at a surprising level of intelligence.

items.name: Succeeding the Trial of Bravery
items.desc:
Steel met shell in the pitch-dark cavern as the chosen colonist charged into the abyss.

The titanic Crustacean reacted instantly, its claws slicing through stone, its bulk shaking the mountain. But the colonist was ready. Luring it into tighter corridors, they baited the creature's movements, striking at joints and sensory nodes identified in advance.

When the dust settled, the creature lay still, its final convulsion echoing through the mountain like thunder. The colonist emerged, covered in blood and dust, but alive.

The Dark Immortal gave a slow nod, as if in appreciation of the colonist's reckless actions. The trial of bravery was completed.

items.name: Succeeding the Trial of Bravery
items.desc:
Combat was never a viable strategy. The colonist observed the crustacean's movements, its aversion to light, its hypersensitivity to vibration, and most critically, its blindness. It responded only to sound. Every movement was an echo and strike reaction. The colonist formed a plan, not of confrontation, but misdirection.

The colonist hurled a series of stones against the chamber's central column. As the sound reverberated, the beast responded instantly, charging at the noise.

The central column shattered, bringing down the roof of the chamber. The colonist found refuge in a narrow recess, shielded from a partial rockfall. The crustacean was buried beneath tons of stone, trapped, and silenced.

The Dark Immortal seemed to appreciate the colonist's cleverness and wits. The trial of bravery was completed successfully.

items.name: Failing the Trial of Bravery
items.desc:
The beast's claws were lightning-fast and hummed faintly in the cave's darkness, each movement a blur, each strike accompanied by a low-frequency pulse that set stone trembling.

The colonist moved carefully, considering their options. A feint, a lure, an attempted blow, or perhaps a distraction. But the creature adapted faster than expected. Its next strikes landed true, and the cavern lit up in a burst of bioluminescent rage.

When the dust cleared, the colonist lay dead. We had failed the trial.

items.name: Trial of Wisdom
items.desc:
A sound, at first trembling and uncertain, began to form within the chamber. Soon, it was as if the rocks themselves were speaking:

§H'I am forged in silence, not conquest or codes,
A pact unspoken, that ancient grudge erodes.
No engine drives me, no mind commands,
Yet I steady the stars with invisible hands.
Few see me come, but all feel the change
A stillness where chaos once held the range.'§!

items.name: Failing the Trial of Wisdom
items.desc: As the words left the colonist's [Owner.Species.GetMouthName], the light dimmed. The Dark Immortal's voice cut through the stillness:'[Owner.GetSpeciesNameInsult],' it said, 'not everything can be answered by the sheer lust for power.'\n\nIn that instant, the colonist was struck. No weapon or flame engulfed them, just pressure and silence. They collapsed without a sound, and the chamber swallowed the body whole. We have failed the trial.

items.name: Succeeding the Trial of Wisdom
items.desc:
The colonist paused after speaking up, hoping to have presented the right answer. The chamber rumbled in approval, and the Dark Immortal seemed almost pleased.

'You understood,' came its words. 'Not all trials are of strength or power. Some require only the courage to open one's mind.'

A soft light filled the room as the riddle faded away. The trial was a success, and the path forward awaits.

items.name: Trial of Sacrifice
items.desc:
A colonist stepped forward to face the trial, and was swept up to stand on a vast, darkened dais. In the center: two obsidian chairs and a long, low table. A single weapon was placed upon it, an elegant, curved blade. As the colonist picked it up with one [Owner.Species.GetHandName], it hummed faintly with power.

In one chair sat King Tamperion, bound not by rope, but by luminous cords of elemental force. His expression was unreadable, showing neither fear nor peace, only stillness. The other chair was empty.

Then the voice spoke into the colonist's mind once more.

'The blade has tasted kings and cowards alike,' the Dark Immortal whispered. 'To pass this trial, one life must be taken. Take the Anathari leader's heart, or sacrifice yourself; the choice is yours. Choose wrongly... and the trial will end.'

items.name: Succeeding the Trial of Sacrifice
items.desc:
The colonist stood before the bound form of King Tamperion, silent, unmoving. Upon the obsidian table, the blade awaited. The Dark Immortal offered no guidance.

The colonist took the blade and drove it cleanly into Tamperion's chest, swift and decisive. He made no cry. There was only a soft metallic chime, like the distant clanging of bells.

King Tamperion looked up, eyes calm. The blade, buried to the hilt, had not pierced flesh, but something else entirely. His chest glowed faintly, pulsing with a golden light. King Tamperion the 'Goldenhearted' indeed...

The bindings around the king dissolved and the dais faded. The Dark Immortal spoke once more into our minds: 'You may proceed.'

items.name: Failing the Trial of Sacrifice
items.desc:
The colonist looked upon King Tamperion, blade in hand. King Tamperion sat still, his soft gaze offering neither plea nor permission. The colonist hesitated, then turned the blade on themself.

A sharp intake of breath, and the colonist collapsed, the blade clattering against the obsidian floor. The choice was clear: to spare the Anathari leader and to carry the burden alone.

But the Dark Immortal's words arrived with neither anger nor triumph: 'Compassion is not absolution. The blade was never meant for the self.'

A silent tear rolled down King Tamperion's face. With the best intentions, we had sealed his people's fate...
The trial ended, not in glory, but sorrow. The colonist was dead, and the path forward was sealed.

items.name: Innermost Desire
items.desc: The Dark Immortal stood before us, unchanged, unknowable. Its form was a silhouette against the stone, vast yet indistinct, as though it belonged to a reality only half-intersecting with our own. It made no sound. Instead, its presence bloomed within our minds, each thought delivered not in words but as inevitabilities.\n\nInto the stillness, the Dark immortal transmitted a thought, soft and almost pleased: 'You have gained my favor, little [Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]. You have impressed me. Now speak, what is it that you desire?'

items.name: A Grandiose Success
items.desc: There was a pause. A silence that stretched across thought and time, but then a hushed agreement. 'The Anathari are no longer mine to watch,' the Dark Immortal spoke. 'You are bound now.' With that, it vanished. No light or sound, only a change in the air, and the sense that something vast has departed.\n\nIn the cycles that followed first contact, the interspecies convergence between colonists and the Anathari intensified. Crops flourished extensively, and cities rose in harmony with the land. Flora and technology walked side by side. For the first time in centuries, [Root.GetName] flourished, its atmosphere no longer burdened by conflict, but recalibrated for peace.

items.name: A Rain of Golden Petals
items.desc:
'As you wish.'

The Dark Immortal withdrew from our thoughts, and with it, something fundamental shifted. The colonists felt a deep, unsettling churning in their spines. All across the planet, the Anathari began to collapse. No scream was reported, no struggle, only the soft rustle of robes folding into dust, like petals falling in the whisper of a breeze.

In the chamber, King Tamperion lingered a moment longer. His eyes blinked in utter betrayal and disappointment for the [Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] species. He raised no hand, spoke no plea. A single golden bloom fell from his sleeve to the cavern floor. And then he, too, was gone. There was no mourning, nor relief. Only the absence of what once was, a people, a song, a civilization, swept from [Root.GetName].

The Dark Immortal seemed pleased.

items.name: A Grandiose Failure
items.desc:
The colonists had walked the path to the Anathari, but in the end, it was not enough. The trials failed. The Dark Immortal would remain, its presence looming across the land like a blight.

King Tamperion would need to return to the Court of Blossoms, not as a friend, but as a servant once more to The Dark Immortal. A broken king in a broken kingdom. Our colonists would be permitted to remain on the planet, tolerated, but never trusted again.

'You sought to free them, [Owner.GetSpeciesNamePluralInsult],' the Dark Immortal sounded in our heads. 'But you were not worthy.'

items.name: War is the only Answer
items.desc:
We knew the power of the Dark Immortal was immense. Our assault was immediate and violent. The cavern trembled as the Dark Immortal let out a churning screech.

While our forces took heavy damage, we managed to bind the Dark Immortal. The cavern howled, and the air cracked like splitting bone. Then the Dark Immortal was gone.

Afterward, King Tamperion met the survivors. He approached the colonists and bowed deeply. For all that had been lost, the nightmare was over.

items.name: The Way of the Thralls
items.desc:
Across the planet, the Anathari faltered. Flesh, bone, memory: all they had once been began to fade away. King Tamperion was the last. When his time came, he did not speak. The colonists reported his end as a flash of light and a halo of golden petals.

All that remained was the Dark Immortal. We felt it settling into the hollow spaces in our minds. Something dark and ancient wormed its way within us. A transference, slow and absolute. From the Dark Immortal to us, from what had been to what now was.

Our colonists are no longer just [Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural], but something else now. Something ... new.

items.name: All Life Must End
items.desc:
A colossal entity emerged from the shadows, neither beast nor machine, but something stranger, its form shifting between molten geometry and seething shadow. It did not attempt to communicate. It simply devoured.

Buildings crumbled into the ground. Colonists were torn apart, vanishing into the air or crushed under invisible pressure. Within hours, nothing remained but a low hum echoing across the ruined plain.

Then, as soon as it came, the beast vanished, leaving behind a trail of death and devastation on a scorched planet.

items.name: Coincidence or Fate?
items.desc:
Patrols reported finding grotesque bodies in the forests surrounding [Root.GetName]. Charred skin, blackened bones, and expressions frozen in primal terror. No weapons were to be found, and no signs of any conflict. Nearby vegetation evidenced signs of extreme heat exposure and brief, localized gravitational anomalies.

But whatever hunted there is gone, and the planet is responding. Withered flora bloom in radiant abundance, and the local fauna have returned with cautious harmony. The rich soil appears ready to yield harvests unlike any seen before.

For now, the colony is safe.

items.name: Communications Intercepted
items.desc: By intercepting a message sent to the [CommSpreader.GetName], we have learned that they are in regular contact with another spacefaring empire that we ourselves have no contact with. By tracing this message to its source, we have been able to establish our own line of communications with this previously unknown actor on the galactic stage.

items.name: New Contact
items.desc: We have received a communiqué from a previously unknown spacefaring empire that call themselves the §H[From.GetName]§!. They claim to have learned of our existence by listening in on the communications of another empire we are in contact with.

items.name: Communications Intercepted
items.desc: By intercepting a message sent to the [CommSpreader.GetName], we have learned that they are in regular contact with another spacefaring empire that we ourselves have no contact with. By tracing this message to its source, we have been able to establish our own line of communications with this previously unknown actor on the galactic stage.

items.name: Face the Tempest
items.desc: In the aftermath of the devastation from the §HCosmic Storm§!, we have gained some unique insight on these galactic phenomena.\n\nBy studying astrometeorology, we can better protect ourselves in the future. This new field of research might eventually yield the means to master these storms.

items.name: A Tale of Two Planets
items.desc:
From the moment we detected [From.Planet.GetName], its mere existence has been a source of fascination.

It is not the collision of two celestial objects that is unusual, as the galaxy is a vast and chaotic place. However, in all known instances of such an impact, one or both of the bodies in question was destroyed.

The collision that formed [From.Planet.GetName] took place millions of years ago, and yet these two worlds maintain a strange equilibrium, and have even formed a life-sustaining atmosphere in the process.
items.trigger:
has_modifier = collided_planet
exists = owner

items.name: Precarious Balance
items.desc: The situation on the so-called "collided planet" has turned out to be far more precarious than anticipated. A recent series of earthquakes opened up the old scars around the impact zone, causing a significant amount of magma to erupt from the ground. Various planetary biomes are already beginning to suffer from rising global temperatures and the volcanic ash that clouds the skies.\n\nTo make matters worse, if the joint planets are not stabilized within the next 50 years, our readings predict that tectonic activity will continue to escalate, ultimately causing the complete disintegration of [From.Planet.GetName]!

items.name: Metamorphosis Unchained
items.desc:
Our top geologists came together and formed two possible plans to save the [From.Planet.GetName] from succumbing to tectonic terror.

The first plan is to stabilize the collision. While it would take many centuries to heal the volcanic wound around the impact zone, through careful terrestrial trepanning we can alleviate the pressure on the planet's crust, preventing further tectonic instability. The remaining volcanic byproducts will be used to terraform the planet into a stable biome.

The second plan is far more ambitious. Instead of alleviating the pressure on the planet's crust, the energy and materials generated by the volcanic eruption could be adapted to a tailored terraforming process.

This approach allows us to sculpt a multitude of biomes capable of sustaining every type of lifeform, turning this world into a paradise. However, there is a significant chance that this procedure will fail - and could even lead to the complete and utter destruction of this unique stellar body.

items.name: Collision Maintained
items.desc: Our efforts to stabilize the collided world paid off! The tremors that previously threatened [From.Planet.GetName]'s existence have been silenced and the volcanic byproducts are rapidly decreasing as we speak, returning the world to its fragile balance.\n\nOne question remains for our final terraforming push: which class of planet shall [From.Planet.GetName] become?

items.name: A World For Everyone
items.desc:
Extraordinary! We thought our efforts would only go as far as to stabilize [collided_planets.GetName], but it turned into something so much more!

Behold, a paradise, a planet capable of sustaining nearly every form of life imaginable.

To be able to save a doomed world and to transform it into something this inspiring - has there ever been a greater accomplishment? Fortune surely favors us.

items.name: Fixer Upper
items.desc:
While the world itself was thankfully saved, our endeavor to terraform the collided planet into a paradise has failed.

Our attempts to tailor the biome were frustrated by the planet's severe tectonic activity, although the worst of the destabilization appears to be over. Volcanic activity has returned to the levels first witnessed before the recent upheaval, and while the impact site remains active, it is unlikely to escalate any time soon.

The worst appears to be over. Our challenge now is to rebuild this world.

items.name: Home Asunder
items.desc: Our attempt to save the collided planet from impending doom has failed miserably. While our scientists took every possible precaution, their models were never able to take every contingency into account.\n\nAs the remnants of these worlds drift ever further into the void, the galaxy mourns the loss of this unique phenomenon.

items.name: Collided and Crashed
items.desc: The collapse of the collided planet followed our timeline predictions down to the decimal. Where once the galaxy was enriched by a unique phenomenon, now nothing but rocks remain.
items.trigger:
is_colony = yes
exists = owner

items.name: Crimson Crawlers
items.desc:
From a distance, [From.GetName]'s shone like some precious crimson jewel. Clay or other soil types infused with hard metals would be the usual explanation for such a geographical anomaly, but the truth was far more bizarre.

Bugs. Trillions, upon trillions, of bugs. They swarm over the surface of [From.GetName] in an almost unbroken carpet of multi-legged life.

Quickly dubbed the 'crimson crawlers', these invertebrates possess a remarkably hyperactive reproduction cycle. While not harmful to their native environment, [From.GetName] is not well suited for colonization with these creatures scurrying about.

One rather unorthodox method of handling the insects has been proposed. Initial scans show they are edible, so perhaps we have found a new food source? We advise at least investigating the opportunity.

items.name: Uncommon Cuisine
items.desc:
The idea of consuming the crimson crawlers may have seemed preposterous at first, but when a specimen was brought on board, it became far more palatable.

The insects are a creature of wonder, possessing an extremely advanced nervous system without the benefit of a central processing organ. More importantly, their pale flesh is surprisingly tender and moist, and even when consumed raw, the vermillion-hued exoskeleton was deemed both crispy and delightful.

The question remains as to whether the bugs would better serve as research material or as a delectable source of food. Cooking them might provide more flavor and fun, but eating them as they come will be quicker and easier, especially if paired with the appropriate condiment.

items.name: Brand New Bemusement
items.desc: Despite having been dragged across the galaxy by the cosmic storm, the orbital complex suffered very little harm. We found the living and commercial spaces of the habitat in almost perfect condition. Not a single bit of dust laid atop the surface that would betray a previous occupancy, as if it had never before been used.\n\nInside the central control hub we were greeted by a bewildering input system: dials with no explanation, levers with inconsistent settings and a great amount of buttons flashing a whole spectrum of colors at seemingly random intervals. Fortunately, we eventually came across a manual. Once this is successfully translated, we are confident we can reactivate the habitat.

items.name: Manual Override
items.desc: Unfortunately, our previous estimation appears to have been optimistic: the manual turned out to be just as incomprehensible as the control system. Half of the pages appeared to be missing and the pictorial instructions make significant semiotic assumptions. The other half of the manual is written in difficult to interpret hieroglyphs.\n\nHowever, the last page displayed a com frequency accompanied by a set of characters translated to 'help desk'. We're attempting this frequency now.

items.name: Your Call is Important To Us
items.desc:
The manual's com frequency connected us to the help desk mainframe of a commercial entity known as Skygarden.

With a friendly though neutral tone, the help desk AI informed us that it appreciated our reaching out, and asked if there was anything it could aid us with. Among the listed options were 'answering questions about subscriptions', 'learning about the new line of smart defense systems' and if we wished to know more about the corporation's 'social responsibility initiatives'.

However, the subsequent options continued to direct us to entirely unrelated topics. Worst of all, it would often put our [Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural] on hold only to drop the call. Obviously, the service AI has not survived the passing of time as well as the rest of the habitat.

Nevertheless, we will continue trying to find our way through this arcane system.

items.name: Maze of Options
items.desc:
Our [Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural] report that regardless of what they said to the AI, after passing through several menus, the system would simply revert back to a previous statement.

We attempted to run several simulations to map out the exact menu tree, but our efforts returned recursive errors and an inability to both solve and check the solution at the same time. Even running a quantum model achieved no desirable results. We suspect we accidentally collapsed a few wave functions in the process.

We're at a loss.

items.name: Following Protocol
items.desc:
Finally a breakthrough! The AI admonished us for using inappropriate language and stated we should wait until we are contacted by a customer service representative.

For a while we were left waiting, and then the com line was reopened. The entity on the other end introduced herself as the record keeper of the Skygarden Corporation. The help desk itself was an AI program she had inherited from the last record keeper. As far as she knows, the com station had not been used since the bankruptcy of Skygarden many decades ago. When we questioned why she remained working for a bankrupt organization, she simply said it was in her contract.

Explaining our situation, the record keeper dug up an old quick start guide to the habitat. She will transfer digital impressions of the pages to us soon.

items.name: Years to Earn, Seconds to Lose
items.desc:
With the new guide in our possession, restarting the habitat required little effort.

After the noise of activating machinery slowly died down, we decided to reach out to the record keeper once more to thank her.

She told us she had recovered some information on this station. Apparently it had been built over five centuries ago as a prototype, but was lost in the astrological chaos following a particularly nasty cosmic storm. The loss of property and development costs was enough to bankrupt Skygarden.

Helping us was the record keeper's first useful task in years.

"Besides," she said. "It was nice to hear my great-grandmother's voice on the line again, even it was just an AI."

items.name: Stormbound Rises
items.desc:
We are receiving strange reports from the [This.GetName] system. Apparently, the last cosmic storm raging in that sector revealed a ship of unknown origin. Bearing no call sign, it somehow cruised through the tempest as if entirely unaffected by the surrounding violence.

It did not respond to hails, and as soon as the storm dissipated, so did the vessel itself. This might have been dismissed as instrument artifacting, but the visual evidence spoke for itself.

Could this be a display of incredibly advanced technology, or is there something more ominous at play? We will be sure to report back any occurrences of this mysterious vessel.

items.name: Stormbound Returns
items.desc:
One of the research stations in [This.GetName] came to us with a startling report: During the last cosmic storm, a strange ship had almost collided with the outpost. Visual reports show it was the same ominous vessel first reported some time ago.

According to the space station, the hulls on the vessel were constructed from a strange amalgamation of organic compounds, calcium minerals and metallic alloys.

No organic life was detected, leading us to speculate that either this vessel was automated, or had somehow gone rogue.

However, the most baffling thing was yet to come: large sections of its propulsion system were clearly shattered by space debris. This vessel should have been dead in space.

If we assign a science vessel to monitor the next cosmic storm, they might be able to find out more about this mysterious craft.

items.name: Whispers in the Tempest
items.desc:
In the distance [stormbound_science.GetName] witnessed the ominous ship appearing between the layers of the storm. As it floated by, we detected wild readings emanating from the cosmic tapestry.

This finally provided an answer to why this ship could not be observed by our sensors: its physical manifestation had been stretched beyond the manifold, as if it had both entered and not entered a wormhole. It was likely due to the hyperdimensional origins of cosmic storms that the ship managed to return to our space.

Knowing this, we should be able to detect the next occurrence, and perhaps pull this craft back to our reality.

items.name: Stormbound Sighted
items.desc: The ominous ship has been sighted in §Y[this.GetName]§!.

items.name: Homebound
items.desc:
There it is! Positioning itself in front of [Root.Fleet.GetName], the ominous ship hailed us. A mechanical entity in an ornate mask appeared on screen. Identifying herself as B'Tiin, her tale was a fascinating one.

She was once a renowned officer, a true paragon of an organization known as the Convention of Benefactors. While on patrol, she and her crew were caught inside a cosmic storm, and in a daring bid for survival, she made the decision to overcharge the ship's 'Breach Drive.' This experimental technology had never been tested, and the vessel and its crew was trapped within the storm's hyperdimensional field.

Her story finished, a small container was released from the decimated ship. Inside was a collection of documents. "Take these home," B'Tiin requested, after which the transmission ended, and the ship disappeared into the spatial manifold.

The documents are written in a foreign script, and will take some time to decipher.

items.name: Letters From The Manifold
items.desc:
The contents of the strange container have been deciphered. One document contained a schematic of the ship's so-called Breach Drive. While still beyond our own technology, careful study of the principles behind its construction have already improved our understanding of hyperspatial travel.

Less beneficial perhaps, but more affecting, were the translations of personal letters. Each is addressed to a loved one, speaking of fondness, hope, and regret.

It seems B'Tiin's intention was to give her crew one last chance to reach out. Unfortunately, we have no way of knowing where to deliver these letters. Making them available to our own people could at least preserve their strange legacy. Alternatively, it might be wise to destroy them. Knowledge of strange ships and ghostly letters may be unsettling.

items.name: But They're Cute!
items.desc: From the moment the creature was discovered, its impact was undeniable, inspiring love and devotion among us almost instantaneously. Its four bulging eyes displayed innocence and invited anyone to stroke its soft, cloud-like fur. It seems particularly attached to [Root.GetLeaderName], spending most of its time on [Leader.GetHisHer] lap enjoying [Leader.GetHisHer] affections, not showing any signs of aggression or danger. It is as if it was perfectly engineered to be as inoffensive as possible.\n\nStill, some skeptics have pointed out how irresponsible it would be to keep a previously undiscovered life form aboard the ship without prior approval. [Root.GetLeaderName] vouched that it is definitely probably safe, but has agreed to request a formal investigation.

items.name: Biological Marvel
items.desc:
The docile hexapod did not need to be sedated or even coerced into being prodded and scanned. It seemed strangely agreeable. The crew nicknamed it Gurr, after the soft noise it makes when petted.

We have concluded that Gurr is an omnivore, and that its fur consists of familiar and very soft keratin-based filaments. But the true marvel and mystery takes place inside the adorable creature: it achieves total cell renewal within a month. This includes its nervous system, meaning that it could regrow fully functional body parts within a matter of days.

It seems unlikely something with such a sophisticated biological makeup is a product of natural evolution. We have never before seen anything like it, and cannot be certain of its temperament. Despite its apparent docility, it could turn on us at any moment. That said, since its appearance, [Root.GetLeaderName] seems more motivated to work than ever.

What shall we do with Gurr? Can we keep it?

items.name: Emotional Support Gurr
items.desc: The adorable creature was allowed to stay aboard the science vessel and has since settled in nicely. It calms [Root.GetLeaderName], lightens the mood wherever it trots, and crew morale is at an all time high!\n\nHopefully this remarkable wonder of "nature" will continue to be a cute, docile, friend to all of us. From now until the end, it shall be ours, and it shall be named Gurr.

items.name: The end of Gurr
items.desc: Given its unusual and clearly genetically engineered body, the creature could not stay aboard the science vessel. The risk of it adversely affecting the crew, or an aggrieved owner appearing to demand its return was simply too great. The deed was done swiftly and mercifully. In an instant, its soft "gurr" was silenced forever.\n\nWhile understandable, this decision has prompted an emotional backlash from [Root.GetLeaderName] and the crew. It will take some time to get over the loss of this adorable freak of nature.

items.name: The end of Gurr?
items.desc:
Neutralizing the adorable creature was meant to be the end of it, but its remarkable regenerative characteristics seemed to have gone further than we could have guessed.

Not too long after its demise, two identical copies of the creature were spawned from its apparently lifeless tissue. Even after our decision to terminate its progenitor's life, the resulting lifeforms are not showing any signs of aggression.

We shall leave it at this, rather than risk creating an army of Gurrs. [Root.GetLeaderName] and the crew have expressed their delight at being allowed to keep the pair.

items.name: The Imitator
items.desc:
The pod discovered in [From.Planet.GetName] has been left to the mercy of the storm. Even though the data signature it uses looks to be one of ours, the pod is definitely alien. We answered the request for communications cautiously, but we were met with elation by the capsule's inhabitant.

[event_target:the_imitator.GetHeSheCap] explained [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] has been dragged along by the tempest for some time and is seeking rescue, [event_target:the_imitator.GetHerHis] vessel's life support systems on the brink of failure.

When asked to identify themselves, the stranger bizarrely claimed to be a member of our own crew. The lie is painfully obvious, if for no other reason than the fact that everyone on board our ship is accounted for.

items.name: The Imitator
items.desc:
We brought the escape pod aboard our ship. The ruse ended as soon as the capsule's seal opened, after which the alien within immediately launched into a desperate plea.

During a routine inspection of the escape pods on [event_target:the_imitator.GetHerHis] mother ship, [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] was trapped inside and ejected into space. Sadly, no one aboard their vessel noticed [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] was missing.

Stranded for months, [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] used what little tech [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] could find aboard [event_target:the_imitator.GetHerHis] pod to mimic the energy signals of passing ships as a type of lure. However, even this failed to attract help. Worst of all, a cosmic storm took hold of the pod, dragging it lightyears from its home system. Driven to extremes by loneliness and fear, [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] concocted a plan to pose as a missing crew member of any ship that happened by. The pod-dweller apologized for the deception, but is glad to be alive.

items.name: A Curious Collage
items.desc:
Near our basecamp we were greeted by a set of peculiar city ruins.

The architecture showed characteristics of every civilization we've encountered so far - including our own!

However, the material composition is similar to what we use to establish base camps during planetary colonization. This is strange because these materials could never hold out for multiple decades, let alone the age our scanners determined these ruins to be.

It's unlikely for these ruins to have belonged to a mysterious precursor, yet the scanners persist in their conclusion. What could be at play here?

items.name: Weathered Situation
items.desc: The trail of the signals led to a pathway into the lower levels of the ruined city. Usually archeological sites of this type have an underground transportation network or a collection of safety bunkers. Instead we found a small cave system littered with scraps of fabric, polymer containers and even organic waste. It appears we are not the first to explore this archeological site.\n\nWorryingly, [Root.GetLeaderName] informs us the skies outside are turning green; a cosmic storm is about to develop inside [Fromfrom.getName]. Still, we press on towards the origin point of the signals.

items.name: Folly
items.desc:
Our progress was briefly halted by a set of badly damaged metal doors. With little effort we worked our way past this obstacle and a rudimentary storage facility revealed itself.

Its shelves were filled to the brim with an assortment of derelict technologies. Boxes of well known corporations had been carefully stacked against the walls. And finally, the source of the signals we had been chasing for so long: a transponder computer not unlike our own.

As we logged into the device and searched its databases, our [Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural] started forming a wild conclusion: the signal was deliberately constructed to appear as mysterious and intriguing as possible - mimicking and combining characteristics from other civilizations.

What's more, inside the boxes we found construction kits of the ruins we encountered above ground.

We contacted our basecamp to report our findings, but the cosmic storm has already started interrupting our com lines. The last thing we heard from [Root.GetLeaderName] is a worrying set of commands; it appears our basecamp is under attack!

items.name: Pirates!
items.desc:
The cosmic storm inside [Fromfrom.getName] turned out to have been concealing a pirate fleet! It was their crew that attacked our basecamp. The pirates asked us to relay this message to you:

§LDear absolute fools,

Thank you for joining us at our most elusive retreat.

Isn't it amazing just how quickly seemingly intelligent beings abandon all reason whenever they detect the merest whiff of ancient artifacts and devious relics? Perhaps you had hoped to find a means to destroy a great enemy? To build fleets as far as the event horizon reaches? Or were you just trying to be nice to your own people? How quaint.

Please don't feel bad - many others came before you, and our business model depends on that many more will follow your footsteps.

Now, for a modest sum of 2000 energy credits we will return something you have lost.

Reject our offer and who knows what terrible things could happen to [Leader.getHerHim] and [Leader.getHisHer] poorly armed crew that is still trapped on the planet.

Please choose wisely.§!

We are safe in these caverns for now, but we don't know for how long. Are we going to entertain these bandits?

items.name: Pushback
items.desc:
We have received a new message:

§LShame. There are a lot of fun things we could've done with those resources.

We will inform the leader and [Leader.getHisHer] crew that their lives weren't worth the effort or credits. Maybe a nearby slaver or a very driven assimilator might be interested. We hear nerve stapling is the hot new trend.

Entrepreneurs out.§!

We have used everything we could find to barricade ourselves in, and there are enough supplies to keep us safe for a while. But the pirate fleet is bound to break through our defenses eventually!

items.name: Won't Get Fooled Again
items.desc:
These pirates could not back up their cocky speeches with skill. Before long, whatever was left of their fleet became a part of the galactic ecosystem.

We reestablished contact with the crew on the surface soon after. They were rather shaken by the experience, but suffered no harm.

While we discovered no insights into ancient civilizations here, our experience instilled a need for vigilance. The expedition leader failed to see incoming danger - we will not make the same mistake.

items.name: The Pleasures of Doing Business
items.desc:
We've received a message in return:

§LMarvelous choice, if we may say so!

Let it be known that your contribution to our 'Fund for Disadvantaged Entrepreneurs in Need of a Resort Planet' has been received and processed.

You will find your leader and the complimentary crew in your possession soon enough.

And do recommend us to all your trade partners.§!

Soon after we were able to reestablish contact with the crew on the surface. They reported to be rather shaken by the experience, but suffered no harm.

While we discovered no insights into ancient civilizations here, our experience instilled a need for vigilance. The expedition leader failed to see incoming danger - we will not make the same mistake.

items.name: Terrestrial Telescopes
items.desc:
Boarding the station and activating the telescopes took some finessing from our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural], but it was nothing they could not handle. However, the corner of the galaxy the instruments were pointed at showed nothing of note.

Some interesting artifacts were found scattered around the station: detailed images recorded from the telescopes, neatly presented in decorative frames. Every single capture is focussed on cosmic storms, with multiple prints of each storm that has passed through this system. The telescope operator used different angles, zoom levels, and even artistic tilts to show the storms in their best light.

Upon deeper investigation, the artwork is the only interesting find aboard the abandoned station. We will archive them so many future generations can enjoy these images of rare power and beauty.

items.name: Hyper-Magnetized Planetary Core
items.desc: Unusual after effects are being reported on [this.GetName] in the wake of the recent §YMagnetic Storm§!. The storm's potent energy fields increased magnetic volatility in the planet's molten core, resulting in the widespread failure of technological infrastructure.\n\nHowever, the situation also presents a unique resource extraction opportunity. Metal-rich lava flows underneath the planet's mantle are now electromagnetically charged and can be harvested with the aid of mining magnets.

items.name: Electrified Oceans
Ghostly Apparitions
Volcanic Inactivity
items.desc:
The residual radiation from the recent §YCosmic Storm§! has led to erratic geological activity across §H[this.GetName]§!.

Most notably, the impact of the storm has rendered an active volcano extinct, cutting it off from its geological hotspot and severing the supply of magma.

These changes present us with new opportunities to develop the planet further, as the cooling magma opens up new lands.

items.name: Mountains in the Sky
items.desc: A severe §YGravity Storm§! caused an extraordinary transformation of §H[this.GetName]§!'s landscape. The storm's powerful gravitational fluctuations severed the planet's largest mountain range from its tectonic shelf, lifting it vertically above the planet.\n\nIt remains suspended in the upper atmosphere, held aloft by a residual gravitational effect of the storm. This remarkable upheaval has exposed previously inaccessible ore reserves in the bedrock underneath, as well as providing [owner.GetResearchers] with much to analyze.

items.name: Cosmic Clogging
Filters Unclogged
items.desc: The [Owner.GetEngineerPlural] have dealt with the hydroponic blockages and water shortages on §H[this.GetName]§!. The colony's water supply network has been improved and can now filter out complex impurities such as those introduced by the Stardust Storm.\n\nThese improvements to our water infrastructure can be repurposed to improve irrigation efforts across the [Owner.GetName].

items.name: Flightless Fauna
Airborne Again
items.desc:
Following the passing of the §YGravity Storm§!, the temporarily flightless fauna of [this.GetName] have taken to the skies again having taken shelter inside our avian reserve.

While many of the creatures have now returned to their former habitats, significant numbers remain in the reserve, seemingly enjoying the comforts and protections it provides.

This presents a unique opportunity to study the planet's avian wildlife at close proximity.

items.name: Eye of the Storm
items.desc: Scans detect irregularities in the eye of [fromfrom.GetName] raging in [from.GetName], indicating that the formation is carrying a strange mass at its center. These unusual readings warrant closer investigation, before the storm dissipates or leaves the system.

items.name: Drifting Capsule
items.desc: A mysterious capsule is adrift in §H[from.GetName]§!. It has no obvious offensive capability and is unresponsive to our signals.\n\nInitial scans show that its damaged exterior is constructed using advanced materials and unfamiliar engineering techniques. Further analysis is needed.

items.name: Drifting Capsule
items.desc: A mysterious capsule is adrift in §H[from.GetName]§!. It has no obvious offensive capability and is unresponsive to our signals.\n\nInitial scans show that its damaged exterior is constructed using advanced materials and unfamiliar engineering techniques. Further analysis is needed.

items.name: Storm Trap
items.desc:
[this.leader.GetName] believes that the mysterious capsule drifting through the [solar_system.GetName] system is an ancient "storm trap", which may have once been part of a larger defense grid.

The device's intake port is sealed tightly, but our readings suggest it is holding the compressed energy and matter of a captive cosmic storm inside.

Finding a way to open this remarkable container may teach us a great deal about storm mitigation, although at the risk of releasing whatever forces are currently contained within.

items.name: Storm Released
items.desc: [leader.GetName] completed analysis of the ancient storm trap's workings and was able to unlock its intake mechanism. As the ports opened, the §HCosmic Storm§! held inside was released into the void of the [solar_system.GetName] system.\n\nStudy of the trap's complex engineering has produced fascinating insights into storm-resistant materials and structures, though we still do not understand how the device is capable of containing storms entirely. This knowledge will greatly aid us in weathering future cosmic disturbances.

items.name: §YCaravan Fleet:§! The Racket Industrial Enterprise
items.desc:
Commiserations, [this.GetSpeciesNamePlural]! We chanced to see a big storm wreaking havoc in [this.GetName].

Of course, we were very sad to hear of the damage done there. We cried, indeed we cried! So please, allow us to help... with a special one time super deal!

We can provide gadgets, first class gadgets. Only the best from us! With these, when the next storm comes, you will be ready. So do we have a deal?
items.trigger: exists = event_target:caravaneer_fleet3_country

items.name: Psionic Switch
items.desc: In a flurry of psionic activity, [from.GetName] was switched with a [from.GetClassName] from parts unknown.

items.name: Mass Transfiguration
items.desc: A surge of psionic energy has swept through [from.GetName], leaving parts of its population altered in ways that defy natural law. Entire groups have been reshaped, their forms now alien and unfamiliar, as if something beyond our understanding has rewritten their very essence.

items.name: Stellar Transmutation
items.desc: A surge of psionic energy has remade [from.GetName], transforming it into a star of an entirely new nature. Now, a [from.GetClassName] casts its strange light upon the [from.solar_system.GetName] System, as if reality itself has been altered.

items.name: Fortified Entrance
items.desc: The entrance of the isolated complex on §H[From.Planet.GetName]§! is of exceptionally robust construction. Clearly built to last, its exterior features heavy armor plating, radiation shields, and an array of atmospheric sensors. §H[Leader.GetName]§! believes it was built to withstand extreme conditions.\n\nScans suggest that a large underground chamber can be accessed via a series of sealed security doors.

items.name: Survival Shelter
items.desc:
Having gained access to the main interior, §H[Leader.GetName]§! concludes that we have discovered an unused survival shelter, built long ago for some unknown organic species.

It is outfitted with well stocked habitation quarters comprising sleep pods, leisure zones, and a medical bay. Storage lockers on every floor hold deep reserves of unopened nutrient packs, batteries, and tools. Everything contained in this hidden vault is in pristine condition.

One final set of security doors remains sealed. We believe they will lead us to the facility's command deck.

items.name: Cosmic Alteration
items.desc: A passing cosmic storm has left more than mere devastation in its wake. On [Planet.GetName], it has created an entirely new geographical feature.

items.name: Storm Calibration
items.desc: The preparations towards the Cosmic Storm in the §H[target.solar_system.GetName]§! system have reached a pivotal stage. The next actions require intense focus and new resource commitments to forge a §YRadiant Storm§! by manipulating the solar winds of §H[target.GetName]§!

items.name: Storm Calibration
items.desc: The preparations towards the Cosmic Storm in the §H[target.solar_system.GetName]§! system have reached a pivotal stage. The next actions of [storm_researcher.GetName] require intense focus and new resource commitments to take advantage of the bloated state of [target.GetName].

items.name: Unleash the Storm
items.desc:
The intensified solar winds of §H[target.GetName]§! have reached critical mass.

We are on the brink of unleashing a §YRadiant Storm§!.

Harnessing the power of the Cosmic Storm has been no small feat. We can finally reap the long-awaited rewards of our endeavor.

items.name: Unleash the Storm
items.desc:
The electron fields of §H[target.GetName]§! have been fully severed.

We are on the brink of unleashing a §YElectric Storm§!.

Harnessing the power of the Cosmic Storm has been no small feat. We can finally reap the long-awaited rewards of our endeavor.

items.name: Unleash the Storm
items.desc:
The ions of §H[target.GetName]§! have been successfully magnetized.

We are on the brink of unleashing a §YMagnetic Storm§!.

Harnessing the power of the Cosmic Storm has been no small feat. We can finally reap the long-awaited rewards of our endeavor.

items.name: Unleash the Storm
items.desc:
The saturated particles of §H[target.GetName]§! have reached their breaking point.

We are on the brink of unleashing a §YParticle Storm§!.

Harnessing the power of the Cosmic Storm has been no small feat. We can finally reap the long-awaited rewards of our endeavor.

items.name: Unleash the Storm
items.desc:
The gravitational field of §H[target.GetName]§! has been sufficiently destabilized.

We are on the brink of unleashing a §YGravity Storm§!.

Harnessing the power of the Cosmic Storm has been no small feat. We can finally reap the long-awaited rewards of our endeavor.

items.name: Unleash the Storm
items.desc:
The stardust of §H[target.GetName]§! has been fully scrambled.

We are on the brink of unleashing a §YStardust Storm§!.

Harnessing the power of the Cosmic Storm has been no small feat. We can finally reap the long-awaited rewards of our endeavor.

items.name: Tutorial: Storm Manipulation
items.desc: We can §Smanipulate§! the §Spath§! of a §YCosmic Storm§! for our own benefit. Either to §Sdeflect§! them away from our systems, or §Sattract§! them to utilize their positive effects.
items.trigger:
is_nomadic = no

is_tutorial_level = 2
NOT = {
	has_country_flag = storm_tech_influence_tutorial
}
has_technology = tech_storm_manipulation
