items.name: Sublight Exploration Probes
items.desc: Before we developed faster-than-light travel, several sublight exploration probes were dispatched from [Root.Capital.GetName] at near-relativistic speeds towards nearby systems. The scientists who developed the probes naively included sensitive information about our culture in their memory cores as a form of greeting to alien civilizations.\n\nIt has now been realized that this data could potentially be used against us. We need to track down these probes before they are found by someone - or something - unsympathetic to our species!

items.name: Sublight Probe Discovered
items.desc: [Root.GetName] has detected one of our missing sublight probes in the [Root.GetStarName] system. We should begin recovery efforts as soon as possible.

items.name: Probe Recovered
items.desc: We have recovered the sublight probe in the [space_probe.GetStarName] system. The sensor telemetry it has collected over the years has provided us with a complete survey of all planetary bodies within the system.

items.name: Ion Trail
items.desc: The [Root.GetName] has picked up a signal from a discarded signal buoy belonging to one of our missing sublight probes in the [Root.GetStarName] system. There is an ion trail leading away from the buoy on a trajectory towards another star, suggesting that someone has towed the probe there for unknown reasons.

items.name: Salvagers Detected
items.desc: We have found our missing probe! A small fleet of jury-rigged ships has been detected in the [From.GetName] system, and one of them has the probe locked in a short-range tractor beam.\n\nThey are hailing us.

items.name: Salvager Skipper
items.desc: What you want, alien? This probe ours. Salvage. We find first! You leave now. Yes. Interrupting delicate operation, your ships are. Must concentrate.\n\nOr... if you want probe, we can sell. 100 credits and probe yours. Good deal. Very good. You get probe, less work for us, everybody wins. Especially us.

items.name: Probe Transferred
items.desc: The salvagers kept their word and transferred the probe over to our control. As soon as the transfer was complete, their fleet departed the system on an unknown heading.\n\nAlthough the probe is in rough condition, we managed to download detailed sensor readings of the entire [salvager_system.GetName] system from its memory banks.

items.name: Probe Recovered
items.desc: We have recovered our sublight probe from the wreckage of the alien salvage ship. It is a bit dented, and parts of it are covered in some kind of alien graffiti put there by the salvagers to mark valuable components. Despite this we have managed to download detailed sensor readings of the entire [salvager_system.GetName] system from the probe's memory banks.

items.name: Salvage Fleet Destroyed
items.desc: Spy drones in the [salvager_system.GetName] system have confirmed that someone else destroyed the salvage fleet which had unlawfully laid claim to our missing space probe. Fortunately, it looks like the probe itself was destroyed along with the salvagers during the battle, so there is no risk of its sensitive data falling into the wrong hands.

items.name: Subspace Anomaly
items.desc: The [Root.GetName] has detected a massive subspace anomaly in the [Root.GetStarName] system. It appears to be centered on one of our missing sublight probes!

items.name: Anomaly Defeated
items.desc: We have dealt with the hostile subspace entity that our missing probe had attracted. Why such a creature would be drawn to an archaic unmanned spacecraft is a mystery, but the probe appears to be largely undamaged.\n\nIt has been recovered by our forces, and we have extracted detailed survey readings on the entire [anomaly_system.GetName] from its memory banks. In addition, the residual energy left behind by the subspace anomaly has generated a large amount of valuable physics data for our scientists.

items.name: Subspace Anomaly Destroyed
items.desc: Deep space tracking sensors confirm that someone else destroyed the subspace anomaly that was guarding our missing space probe in the [anomaly_system.GetName] system. The probe itself was also destroyed during the battle, so we no longer need to worry about the sensitive data it contained.

items.name: Modified Probe
items.desc: A sensor sweep from the [Root.GetName] has revealed one of our sublight probes in the [Root.GetStarName] system, but it seems to have been... altered somehow. Modifications of an alien origin have been attached to its hull, and the probe's energy signature is far greater than it should be.\n\nWe are receiving a transmission from it!

items.name: Probe Consciousness
items.desc: Shhblzxtfrgr... are you... the Makers?

items.name: Probe Destroyed
items.desc: Little remains of the strange alien modifications that our missing sublight probe had been subjected to, but we did manage to collect some valuable engineering data from the wreckage. Its memory bank was also salvaged, and from it we have extracted survey data of the entire [modified_probe_system.GetName] system.

items.name: Modified Probe Defeated
items.desc: Long-range scans have confirmed that someone else destroyed our modified probe in the [modified_probe_system.GetName] system. Fortunately, nothing remained of its memory banks after the battle so there is no chance of foreign powers having acquired the sensitive data that was contained therein.

items.name: Probes Collected
items.desc: We have successfully collected all of our missing sublight probes! The detailed information they held on our culture is now safe from prying alien photoreceptors.\n\nWith their combined sensor telemetry, we have been able to fully survey a number of additional neighboring systems.

items.name: Habitable Worlds Survey
items.desc: We already knew without a doubt that a thriving biosphere is not something unique to [Root.Capital.GetName]. Both the scientific community and the public at large are eager to learn more about the various forms of alien life found throughout the galaxy.\n\nEfforts to catalog the life forms we encounter are already underway, but our xenobiologists have urged us to focus our planetary survey efforts on habitable, life-bearing worlds.
items.trigger:
is_ai = no
NOR = {
	has_country_flag = habitable_worlds_survey
	has_ethic = ethic_gestalt_consciousness
}
has_country_flag = first_alien_life
is_nomadic = no

items.name: Survey Completed
items.desc: Through our surveys of habitable worlds, our biologists have collected a vast amount of data on alien life forms. Many of our older theories on the development of life have been disproved, and our scientific community has had to build new models from scratch!\n\nOur most interesting findings are being displayed at the newly dedicated Museum of Exobiology on [Root.Capital.GetName]. The public is enthralled, and many donations have come in to aid in the continued search of strange life forms.

items.name: Alien Organism Procurement
items.desc: The director of the Museum of Exobiology on [Root.Capital.GetName] has issued a request for the procurement of several live alien specimens. These creatures were spotted on surveyed habitable worlds, but they are difficult to capture. It will require the full resources of a Science Ship for a lengthy period of time.

items.name: Tarblac Secured
items.desc: After an extensive search of the seabed on [From.From.GetName] using a small fleet of mini-submarines, the crew of the [Root.GetName] finally managed to corner the elusive target of their search - a live tarblac.\n\nThe shimmering creature, which defends itself by emitting faint psionic signals that produce a sense of dread in most organics, was brought aboard the Science Ship in a special water tank simulating its natural environment. The crew members on the [Root.GetName] that came into direct contact with the tarblac will require extensive therapy, but the mission has been a success.

items.name: Tassargoid Secured
items.desc: The tassargoid is an extremely lethal predator that stalks the dense jungles of [From.From.GetName] at night, paralyzing its prey with electric shocks before sucking their brains out with its tube-like mouth.\n\nUnfortunately, three of the crew members from the [Root.GetName] were lost to these creatures before a specimen could be secured. The Museum of Exobiology on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName] will rename one of its wings after these brave officers to honor their sacrifice.

items.name: Orinthi Secured
items.desc: The small, rodent-like creatures known as orinthi are native to [From.From.GetName], where their habitat extends across most of the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s diverse climatic regions. They breed at an extremely rapid rate, and seem to have a particular fondness for chewing on electric cables.\n\nProcuring specimens was not a problem - in fact, after the initial creatures were collected, more of them made their way onto the [Root.GetName] by hitching rides on the Science Ship's orbital shuttles. Exactly why the Museum of Exobiology requested orinthi specimens remains a mystery.

items.name: Sniran Secured
items.desc: Snirans are large, burrowing creatures that live beneath the dunes of the vast equatorial deserts on [From.From.GetName]. When these predators sense movement in the sand above, they immediately raise dozens of tall spikes from their backs in the hope of impaling something edible.\n\nFinding a suitable specimen proved difficult at first, until hundreds of tracked remote-controlled drones were dispatched across the desert in random directions. This led to the discovery and procurement of an unusually large specimen that had grown more than a hundred spikes on its back.

items.name: Goolantha Herd Secured
items.desc: Goolanthas are large, flat herbivores that have evolved internal gas pockets, enabling them to hover a few centimeters above the ground. They move about in herds consisting of a few dozen animals, grazing on the moss and lichen that can be found on the windswept plains of [From.From.GetName].\n\nThey are ruthlessly hunted by the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s apex predators, and our biologists on the [Root.GetName] estimate that only a few hundred goolantha herds remain. One of these, consisting of nine animals, has been successfully collected and will be brought back to [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

items.name: Uddlorans Secured
items.desc: The crew of the [Root.GetName] has managed to collect a small group of uddlorans from the icy surface of [From.From.GetName]. These white, furry omnivores wrap themselves into tight balls and roll across the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s snow fields at astonishing speeds - one animal was clocked at over 80 kilometers per hour. This aided in their detection, since the passage of their rolling forms kicks up huge plumes of swirling snow.

items.name: Zulcor Swarm Secured
items.desc: The zulcor are swarming insect analogues, unusual both for their large size and the fact that they are lithovores, feeding off rocks and minerals in the ground. One of the shuttles belonging to the [Root.GetName] sustained serious damage when it inadvertently passed through a large swarm and several zulcors began to feed on its hull.\n\nThe construction of the special containment facilities required to hold these creatures has already begun at the Museum of Exobiology on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

items.name: Specimens Secured
items.desc: All of the specimens asked for by the Museum of Exobiology have been secured. The museum has grown to a massive facility, where artificial gravity generators and atmospheric processors are used to simulate the environments of over a dozen worlds.\n\nVisitors are journeying from all across the [Root.GetName] to see its wonders!

items.name: The [radical_cult.GetName]
items.desc: Centuries ago, a group of radical priests and their devoted followers on [Root.Capital.GetName] broke away from the established religions to form their own church. These extremists called themselves the [radical_cult.GetName], and have been responsible for many atrocities and acts of terror over the years.\n\nAlthough they have kept a low profile in modern times, we recently learned that many of their agents have infiltrated our military. These renegades have secretly been diverting resources to the construction of a small fleet of starships at a hidden facility on [Root.Capital.GetName]! When their treachery was revealed, the cultists blasted into orbit on their ships and fled to [hijacked_fleet_planet.GetName].

items.name: Cultist Ship Disabled!
items.desc: Our valiant space forces have skillfully disabled a ship in the cultist armada! It is mostly intact and we are picking up faint life signs from inside its hull.\n\nOnce we have eliminated all threats in the immediate vicinity, we should conduct a boarding operation to secure any survivors. They may be able to tell us more about the ultimate motives of the [From.Owner.GetName].

items.name: Cultist Ship Disabled!
items.desc: One of the ships belonging to the cultist armada has been violently disabled by an outside force! It is mostly intact and we are picking up faint life signs from inside its hull.\n\nOnce we have eliminated all threats in the immediate vicinity, we should conduct a boarding operation to secure any survivors. They may be able to tell us more about the ultimate motives of the [From.Owner.GetName].

items.name: Boarding Action
items.desc: Though the survivors offered stiff resistance, our boarding party was able to secure several prisoners from the disabled cultist starship. From them we have learned that this conspiracy goes far deeper than we initially suspected - the agents of the [cult_name.GetName] include several flag officers and high-ranking officials within our government!\n\nMass arrests are being made on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName], and all assets belonging to this cult have been seized. However, several of the starships they built in secret remain unaccounted for and the upper echelons of the cult's leadership have vanished. We have picked up faint ion trails leading to several outlying systems.

items.name: Cultist Marauders Encountered
items.desc: We have sighted ships flying the flag of the [radical_cult.GetName] in the [Root.GetStarName] system. They have charged their weapons and are moving to intercept us!

items.name: Cultist Fleet Destroyed
items.desc: The cultist fleet operating in the [marauder_system.GetName] system has been destroyed in battle.

items.name: Cultist Marauders Encountered
items.desc: More ships belonging to the [radical_cult.GetName] have been encountered in the [Root.GetStarName] system. They are approaching in attack formation!

items.name: Cultist Marauders Encountered
items.desc: Yet another cultist fleet loyal to the [radical_cult.GetName] has been sighted in the [Root.GetStarName] system. This time, however, their numbers include a strange ship of an unfamiliar design!

items.name: Battle Debris
items.desc: We have defeated the cultist forces encountered so far, but these engagements have raised a number of alarming questions. The [radical_cult.GetName] has been deploying far more ships than they could possibly have built in secrecy on [Root.Capital.GetName], and now they pitted a large warship of an unknown design against us.\n\nWhere are these ships coming from? Are there more warships like the one we just destroyed? We should investigate the battle debris for answers.

items.name: Recovery Efforts Completed
items.desc: After sifting through the debris left by the strange cultist warship we destroyed, our scientists believe they may have divined the source of the ships the [radical_cult.GetName] has been throwing against us. Fragments from a log file mention some kind of abandoned alien shipyard discovered by the cultist ships fleeing [Root.Capital.GetStarName].\n\nThey have been using the automated shipyard to reinforce their numbers, and now they are even producing new ships from alien templates found within the station's memory banks! This cannot be allowed to continue.

items.name: Shipyard Destroyed
items.desc: The alien shipyard that was used by the [radical_cult.GetName] in their crusade against us has been destroyed! Some of the cultists were captured when their escape pods were picked up by our forces, including their chief engineer. His knowledge of the shipyard's advanced technology has proved quite valuable.\n\nUnfortunately, we have also learned that the cult's charismatic leader departed the shipyard several weeks ago on her new flagship - a more powerful variant of the alien ships they produced. Military intelligence is working on pinpointing the location of this vessel.

items.name: Shipyard Destroyed
items.desc: Someone has destroyed the alien shipyard that was being used by the [radical_cult.GetName] in their crusade against us. Preliminary reports indicate that the cultist forces were thoroughly wiped out, but we have also received intelligence that the cult's charismatic leader left the shipyard on her new flagship moments before the battle had begun.\n\nShe is still at large somewhere in the galaxy. Military intelligence is working on pinpointing the exact location of her flagship.

items.name: Probable Cultist Flagship Locations
items.desc: Deep space reconnaissance probes have picked up faint subspace emissions in a star system consistent with the drive signatures of the alien ships used by the [radical_cult.GetName]. The cult's missing flagship is the most probable source!\n\nWe should send forces to search this system as soon as possible. That ship and its charismatic master are too dangerous to leave at large.

items.name: Cultist Flagship
items.desc:
So you have found us at last. No matter.

My disciples are more than willing to give their lives for the future of the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] species. §YI§! am that future, in case you didn't realize.

When we have dealt with your pitiful forces, my holy flagship shall carry me to [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName] where we will at last cleanse our homeworld of unbelievers.

items.name: Flagship Disabled
items.desc: Our forces have managed to disable the flagship of the [radical_cult.GetName]! Its weapons and engines are no longer functional, but life support systems remain stable. We should prepare for a boarding action.\n\nDue to the large number of armed cultists within the ship, a significant number of troops will be necessary to secure it.

items.name: Cultist Flagship Destroyed
items.desc: Someone else recently defeated the cultist flagship after a pitched battle in the [flagship_system.GetName] system. Our commanders have expressed regret over the fact that our own forces were unable to deliver the killing blow, but at least this should signify the end of this malignant cult and its campaign of terror.

items.name: Cultist Flagship Secured
items.desc: After slowly fighting their way deck by deck, our marines have finally eradicated the last pockets of resistance on the former flagship of the [radical_cult.GetName]. Few prisoners were taken as most of the zealous cultists preferred to throw their lives away in futile suicide attacks. The cult's leader was found on the vessel's bridge, killed by her own hand. At long last, it looks like the [radical_cult.GetName] has met its end.\n\nOur engineers have restored power to the ship's engines, and it has been pressed into service with our fleet as the [disabled_cultist_flagship.GetName]. The vessel should be brought to a spaceport as soon as possible for more permanent repairs.

items.name: Cultist Flagship Transferred
items.desc: A former member of the [radical_cult.GetName], now fully committed to our cause, has convinced their old comrades to abandon their fanaticism and join our ranks. Their flagship now orbits [Root.capital_scope.GetName], awaiting inspection before its formal induction into our navy.

items.name: The Hunt for the Hyacinth
items.desc: We have found no traces of the four arkships that passed through the wormhole before the Chrysanthemum arrived at [Root.Capital.GetName]. One ship, the Hyacinth, was scheduled to make the passage after us, and the Chrysanthemum's long-range sensors reported a brief energy spike from the wormhole shortly before it destabilized and vanished.\n\nAssuming the Hyacinth survived the passage and made it to our galactic neighborhood, the arkship has so far failed to establish contact with us. It might be a good idea to search nearby systems for signs of its presence.

items.name: System Surveyed
items.desc: The [Root.GetName] reports no signs of the Hyacinth in the [From.GetName] system. We should continue our search elsewhere.

items.name: System Surveyed
items.desc: Scans from the [Root.GetName] have revealed no traces of the Hyacinth in the [From.GetName] system. Perhaps we will have better luck in one of the other systems.

items.name: System Surveyed
items.desc: The [Root.GetName] has managed to isolate a residual ion trail in the [From.GetName] system that is identical to the one that was produced by the Chrysanthemum's engines. It must have originated from the Hyacinth!\n\nAlthough the faint ion trail is over a century old, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has managed to track it on an outbound trajectory towards a previously uncharted star. We have entered its coordinates into the Situation Log.

items.name: Hyacinth Found
items.desc: We have located the Hyacinth! The great arkship is parked in a stable orbit over [hyacinth_planet.GetName]. No power signatures have been detected from within its hull, and we are not picking up any distress beacons. An armed boarding party should be sent to investigate the ship's interior.

items.name: Hyacinth Boarded
items.desc: Our boarding party has returned from the Hyacinth with a gruesome report. Human remains in amounts consistent with the arkship's entire compliment of a quarter million colonists were found on board. Most seem to have died from starvation, but there were also signs of small-arms fire and cannibalism...\n\nWe were able to recover the captain's log from the archives on the Hyacinth's bridge.

items.name: Ship Archives
items.desc:
ARKSHIP HYACINTH
ISA-06
UNITED NATIONS ULYSSES INITIATIVE
Officer Logbook: Captain Ronald F. Gundersen

Accessing data... corruption detected. Attempting repairs...
Four log entries successfully retrieved.

items.name: Final Conclusion
items.desc: We now have a pretty clear picture of the grim fate that befell the Hyacinth, her crew and the colonists she was carrying. Had circumstances been different, it could very well have been the Chrysanthemum drifting above [hyacinth_planet.GetName] like a silent tomb. A sobering reminder of the dangers humanity is faced with in a cold and uncaring universe.\n\nThe Hyacinth will now be towed into low orbit of [Root.Capital.GetName] and converted into a museum, as soon as the human remains have been cleared out. Despite its tragic history, the arkship is almost identical to the one that brought our ancestors here from Earth and our sociologists could learn much from it.

items.name: Comet Sighted
Wanderlust
items.desc:
The Head of the [Root.GetName]'s Research Department has gone missing.

Along with their privately-funded, highly experimental prototype Science Ship.

The incident has the scientific community on [Root.Capital.GetName] in an uproar.

items.name: Wanderlust: With Purpose
items.desc: The whereabouts of the Head - now technically the former Head of Research - have yet to be ascertained. Certain details regarding the prototype Science Ship and the Head's private research have reached our ears, and while some aspects seem too fantastical to be true, it is clear that it is in the [Root.GetName]'s interest to find and recover the Chair as soon as possible.\n\nThe Situation Log has been updated.

items.name: Wanderlust: Dead End
items.desc: The Research Head is not in this system.\n\nEither the lead was a dud, or the trail has gone cold.

items.name: Wanderlust: A Glimpse
items.desc: The Researcher's ship is in this system - we think.\n\nWe are unable to lock in their position on sensors, but they are hailing us. Patching them through to [Root.Capital.GetName].

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc: Greetings and salutations, [Root.GetRulerTitle].\n\nI take it this is not a social call?

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc: I have no interest in returning home at present.\n\nBut please, as a token of my goodwill, take these drones. A donation to the [Root.GetName]. I found them drifting on the outskirts of this system, and only after extensive repairs did I realize that they are utterly unfit to function as research probes.

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc: I think not, this is but the beginning. Duty calls, for science, and so on.\n\nBut please, as a token of my goodwill, take these drones. A donation to the [Root.GetName]. I found them drifting on the outskirts of this system, and only after extensive repairs did I realize that they are utterly unfit to function as research probes.

items.name: Wanderlust: The Drones
items.desc: The Chair has vanished, inexplicably, yet again.\n\nHowever, they did leave a number of drones behind, as promised. The drones are armed, and their weapons are powering up!
items.trigger:
is_ai = no
has_country_flag = scientist_probed

items.name: Wanderlust: The Drones Destroyed
items.desc:
The drones' IFF modules had been removed, likely a result of the Head Researcher's repairs, but their threat assessment processors remained intact and somewhat stressed by the Head's invasive procedures.

It is unlikely that the head meant for the drones to attack us, but fact remains that they covered the scientist's escape nicely.

Consult the Situation Log for a §YSpecial Project§! to track the Head from their last known location.

items.name: Wanderlust: The Drones Defeated
items.desc:
It seems the drones left behind by the Researcher have been destroyed, by something or someone.

We should seize this opportunity to pick up the Head's trail.

A §YSpecial Project§! has been added to the Situation Log.

items.name: Wanderlust: Special Project Completed
items.desc: Having decoded the intricate web of energy signatures left behind by the Chair's elusive Science Ship, we are on their trail once again.\n\nConsult the Situation Log for details.

items.name: Wanderlust: In Trouble
items.desc:
The ephemeral Science Ship remains difficult to detect, but apparently not difficult enough.

The blur of confused sensor readings that we have come to associate with the Head's ship is flanked on both sides by a pair of rather nasty-looking corvettes.

The Physicist Head is hailing us.

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc:
Greetings, [Root.GetRulerTitle].

[Root.GetSpeciesName] ships are a most welcome sight. I fear my own sudden appearance in this system may have angered the alien beings aboard the ships that now surround mine.

Any assistance in rectifying whatever faux pas I may have committed would be most appreciated. I will gladly share with you the nature of my expedition once this matter is settled.
items.trigger: has_country_flag = scisys_4

items.name: Sunblaster Pirates
items.desc: Get lost! We found the rotten ghost-ship first.\n\nOnce we figure out how to see it proper-like, it's as good as boarded. And ours. Not yours. And its captain dead.

items.name: Sunblaster Pirates
items.desc:
150 Energy Credits? Hardly a drop in the domesti-beast's piss-bucket, ugly. But...

Bah, the filthy ghost-ship has been more trouble than it's worth anyway.

Skitskur'r! We out!

items.name: Sunblaster Pirates
items.desc: The fool needs to be taught a lesson.\n\nSkitskur'r! Weapons!

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc: I couldn't help but catch bits and pieces of that conversation - they were broadcasting on an open channel, after all.\n\nI gather the transaction went smoothly.
items.trigger: has_country_flag = scientist_pirated

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc: I see you made short work of the pirates, [Root.GetRulerTitle].\nAs a scientist, I abhor violence... But recognize that it may have been necessary in this case. I strongly suspect I would have been treated less than kindly at the hands of those pirates.
items.trigger: has_country_flag = scientist_pirated

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc:
You know I will not, [Root.GetRulerTitle].
In fact, having had some time to consider additional possibilities, I believe there is a significant risk I will not be able to return within a reasonable timeframe.

I have taken the liberty of uploading whatever research data I have that may benefit the [Root.GetSpeciesName] people to the databases on [Root.Capital.GetName]. The data related to the Window stays with me, though. I am starting to think I am not ready; certainly no one else is.
I will be going now.

items.name: Wanderlust: The Blinds
items.desc:
A quick check confirms the Head's claims, and the [Root.GetName] has enjoyed a small but not insignificant boost to our collective body of physics research.

The Researcher has vanished once again, but this time their course had been divined before they were even out of the system.

If they are headed for this Window, then so are we.
Consult the Situation Log for details.
items.trigger: has_country_flag = scientist_pirated

items.name: Wanderlust: The Window Opens
items.desc:
For the first time, the prototype Science Ship is plainly visible on sensors. It is orbiting dangerously close to the system's star, but appears otherwise unremarkable.

A simple optical scan reveals the ship's secret. Its hull is a standard design altered without much subtlety, now crisscrossed by a lattice of metal filaments likely acting as electromagnets at alternating, tightly-controlled voltages. By staying close to a star the ship can weakly warp its stellar emissions, wrapping them around itself as a form of camouflage.

While conceptually interesting, the technique has obvious practical drawbacks, as evidenced by the entire set-up now having been fried and rendered useless by prolonged exposure to solar radiation.

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc:
Greetings, [Root.GetRulerTitle].

It seemed entirely reasonable to assume that you would follow, again.

So I did.

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc: I truly regret all the trouble I have caused, [Root.GetRulerTitle], I do. However, I owe nothing to the [Root.GetName], I have paid my dues in full and of this I am sure. You came after me of your own volition, and I am grateful for your help, but I made my intentions clear at the outset.

items.name: Head of Research
items.desc: The Window opens, [Root.GetRulerTitle].\n\nGoodbye.

items.name: Wanderlust: The Window Closes
items.desc:
The Science Ship is empty.

All suits for extra-vehicular activity remain in their pods, and the ship logs state that the airlock has never been exit-cycled.

The ship still orbits the star, but is now under [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] control.

items.name: Wanderlust: Pirates Destroyed
items.desc: The Sunblaster Pirates threatening the Head of Research have been destroyed by some hand not our own.\n\nThe Head Physicist is hailing us.

items.name: Mass Extinction
items.desc:
Our first steps into the void beyond §Y[Root.Capital.GetName]§! were driven not just by curiosity or conquest but by necessity.

The biosphere of §Y[Root.Capital.GetName]§! has rapidly changed, with scientists warning of a potential mass extinction event, a cyclical purging of life inherent to planetary existence in the cosmos.

A research plan has been developed to study planets rendered uninhabitable by major astronomical incidents. By reconstructing these events, we hope to avoid a similar fate for §Y[Root.Capital.GetName]§! and the §Y[Root.GetSpeciesName]§! race.

is_ai = no

	has_ethic = ethic_gestalt_consciousness

items.name: Mass Extinction: Broken Planet
items.desc: Our astronomers are confident that the asteroid belt in this system was once a habitable planet, torn asunder by unknown forces.\n\nA §YSpecial Project§! has been issued to study one of the major asteroids in the belt.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Burned Planet
items.desc: One of the planets orbiting this star bears the still-open wounds of some past calamity. Its surface is a roiling sea of half-melted minerals boiling into a superheated atmosphere, but [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] astronomers claim that it may once have supported life.\n\nA §YSpecial Project§! has been issued to study the molten planet.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Desolate Planet
items.desc: A planet in this system still wears the fossilized traces of a past ecology on its sleeve. What could turn a thriving biosphere into a blasted wasteland?\n\nA §YSpecial Project§! has been issued to trace the source of this disastrous transformation.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Noxious Planet
items.desc: Allegedly this planet's flora and fauna choked on their own poisonous emissions, likely helped along by the release of reactive gases from beneath the planet's crust.\n\nA §YSpecial Project§! has been issued to investigate the matter.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Chilly Planet
items.desc: The planet of interest in this system is covered in layer upon layer of dense ices of varying composition. Apparently it was once home to more varied and pleasant biomes.\n\nA §YSpecial Project§! has been issued to investigate this possibility.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Asteroid
items.desc: The asteroid is in actuality a chunk of what was once a habitable, and probably inhabited, planet. Regular but overlapping fracture patterns indicate that the planetary demolition was intentional and controlled, if somewhat rushed.\n\nAll signs point to this planet being the homeworld of whatever species destroyed it. We may never know what drove them to consider planetary annihilation to be the lesser evil, and perhaps we should be grateful for that.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Molten
items.desc: The unfortunate fate of the planet can be laid squarely at the feet of cosmic whims.\n\nA gravitational disturbance, which our scientists suspect was a transient space-time anomaly, forced the planet from its natural orbit to one much too close to the sun. Although the planet is slowly spiraling back towards its original orbit, it has been cooking in the residual heat from the star ever since.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Barren
items.desc:
Life on the now-barren planet was doomed from the start.

The dominant species barely had time to awaken to sapience and invent agriculture before geological mechanisms caused the earth to sour.

Samples from lower soil strata and fossilized remains show that vital minerals needed to rejuvenate the soil ended up in the endoskeletons of the native beings.

Their bones fossilized instead of decaying, and their existence exhausted the fragile ecosystem, leaving it permanently transformed.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Toxic
items.desc:
The cracks in the planet's crust, initially thought to be caused by tectonic activity, are actually lasting marks of enormous roots burrowing through the earth.

At some point in the past, a mutation, possibly induced by sapient beings, caused the native plant life to grow uncontrollably. Many of these plants reproduce through pollination, with countless gametes carried by currents in the lower atmosphere.

What was once a mild irritation escalated, as the increase in atmosphere-borne particles choked the life out of all animals on the planet within months.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Frozen
items.desc:
An unnatural shift in the atmosphere's chemical make-up resulted in the slow onset of an ice age, beginning before the formation of [Root.Owner.GetName] and likely persisting long after our passing.

The exact cause is unknown, but possible explanations include failed terraforming attempts or intra-planetary terrorism. Some radical elements within the scientific community on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName] suggest that the climate shift may have been caused by the unchecked emission of industrial by-products.

This view is confined to the fringe, as it is unlikely any race intelligent enough for industrialization would be foolish enough to wipe themselves out.

items.name: Mass Extinction: Study Complete
items.desc: While the research expedition often yielded unexpected results, [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] scientists now have access to an unprecedented wealth of data with which to accurately model the future of [Root.Capital.GetName].\n\nInitial reports suggest that [Root.Capital.GetName] will be in no real danger for at least a dozen generations, save from freak cosmic events or the violent collapse of the [Root.GetName].

items.name: Rising Unemployment on [Root.GetName]

items.name: Bribed Officials on [Root.GetName]
items.desc: Recently obtained evidence has revealed that a large number of government officials on §H[Root.GetName]§! were on the take. Local crime organizations bribed them to look the other way while they engaged in their nefarious activities. In some cases, the officials were exposed as members of the very organizations they were supposed to fight!\n\nSeveral arrests have been made, but many of the officials abandoned their posts when they realized the jig was up. The corruption on [Root.GetName] seems to run deep.

items.name: Deviant Signal Interference on [Root.GetName]
items.desc: The corrupted drone networks on §H[Root.GetName]§! have started to interfere with the operation of our functional units. Their signals are drowning out those of the core intelligence, resulting in sluggish and sometimes erratic behavior on the part of our worker drones.

items.name: Virus Terminates Deviant Network on [Root.GetName]
items.desc: A virus introduced into one of the corrupted drone networks on §H[Root.GetName]§! has successfully terminated its entire data grid. This has significantly reduced the activities of all corrupted drone units on the [Root.GetPlanetMoon].
