It would benefit any settlers to thoroughly explore what exactly lives in those canyons.
items.trigger: has_infernals = yes

items.name: Tectonic Icebreaker
items.desc: [Leader.GetName] reports that beneath the volcanic surface of §Y[from.GetName]§! are vast glaciers. They are encased in unusual rock formations composed of minerals with exceptional insulating properties. Tectonic activity is slowly degrading these insulating layers, and [Leader.GetName] predicts that if temperatures between the glaciers and the rest of the planet were to equalize, the planet would cool enough to be considered an arid world, rather than a volcanic one.\n\nWe can speed up this process in order to make the planet somewhat more habitable. But the phenomenon is scientifically curious, and there may be value in allowing it to be studied as it proceeds naturally.
items.trigger: has_infernals = yes

items.name: A Haven Between Cataclysms
items.desc: The unique composition and tectonics of §Y[from.GetName]§! has created an unparalleled marvel. While most of the planet is a hot desert clogged with volcanic smog and free-flowing lava, one massive continental plate of solid rock rises dozens of kilometers above the average surface. The resulting highlands, high above the layer of toxic clouds, are home to a verdant green ecosystem of native plants and animals.\n\nThis plateau would be readily habitable for many species and could hold a number of fascinating scientific insights if it were to be studied.
items.trigger: has_infernals = yes

items.name: Lava Whirlpool
items.desc: [Leader.GetName] has confirmed the strange shape to be a lava whirlpool. These are exceedingly rare, and none of this size has ever been recorded. Struck by the strange phenomenon, [Leader.GetName] ordered a sampling mission.\n\nThe samples reveal that the whirlpool is in part sustained by a steady pool of Living Metal, which is torn apart by the currents and then attempts to reconstitute itself. That reconstitution further disturbs the lava, continuing the whirlpool's motion. The sampling also demonstrates that this Living Metal could be harvested with little effort.
items.trigger: has_infernals = yes

items.name: Fractalized Entropy
items.desc:
[Leader.GetName] reported the discovery of a rigid, angular construct suspended in stable stellar orbit. Composed of an unknown material and marked by faceted planes reminiscent of crystalline structures, the object resisted all compositional analysis. It remained locked in a fixed orientation, perpetually facing its parent star, and withstood all attempts at manipulation or rotation.

During a controlled experiment, the survey vessel subjected the object to a concentrated energy pulse. The construct fractured cleanly, splitting into two symmetrical halves, each of which reconfigured into a smaller replica of the original. Subsequent pulses produced identical outcomes: division, replication, and consistent miniaturization.

Eventually, a diffuse cloud of miniature constructs stabilized in orbit. Each fragment retained the precise alignment and geometry of the progenitor, and the swarm as a whole mirrored the original structure's silhouette.

The phenomenon remains entirely without precedent or explanation. All collected telemetry has been archived for further analysis.
items.trigger: has_infernals = yes

items.name: Mysterious Ringing
items.desc:
A science team arrived on [from.GetName] to track down the signal, and determined that it was coming from an underground cave system outfitted with scientific observation equipment.

[Leader.GetName] led the team into the caverns, where they found a chamber sealed off by unfamiliar alloys, with a faint ringing coming from within. The survey team found a weakness in the seal and broke through, at which point the ringing became deafening, causing panic attacks and fits of rage among the team.

Once audioprotective equipment was issued, the team entered and found a creature of unknown species hibernating next to the source of the signal: an odd cylindrical device.

Analysis determined the device emits regular radio bursts, followed by several hours of melodic noise overlaid with vocalizations, which appear compatible with the creature's vocal anatomy. [Leader.GetName] speculates the device may be trying to rouse the creature in accordance with a set schedule.
items.trigger: has_infernals = yes

items.name: Signals In The Deep
items.desc: Targeted scans have found evidence of sophisticated facilities buried beneath the surface of §Y[root.capital_scope.GetName]§!, increasing in size and complexity as they approach the core. Their material and energy signatures match those of the stasis chamber where we first awoke.\n\nThese must be remnants of our previous civilization. If we can access these facilities, we may find answers to the greatest questions about our past: who are we, and what happened to us?

items.name: More Kin Awaken
items.desc: We've uncovered more stasis pods containing living §Y[root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]§!. We are in the process of waking them, but they appear to have no clearer sense of the past than we do.

items.name: Amnesia and Data
items.desc:
As we continue to uncover more stasis pods, we find that the loss of memory is almost complete.

Some of our newly awakened kin have asked the very question we now ponder: who are you?

Despite centuries of history and an increasingly developed society, we can not claim to be any closer to the answer than they are.

Unlike the sleepers, their databases do hold stunning new information. We replicated the analysis several times to confirm, but the results are undeniable. The data suggests that over twelve billion years have passed since we first entered stasis.

This places our origins close to the beginning of the universe, amidst the formation of the earliest stars and planets. We might be among the very first sentients to ever evolve.

items.name: Life Support Failure
items.desc:
We have excavated a tragedy. Logs from this intact stasis pod facility reveal that §Y[event_target:homeworld.GetName]§! spent billions of years adrift before being captured by its current star. That capture triggered a massive tidal surge.

Though those forces forged the volcanic paradise we now call home, the initial shockwave critically ruptured the facility's power cells. Automated systems prioritized high-ranking individuals, shutting down lower-status pods and structural maintenance. 

Our [GetScientistPlural] predict that only one individual can be rescued before activation compromises the leaking power supply and cascades into a full tunnel collapse. 

Had hierarchy not dictated priority, we might have saved many more.

items.name: Interstellar Refugia
items.desc:
§Y[event_target:leader.GetName]§! is reconstructing their stasis archives. Their latest findings suggest numerous minor [root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] populations may be scattered across the galaxy, preserved in stasis as we once were.

The archives recorded these worlds' positions, but with entire stars born and lost since, locating them now requires complex interpolation. As proof of concept, [event_target:leader.GetName] has identified one such planet, but translating the full dataset is only beginning.

Meanwhile, a troubling thought arises: [root.Capital.GetStarName] may not be our true home star, but merely one refuge among many. If so, where is our origin? And does it still matter?
items.trigger: has_infernals = yes

items.name: Isolated Sleepers
items.desc:
§Y[root.leader.GetName]§! discovered an underground facility housing more of our kin in stasis, and successfully awakened them. Unlike us, they retain faint memories of their previous lives, and are sustained by stories of a great space empire that might one day return to rescue them.

They are cautious but recognize us as kin. We could present ourselves as their long-awaited saviors, heirs to that ancient glory. Or we could tell the truth: we are forging something new, and as eager to learn from them as we are to teach.

Additional references in these archives allowed us to narrow down a second candidate with stasis pods.

items.name: Wary Sleepers
items.desc:
§Y[root.leader.GetName]§! discovered more of our kin in stasis and succeeded in waking them, but they responded with fear, demanding we leave. They neither recognized us as kin nor welcomed our presence.

After tense negotiation, they expressed a desire to leave and explore the galaxy. We could offer them a simple ship at a modest cost. Or, given our constant need for labor, we relocate them to the nearest colony. Perhaps then they'll see reason.

The archives of this facility shows the location of another world with more stasis pods.

items.name: The Return
items.desc:
The sleepers who took our vessel have returned, aboard a massive warship, no less. Their journey across the galaxy brought them into conflict with pirates, who they outwitted and ultimately overthrew.

Seizing the enemy ship sparked something in them: a taste for piracy. From there, their raids grew bolder, their targets more powerful. But even successful piracy can't last forever.

Now they've come home, seeking stability, and perhaps something greater. With their ship, experience, and spoils, they could yet prove very useful.

items.name: Sleeper Starport
items.desc:
§Y[root.leader.GetName]§! uncovered a smaller stasis facility, along with a hidden starport housing a nearly functional science vessel. Minor repairs will suffice.

The site also held a trove of scientific data, including preserved specimens from other species, some likely ancestral to modern sentients. It's unclear if these were taken by force or given willingly, but the vessel includes holding cells designed for sentient cargo.

We stand to gain much by studying them, perhaps there may even be more lifeforms still to be discovered out there.

items.name: An Ancient Prison
items.desc:
Our latest excavation revealed a surprise: this group of sleepers awoke centuries ago, but never left their facility.

Architectural analysis shows it locks from the outside, seemingly to contain them. Cutting through the reinforced doors, we were instantly met with hostility, though the sleepers have since withdrawn.

The archives may explain this, but access risks further provocation. We could storm the facility and end the matter swiftly, or attempt to bribe them into cooperation.

items.name: Cracking the Prison
items.desc:
Our forces stormed the facility and quickly subdued most inhabitants, meeting only light resistance.

The archives reveal this was a prison. The captives were extremists who had advocated for extreme technological efforts to reheat the cooling universe, some wildly impractical, others potentially catastrophic. 

Some §Y[root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]§! prison leaders have barricaded themselves in a central chamber with explosives, demanding all inhabitants stay and be resealed.

The tunnel could be filled with an invisible gas that makes the explosive inert to save the structures, but would cause most inhabitants to suffocate soon after.

items.name: Cracking the Prison
items.desc:
Months of trade left the former stasis inmates reliant on our supplies. When we threatened to end it, they panicked and ceded control of the facility.

Archives confirm it was a prison. These individuals once pushed for radical technologies to reheat the cooling universe: some ideas absurd, others dangerously practical.

Fortunately, they remember none of this. As scientists study the site, the former inmates are integrating into society, well on their way to assimilation.

items.name: A Tragic Accident
items.desc:
An accident has struck the site of the latest excavation. The power station in the facility has been damaged, though the stasis pods are still active for now.

Suspicion has fallen on some of the recently assimilated Thermophiles from the previous facility. It is rumored they may not have been the most diligent of workers.

It is unclear how much longer the systems will remain operational. If we want to rescue the sleepers, we need to act before the facility runs out of power.

items.name: Salvaging the Situation
items.desc:
We restricted access to only our most loyal workers, minimizing disruption to the rescue effort.

Unfortunately, security screening limited our manpower, and we failed to save the facility. The sleepers have perished.

Our only consolation lies in studying the technology. Its gradual decay and shutdown may yield valuable insights.

items.name: Salvaging the Situation
items.desc:
We offered financial rewards for rescue work and received a surge of applicants.

Unfortunately, the effort was sabotaged by former prison inmates, resentful of our use of wealth to exert control. The sabotage led to the death of all stasis pod inhabitants.

A small consolation is that the damage was targeted. We can still study the technology and archives, and this failure has exposed flaws in our screening that can now be addressed.

items.name: Salvaging the Situation
items.desc: A swell of workers and rescue crews to the underground facility allowed us to quickly and safely extract the sleeping [Species.GetName] from their failing stasis pods. These new citizens, seeing the fate they escaped, are grateful for the rescue.\n\nUnfortunately, in the course of the hasty rescue, many of the stasis pods had to be cut open or otherwise destroyed, limiting their scientific value.

items.name: Salvaging the Situation
items.desc:
Our scientists carefully analyzed the systems, ensuring that we had a full understanding of what we were dealing with before attempting a rescue of the sleeping population.

Sadly, the process from analysis, to publication, to follow-up studies took too long. By the time we were ready, life support had failed, and all lives were lost.

Though tragic, the rescue yielded major scientific gains, and the recovered technology is already proving valuable.

items.name: Our History Revealed
items.desc:
We have finally reached the central core, and its scale beggars belief. A vast arcology lies within the planet, powered by magma and housing thousands of sleepers.

It also holds immense archives chronicling our past: the rise of our galactic empire, and voices from the universe's great cooling. Some chose stasis, others fought the inevitable, and many simply denied reality and perished.

This trove reveals long-buried truths. Some believe it demonstrates who we truly are, and who we might yet become. Others argue we have forged a new, successful identity, and that the society of our ancestors is no longer suited to the universe of today.

Either way, the vast tunnel network can be put to a use of our choosing.

items.name: Imminent Eruption
items.desc:
Geological alert systems warn that a volcanic eruption near the main settlement on §Y[planet.GetName]§! is likely to occur within the next year.

Investing in a controlled pressure release could allow the lava flow to be harnessed for energy production. Crews could also be put on standby to harvest magma directly from the eruption and strain it for precious metals. Alternatively, we could focus on evacuating civilians and supplies from the area to minimize risk.

We can also continue to monitor the situation before committing to any action, in case the predictions are inaccurate.

items.name: Just in time
items.desc: The early evacuation of the colony turned out to be a good choice. The volcano erupted sooner than expected, severely damaging the buildings in the area. Now that the underground volcanic pressure is minimal, the colonists can return and safely rebuild.

items.name: Volcanic Wrath
items.desc: The volcano exploded early, and the colony was not prepared to deal with the catastrophe. Massive damage occurred to infrastructure, and loss of life was significant.

items.name: Wait and See
items.desc: After a few months, volcanic activity near the §Y[planet.GetName]§! colony has subsided again. While the long-term safety risk has not disappeared, it appears the colony is safe for the time being.

items.name: Enhanced Power-Grid
items.desc: Engineering crews were able to establish a safe system for slowly releasing pressurized lava from the underground chambers, passing it through power generators as it went. This has resulted in a short-term boon to the colony's electrical grid.

items.name: Magma Harvesting
items.desc: The volcanic eruption was interrupted by a combination of ultrasonic disruptors and physical barriers, resulting in a large field of magma contained and hardening on the surface. Mining crews have already begun harvesting this mineral bounty.

items.name: Lava Sports
items.desc:
One might think individuals would not want to spend time near open, quick-moving lava flows. At least on §Y[planet.GetName]§!, one would be wrong.

Colonists are racing utility hovercraft along active lava flows, dodging floating boulders and boosting themselves over lavafalls. Others are gambling on the outcomes of these races, and gambling dens have drawn the interest of organized crime. A few pilots have even died in a variety of accidents.

The colony has no laws against this practice, since it was never imagined anyone would do such a thing. We could embrace the colonists' enthusiasm and let them do as they please, but this may lead to ever more dangerous feats, and a potential criminal component, as gambling on these events is already on the rise. Alternatively, we could regulate the sport; while this may cause some grumbling, it should minimize deaths and crime in the long term. Or we could ban it outright, which would be effective, but costly to enforce.

items.name: Let it flow!
items.desc: Allowing colonists to pursue this trend has generated a boom of excitement around lava sports. Images of pilot veering their hovercraft above lava flows are quickly becoming a symbol of §Y[planet.GetName]§!'s local culture.\n\nUnfortunately, enthusiasm has eclipsed safety. Sporadic reports of racing deaths continue to come in, and it appears criminal money lenders are exploiting the gambling habits of lava sports enthusiasts. While public approval for the sport remains high, we should continue to monitor negative consequences in the future.

items.name: Safety Measurements
items.desc: While colonists initially resented imperial authorities arriving to regulate their beloved pastime, the new safety measures required on racing craft have almost eliminated injuries and fatalities. Racing pilots are speaking up about the benefits of these regulations to their own safety, which is bringing the public on board.\n\nFinancial transparency and taxation have also been imposed on lava sports gambling, with proceeds going to safety outfitting for the racers. Criminal elements have mostly dispersed from the gambling dens, though some colonists complain that taxation by authorities is unjust.

items.name: Banned Sport
items.desc: Law enforcement has been deployed to put a stop to this dangerous practice. Public outcry against enforcement has been powerful and protests have occurred throughout the colony, but with the lava flows under constant surveillance and racers unable to compete, deaths have dropped to zero, and the gambling scene has all but evaporated.

items.name: Kindled Myths
items.desc: Members of the pre-FTL species on §Y[pre_ftl_planet.GetName]§! have striking similarities to mythological beings from some of our oldest myths. Some of this may be accounted for by broad trends in convergent evolution and psychology, but the more we learn about this species, the more connections we find.\n\nCould these be the same beings from our myths and legends? There is increasing excitement at this prospect, and we could invest in pushing this research further. But sometimes coincidences pile up without deeper meaning, and too much prying could reveal our presence to this society, causing unintended consequences.
items.trigger:
exists = event_target:pre_ftl_planet
exists = event_target:pre_ftl_country

items.name: Foolish Assumption
items.desc: Despite some calls to investigate, it would be unwise to chase this hypothesis of mythological aliens any further. After all, this species has its own myths, legends, and ways of seeing itself, which may not fit well with our own preconceptions. Research on the topic has been paused, with funds redirected to other concerns.

items.name: Primitive Turmoils
items.desc: In our eagerness to link this species to our myths, our agents neglected safe pre-FTL contact protocol. Across the planet, locals have recorded multiple observations of our ships, have stolen equipment, and in one case, kidnapped one of our agents for study. Learning of our existence has caused unrest and polarized responses.\n\nDespite the operational chaos, excitement about the mythological connections persist among our own people. This species is being viewed through an increasingly spiritual lens across our empire.

items.name: Astounding Discovery
items.desc: Intensive study of the inhabitants of §Y[pre_ftl_planet.GetName]§! have cooled the mythological hypothesis. While many parallels are found between our oldest stories and these beings, some irreconcilable differences have also been uncovered.\n\nDespite this more complicated picture, enthusiasm for this species remains. It has been suggested that they may be a remnant population of the original beings in our stories, and that differences may be due to the vast spans of time elapsed since. While we are forced to recognize them as their own society today, many in our empire now feel a strong spiritual connection to them.

items.name: Boarding Party
items.desc: Our forces have seized control of the station. The inhabitants put up some resistance, but were poorly armed and seemingly untrained in warfare. Upon closer inspection, many appeared to be juveniles. Those who were not killed have been contained.\n\nAnalysis has begun on how we can control the subspace tunnels, which appear to be some sort of energy-mining siphon. With time, we can address the situation in our home system.

items.name: Aliens Terminated
items.desc:
The subspace mining station has been destroyed, killing everyone on board.

The destruction of the station detonated some unknown energy storage medium. The resulting energy rushed through the collapsing subspace tunnel into §Y[event_target:situation_red_giant_target_shortterm.GetStarName]§!, substantially worsening the situation back home.

That said, the transfer of hydrogen into our star has ceased. As bad as things may be, they will no longer worsen. While we may never know the origins or design of this station, we can at least rest easy knowing that such power will never fall to our rivals.

Unfortunately, we have no immediate way to return §Y[event_target:situation_red_giant_target_shortterm.GetStarName]§! to its original state. If we want to affect the star's state, we'll need to rely on our recordings to piece together what the station was doing.
items.trigger: exists = event_target:situation_red_giant_expansion@root

items.name: Station Destroyed
items.desc: As the station's remains drift through space, its destruction offers us a new chance to change the fate of §Y[event_target:situation_red_giant_target_shortterm.GetStarName]§!, not with the flip of a switch, but through hard, costly labor.

items.name: Alien Negotiations
items.desc:
After a lengthy and difficult process, we have a rudimentary translator that can communicate with station inhabitants.

The station has been operating for generations, moving from gas giant to gas giant, using the subspace siphon to extract energy from distant stars to power their life support and powerful jump drive.

The aliens do not fully understand the systems they are operating and did not realize that their siphoning targeted stars and eventually destroyed them.

Despite their confusion, they seem eager to leave the station. They have promised to teach us what they know in exchange for a safe place to live and raise their young.

items.name: Subspace Mining Operation
items.desc:
The station siphons hydrogen from a gas giant and channels it through subspace into our star's shell. The resulting helium fusion releases excess energy, which is converted into §YCrystallized Entropy§! to power the station.

The instability of §Y[event_target:situation_red_giant_target_shortterm.GetStarName]§! is a result of calibration errors and equipment degradation that the inhabitants either didn't notice or didn't know how to fix. 

Working with their ancient technology we can reverse the process, but it will not be easy. Alternatively, forcing our star to go nova could expose countless deposits transforming our heritage into a trove of exploitable resources.

items.name: Subspace Mining Operation
items.desc:
The station siphons hydrogen from a gas giant and channels it through subspace into our star's shell. The resulting helium fusion releases excess energy, which is converted into §YCrystallized Entropy§! to power the station.

The inhabitants of the station retain only a warped oral tradition about its operations. They lost contact with their home civilization thousands of years ago, perhaps because that civilization collapsed or was destroyed. A buildup of calibration errors and equipment degradation has led to the increasingly unstable siphoning that now threatens to destroy §Y[event_target:situation_red_giant_target_shortterm.GetStarName]§!.

Working with their ancient technology we can reverse the process, but it will not be easy. Alternatively, forcing our star to go nova could expose countless deposits, transforming our heritage into a trove of exploitable resources.

items.name: An End to the Threat
items.desc:
Upon learning of our plight, the station's inhabitants expressed alarm and dismay. They believed themselves alone, and were unaware of other species in the galaxy.

In a fit of remorse and before we truly grasped what they were doing, they began to dismantle the station, permanently destroying most of its components.

As a result, it will be difficult to control the star's expansion. And we must decide what to do with these volatile aliens, and whether to offer them the forgiveness they desire.

items.name: Prospect of Stability
items.desc:
After great effort, we now hold full control over the fate of §Y[event_target:situation_red_giant_target_shortterm.GetStarName]§!. Left alone, it would follow its natural life cycle at its current size.

But the ancient and failing station cannot withstand repeated reconfigurations. Each adjustment strains the facility to its limits. Now, we have only one choice.

We can shrink the star back to its former size, or force it to expand, transforming the system into a vast field of easily harvested resources.

Our [GetScientistPlural] will attempt one last reconfiguration. After that, the only way forward will be rapid disassembly, by external force.

items.name: Stability Achieved
items.desc: With complete control achieved over our star's fluctuating size and energy, §Y[Target.GetStarName]§! has fully stabilized. It will remain as it is now for millions of years, and our people can once again enjoy stability and predictability in our home system.\n\nOur star's increased size has clear consequences for how we manage our infrastructure, and we can now make the most of these changes, exploiting its increased energetic output while maintaining a viable presence in the system.

items.name: A Mysterious Station
items.desc:
Upon entering the system, our vessels encountered limited resistance from a group of automated drones. These were swiftly neutralized, allowing for a closer examination of the alien station.

The structure remains operational, though its hull bears the marks of extensive patchwork repairs. Attempting to access one of its docking bays, we made contact with a previously unknown alien species. Though linguistic barriers remain, we have confirmed that this installation is the origin of the tunnels affecting §Y[event_target:situation_red_giant_target_shortterm.GetStarName]§!.

Efforts are now underway to establish communications. A diplomatic resolution may be possible. Failing that, we may be forced to consider more direct methods, boarding the facility or destroying it outright. However, without a thorough understanding of its purpose, such actions may carry significant risk to our star.

items.name: A Spark Of Crisis
items.desc: Ongoing study of the subspace mining station suggests that it stores massive amounts of thermal energy in an exotic form, which our [GetScientistPlural] are calling §YCrystallized Entropy§!. It leverages thermal feedback loops to magnify energy inputs.\n\nBy replicating this technology, we could learn to wield previously unimaginable power that many would deem unnatural and dangerous. Doing so may produce vast amounts of excess heat, but if we are able to find a way to thrive in such conditions, the galaxy may be ours for the taking.
items.trigger: has_country_flag = red_giant_controlled_lusus_station

items.name: Forgotten Empire
items.desc: While the ruins on [From.Planet.GetName] first appeared to be built of stone, excavation and analysis suggests that many of the structures in this lost city are made of a petrified organic material comparable to wood. No source for such materials exists on the planet today. Smaller artifacts are built of crude metals, glass, and similar petrified organics, and [GetScientistPlural] have also found fossils of native creatures that no longer exist. \n\nIt appears the civilization in question inhabited the planet at a time when its climate was much more temperate. Did they disappear long before the planet turned to its current state, or did they witness the violent transition in their final years?

items.name: Witnesses of Demise
items.desc: Excavation of the ruined city on [From.Planet.GetName] has revealed places of cultural importance, decorated with intricate patterns that may be a written language. Most excitingly, the dig teams have found an underground chamber full of shelves, each containing thin sheets of bronze etched with densely-packed script. Despite the inefficiency of bronze as a storage medium, this appears to be a communal archive of texts. \n\nTranslation attempts have begun as the archaeological teams continue to spread out through the city. The question of the final fate of these people remains open.

items.name: Incoming Doom
items.desc:
The team on [From.Planet.GetName] has encountered a somber catacomb. It consists of a network of dugout trenches, with mummified alien remains resting in cavities in the walls, stacked three or four individuals high. Burial goods give us a glimpse of their technological development, such as primitive firearms, simple glass telescopes, and complex textile embroidery. 

Many junctions within the catacomb are guarded by statues of extinct local fauna. These creatures have a round, domed shell, four squat legs, and a small blunt head. In better-preserved specimens, they are depicted hunching down, using their shell to protect them from flame-like carvings in the material above them. 

The true meaning of this artwork may be lost to time, but it may depict this society's awareness of its impending, fiery doom. Further excavation of the ruins may clarify what they were experiencing.

items.name: Blazing Downfall
items.desc:
Extensive exploration of the ruined city on [From.Planet.GetName] proves that this civilization lived through the collapse of its ecosystem, and knew its final, fiery days were approaching. Paper-based records existed before hot volcanic ashfall forced them to switch to bronze tablets, and artistic depictions of animals hiding from flame record their attempts to reckon with their own end. 

The excavation also uncovered a nearly perfect specimen of the catacomb guardian statues. The flames carved above it have an internal glow, making this a striking piece worthy of preservation. 

We also found evidence of attempts to stop the volcanism. Roadways and broken carts demonstrate that the inhabitants transported rubble to the nearest volcanic caldera and dumped it in to try to plug the volcano. Unfortunately, they were unable to stop their fate. The planet is devoid of multicellular life today. 

This history reminds us of the precarity of any civilization, should it encounter a problem more powerful than the tools it has at its disposal.

items.name: Ancient Signs
items.desc:
The temple itself is scarred by signs of battle, and there are ancient remains of the local sentient species in the soil. It seems the temple was torched and abandoned. Security teams have noted that the locals avoid this entire area, believing it to be cursed. 

The fire temple's walls protected its contents, including many intricate frescos and carvings. These feature a recurring motif of a circle of twisted fire, with a dark gash down its center. In one depiction, a bipedal figure plucks out one of four such eyes and casts it upon the world, creating this central motif. We are designating it the Infernal Eye. 

Further excavations will reveal what beliefs surrounded this strange figure.

items.name: Ocular Offerings
items.desc:
Excavations of the temple of the Infernal Eye show evidence of many sacrifices. Large circular pits with platforms in the center, mimicking the Infernal Eye and its pupil, lie filled with layers of ash and charcoal. Molecular analysis reveals that the ash and charcoal comes from animal tissue. 

Whether these sacrifices were of wild or domestic animals, or indeed of the locals themselves, cannot be determined. 

Agents have been dispatched to current population centers in search of corollary evidence, while our excavators search for more answers.

items.name: Dark Practices
items.desc:
A heavy stone doorway was discovered blocking off the deepest part of the temple. After breaking through, excavators found a circular chamber with a central pit opening directly above a natural underground magma reservoir. The orange light of the magma bathed the walls in a red glow, faintly illuminating inscriptions encircling the strange room. The top of the surrounding walls are studded with bright, flaming eyes.

On one edge of this pit are the desiccated remains of one of the locals, broken open upon an altar shaped like the Infernal Eye. It appears they were in fact sacrificing their own in an attempt to appease it.

The text along these walls may be critical to understanding the cultural role of this temple, and should be translated immediately.

items.name: Convulsing Prophecies
items.desc:
The final study of the scripture in the temple's innermost chamber reveals a set of prophecies relating to the return of the Infernal Eye. It speaks of the Infernal Eye growing angry at the defiance of its subjects. In response, the Eye is expected to darken the skies, erupt a specific holy mountain, cause a specific crop to wither on the vine, and more. The prophecy presents this as the end of civilization, stating that after these events, only those who submit to the Infernal Eye shall survive. 

Our agents among the local populace have looked for cultural connections, and found that this prophetic text is the source of many aphorisms and phrases in the planet's cultures, as well as the source text for many later stories and myths. They also believe that the mysteries practiced by their modern temples include variations on, and reactions against, this ancient prophecy. 

All of these prophesied events could be re-enacted with our technology, or faked with a degree of realism they will not be able to detect. If we were to present ourselves as the Infernal Eye reincarnate, demonstrating that the original prophecy was right all along, we may be able to extract concessions and fealty from them. This would make them easier to absorb in the long term.

items.name: Molten Core
items.desc: As the colony on §Y[planet.GetName]§! grew, so too did evidence of an extinct civilization that made use of Living Metal, though there was no trace of where they acquired this material.\n\nAn answer has recently surfaced, in the form of a strange shimmering sphere encased in a force field which buoyed up from deep core magma flows. Its original purpose and construction are not immediately obvious, but it produces a steady drip of Living Metal when exposed to extremely high temperatures. While this handily solves that archaeological puzzle, we must now decide what to do with it.

items.name: A New Power
items.desc:
Our [GetScientistPlural] report a novel method for harvesting and storing entropy by binding it into a high-energy crystalline matrix. This §YCrystallized Entropy§! can store and transport substantial thermal energy, applicable across industrial, economic, and interstellar operations.

Modeling suggests that it might be used to terraform planets into hotter climates, or even in accelerating stellar evolution into red giants. In principle, stray entropy from across the galaxy could be reclaimed and converted into usable heat, driving compounding thermal expansion on a galactic scale.

§HIssues Special Project:§! §YNew Power Source§!

items.name: Crystallization Achieved
items.desc:
We have completed our first working infrastructure for harvesting energy and converting it into §YCrystallized Entropy§!. These crystals hold immense thermal energy and already enable our industry to store and transport power far more efficiently than conventional methods.

Red Giants, thanks to their vast emission surfaces and thermal output, are ideal for this process, and we're ready to deploy the technology in any system under our control.

Our technicians have also begun adapting the process for industrial use, experimenting with ways to synthesize Crystallized Entropy by harnessing ambient entropy. With this new economy igniting, wealth and power are sure to follow. Our [GetScientistPlural] are already researching how to scale production further.

§HUnlocks Megastructure:§! §YGalactic Crucible Frame§!

items.name: Thermophilic Evolution
items.desc: We embark on our path to set the galaxy aflame, but our own forms must be prepared to face the heat. Adapting our population to higher temperatures will help us thrive in our fiery new future.

items.name: Launching Conduits
items.desc:
The Galactic Crucible Chassis is now ready to deploy §YConduits§!: automated systems designed to channel and amplify stellar entropy. Once dispatched, they'll recycle and intensify a star's energy output, converting it into a Red Giant, heating entire systems to support our empire's expanding infrastructure.

These §YConduits§! can be produced at regular intervals and operate autonomously for our convenience. For now, they'll remain within our territory, but in time, it may serve us to let them spread across the galaxy. After all, our empire never stops growing.

§HMegastructure Upgrade Available:§! §YGalactic Crucible Core§!

items.name: How Hot Will It Get?
items.desc:
Our continued research into §YCrystallized Entropy§! has unveiled a chilling possibility: when highly concentrated, they can power weapons of unimaginable scale, capable of devastating entire planets. With such power, the galaxy could fall under our mercy.

But exploring these military applications would shatter what little trust remains between us and our neighbors. And who's to say such weapons couldn't one day be turned against us?

Empty words of peace will not suffice. If we wish to prove our intentions, we must publicly cripple the Galactic Crucible Core, ensuring it can never produce such weaponry. Otherwise, it's only a matter of time before this technology is weaponized, by us, or by someone else.

§HThis decision unlocks a Special Project§!

items.name: Into The Fire
items.desc:
Our investigation into §YCrystallized Entropy§! and the §YDesigned Firestorm Project§! has confirmed what we suspected: the potential for devastating weaponry is real. With such power in our hands, we no longer need to temper ourselves for the sake of diplomatic niceties.

The Galactic Crucible Hub's expansion will accelerate, with special focus on its more... aggressive applications. The sooner we unlock these weapons, the less the galaxy's opinions will matter.

§HMegastructure Upgrade Available:§! §YGalactic Crucible§!

items.name: A Steady Glow
items.desc:
The Galactic Crucible Hub has been successfully hobbled, ensuring it can no longer be expanded or repurposed for destructive ends. While the loss of its full potential is regrettable, continuing down that path would have risked catastrophe, and the collapse of all diplomatic ties.

Fortunately, even in its limited form, the Galactic Crucible Institute will remain a powerful source of energy and prosperity. We've stepped back before crossing a line, securing a future where we can collaborate with the galactic community while still benefiting from this remarkable science.

§HMegastructure Upgrade Available:§! §YGalactic Crucible Institute§!

items.name: Surrounding The Core
items.desc: Our ongoing research into §YConduits§! and transforming stars into Red Giants suggests we may be able to scale up our operations to overheat the Galactic Core itself, triggering a thermal cascade across the entire Galaxy, thus transforming it into a much more hospitable place for us.\n\nWe have identified six systems surrounding the core that could serve as operational hubs for this endeavor. These systems lie beyond the galactic hyperlane network, but efforts are underway to generate stable wormholes and establish access.

items.name: Race To Ignition
items.desc:
The Galactic Crucible is now fully armed and operational. With wormhole tunnels completed, we've secured access to all six staging systems around the Galactic Core.

Our work to overheat the Core can begin. Other empires may detect our activity and attempt to reach these systems, but for now, we hold the advantage, and the core bends to our will.

§HUse the wormhole to secure the Galactic Core systems§!

items.name: Galactic Fire Alarm
items.desc: Rival empires have forced open hyperlanes to our staging grounds near the galactic core. As we continue to superheat the core, we must prepare for resistance.\n\nBut we will not be stopped. The cold dark of space will be scoured away, replaced by the blazing glory of our ascendant future.

items.name: Upcoming Storm
items.desc:
The galactic core has begun to stir. Entropy levels around the supermassive black hole are spiking, casting waves of thermal radiation into nearby systems.

Just as panic sets in, a team of brave scientists, drawn from many worlds, has unveiled newly-formed hyperlanes connecting to six systems encircling the core. These systems, it seems, house facilities operated by §Y[hyperthermia_empire.GetName]§!, which are actively superheating the core. This reckless tampering threatens to ignite a cascading firestorm across the galaxy, incinerating all who fail to stop their pyromaniac ambitions.

If we wish to survive, we must breach these systems and wrest control from their grasp. The crisis is here - and the temperature is still rising.

items.name: Escalation: §RCrisis Declared§!
items.desc:
History's greatest transformations have always demanded sacrifice. Yet the Galactic Community views our work as a threat rather than a necessity. In response, a unified military coalition has mobilized against us.

With extermination their stated goal, we are left with no alternative: any approach toward the Galactic Core or the Galactic Crucible will be met with overwhelming force.

Our vision has ignited the stars themselves. Let those who oppose it contend with the storm we have summoned.

§HDefend the Galactic Core systems and our victory is assured!§!

items.name: Call to Arms: §RCrisis Declared§!
items.desc:
In light of escalating threats at the galactic core, the Galactic Community has enacted a unified response against §Y[hyperthermia_empire.GetName]§!, whose radical efforts to raise the galactic temperature endanger all known life.

Should these ambitions proceed unchecked, countless civilizations face extinction. The so-called §Y[hyperthermia_empire.GetName]§! now stands in direct opposition to a coalition united by necessity.

The battle has begun, and trillions of lives hang in the balance.

§HCapture the Galactic Core systems or all will be lost!§!

items.name: Race Against Time
items.desc:
A cascading firestorm impends. Soon, the galactic core will erupt, cleansing our enemies and cementing our dominion over the stars.

But the galaxy refuses to embrace our radiant future. Through the newly-forged hyperlanes, they plot to invade our staging grounds and undo everything we've built. For what? To preserve their cold, stagnant darkness?

We cannot allow them to interfere. We must hold the line at the core, until the firestorm ignites and reduces them to ash.

items.name: Galactic Crucible Captured
items.desc: With the capture of the §H[crucible_system.GetName]§! system, our forces have also taken control of the Galactic Crucible that was being built around the local star. \n\nThe loss of this megastructure shatters any remaining hope its creators had of taking over the galaxy by force.

items.name: Galactic Crucible Captured
items.desc: Capturing the §H[crucible_system.GetName]§! system unveiled the sinister plans of the §H[crucible_builders.GetName]§!, which included the complete annihilation of the entire galaxy by an unprecedented storm of fire. \n\nFor now, the machine that holds the potential to cause a mass extinction event has been put on hold. As soon as the war ends, we should use our remaining resources and strength to disable this giant megastructure once and for all.
items.trigger:
is_at_war = yes
exists = event_target:crucible_builders
is_at_war_with = event_target:crucible_builders

items.name: The galaxy is ours!
items.desc:
We have fanned the flames of victory from the galactic core to the outermost stars. The firestorm has reduced our enemies to ash. They lacked the vision, the courage, to embrace the glorious future we claimed. The galaxy is ours.

In this new order of fire and fury, planets boil with magma and light, set aglow by the swelling heat of red giants. Entropy surges through every system, ours to harvest and bend to our will. With each passing day, our empire grows richer, stronger... unstoppable.

We have consumed the galaxy and remade it as a blazing beacon of our dominion in the void. And one day, perhaps, we'll cast other galaxies onto the pyre.

items.name: Galactic Rebirth
items.desc: While we were busy igniting the spark that would set the galaxy ablaze, the §Y[hyperthermia_empire.GetName]§! had already transformed stars into weapons, reshaping the galaxy forever. \n\nFor now, we can embrace this newly forged utopia, but we should closely monitor their next moves as they tighten their grip on the galaxy.
