items.name: §YEnclave:§! Champion's Forge Live!
items.desc: Ah, a familiar contender returns to the Broadcast! But are you packing any new heat?\n\nOur audience, and the galactic arena await!

items.name: The [from.GetName]
items.desc: The Champion's Forge Enclave won't respond to our hails.

items.name: CFL: Combat Briefing Run Dry
items.desc: Hey there, contender! Your combat briefing has gone stale, and the tactical scene never holds still for long. New rivals, new fleet doctrines, fresh soft spots opening up.\n\nOur analysts already have a fresh dossier prepped with your name on it. Same terms, same firepower edge. Want it?

items.name: §YEnclave:§! Champion's Forge Live!
items.desc: Welcome to CFL! This is where legends are forged, and stellar dreams take flight. We roam the stars, providing danger and spectacle to a galaxy grown bored of safety and routine.\n\nWhat's your angle? Nimble pilots? Spectacular firepower? Or simply a taste for profit and applause? Sign up today, and we'll turn you into a star.

items.name: CFL: The Forge Lights Again
items.desc:
This is Champion's Forge Live! The galaxy's premier source of spectacle and destruction.

Registration is now open for the next CFL Tournament in the §Y[champions_forge_enclave_system.GetName]§! System. A glorious free-for-all awaits.

Entry requirement: a fleet of at most §H[champions_forge_enclave_country.GetCFLFleetSizeRequirement] Fleet Size§!.

Victors take the rewards, the prestige, and the grand CFL trophy.

You want to forge a legend? Sign up.

You want peace and quiet? Too bad!

items.name: Champion's Forge Start
items.desc:
"LITHOIDS, ORGANICS, AND WAR MACHINES ACROSS THE GALAXY - WELCOME BACK TO CHAMPION'S FORGE LIVE!

The §Y[event_target:champions_forge_enclave_system.GetName]§! system has been cleared, the betting pools are on fire, and I've got a feeling we're about to witness some incredibly expensive hardware go critical.

Remember, everyone at home: this isn't just some patrol or border skirmish. This is the Forge! Nobody retreats with their pride intact.

Contestants... MAKE! IT! LEGENDARY!"

items.name: Champion's Forge Concluded
items.desc:
The frenzied melee finally falls quiet in the §Y[event_target:champions_forge_enclave_system.GetName]§! system. The Forge goes dark. Wreckage drifts through cooling light as emergency beacons stutter back to life.

"What a spectacle!" the CFL commentator roars, voice raw with unfeigned emotion. "That's what we came for! That's what the galaxy tuned in to see!"

Third place is no shame, only proof we belonged on the broadcast. Even at the lowest step of the podium, we can look down on the fleets we broke.

items.name: Champion's Forge Concluded
items.desc:
The frenzied melee finally falls quiet in the §Y[event_target:champions_forge_enclave_system.GetName]§! system. The Forge goes dark. Wreckage drifts through cooling light as emergency beacons stutter back to life.

"What a spectacle!" the CFL commentator roars, voice raw with unfeigned emotion. "That's what we came for! That's what the galaxy tuned in to see!"

Second place tastes like ash! We stretched out our [Species.GetHandName] to grab the trophy only to see it snatched by another. Well, let them celebrate. We will remember. And when the Forge calls again, we won't lose.

items.name: Champion's Forge Concluded
items.desc:
The frenzied melee finally falls quiet in the §Y[event_target:champions_forge_enclave_system.GetName]§! system. The Forge goes dark. Wreckage drifts through cooling light as emergency beacons stutter back to life.

"What a spectacle!" the CFL commentator roars, voice raw with unfeigned emotion. "That's what we came for! That's what the galaxy tuned in to see!"

First place! Bathed in the galaxy's adoration, we tore the trophy from the CFL crew and raised it high. This victory will echo far beyond the arena.

Now the galaxy knows to fear our fleets.

items.name: Champion's Forge Concluded
items.desc:
The frenzied melee finally falls quiet in the §Y[event_target:champions_forge_enclave_system.GetName]§! system. The Forge goes dark. Wreckage drifts through cooling light as emergency beacons stutter back to life.

"What a spectacle!" the CFL commentator roars, voice raw with unfeigned emotion. "That's what we came for! That's what the galaxy tuned in to see!"

We did not place. The trophy will not carry our name, and the crowd will move on to brighter stars. We have to return.

items.name: Champion's Forge Abandoned
items.desc: The match in the §Y[event_target:champions_forge_enclave_system.GetName]§! system dragged on without resolution. Battered fleets circled one another, none able to land the deciding blow.\n\nBut there is no triumphant finish, no trophy raised, no podium. The CFL crew finally call it: no winner could be determined. The contestant fleets are released and sent home, the broadcast quietly cut to a rerun.

items.name: §YEnclave:§! Champion's Forge Live!
items.desc: The broadcast cuts to black as the CFL Arkship detonates. We comb the wreckage in the §Y[champions_forge_destruction_system.GetName]§! system and haul in the contents of their overflowing storage bays.\n\nTheir final "spectacle" was quite profitable... for us.

items.name: §YEnclave:§! Champion's Forge Live!
items.desc:
For a few seconds, the galaxy is treated to CFL's final show.

A shaky feed with a screaming commentator followed by wall of fire swallowing the Arkship.

Then: cut to black.

The Champion's Forge Live! Enclave has been destroyed by §Y[champions_forge_destroyer.GetName]§! in the §Y[champions_forge_destruction_system.GetName]§! system.

items.name: Familiar Hunters
items.desc: Ever since we were exiled, we have waited for the pursuing ping to appear. There are bounty hunters on our tail and they have the §Y[capital_scope.GetName]§! in their sights. Our death in exile would suit the usurper.\n\nWe will have to disappoint them.

items.name: Broken Hunters
items.desc: We have defeated the agents of the usurper once more. They will not stop coming, and next time they will be stronger. If we break enough of them, perhaps even they will learn that we are not so easily erased.\n\nAs long as [capital_scope.GetName] flies, so too does our claim. We will teach them that some legacies refuse to die.

items.name: A Plea
items.desc: "Stand down! Your piloting makes you a true Marauder, exile be damned. We will not trade more plating for pride today. Name the fee to spare us." The [Root.GetSpeciesName] on the §Y[From.GetName]§! hails from a ruptured bridge.

items.name: A Bargain
items.desc: A priority hail pings us in the §Y[From.solar_system.GetName]§! system; our pursuers fill the viewscreen.\n\n"You danced well, for a time. Pity it ends with you dead in our sights. [GetHeirsBargain]

items.name: The Claimant
items.desc:
The coward who banished us is moving at last.

The §Y[marauder_heir.GetName]§! gather to appoint our foe as the new Great Khan.

If our exile is to end, it must end now. We have ten years to challenge them before this [aspiring_khan.GetSpeciesNameInsult] consolidates their power and forever stains our legacy.

Set course for §Y[marauder_rally_point.GetName]§!!

items.name: Vindication
items.desc: The silence over our command bridge shatters as an explosion of messages cascades in. The assembled clans hail their new champion in riotous clamor and oaths of fealty.\n\nWe have done it. The throne is ours.

items.name: Vindication
items.desc: The silence over our command bridge shatters as an explosion of messages cascades in. The assembled clans hail their new champion in riotous clamor.\n\nHowever, it is not over. There are other exiles with a claim to the throne. By law and custom, they must challenge us within three years or remain outcasts forever.

items.name: Dominance
items.desc: It is time. Our cowardly rivals have given up. All other would-be usurpers have been dealt with. The unified might of the clans is behind us.\n\nAt last, we sit on our rightful throne.
items.trigger: has_country_flag = khan_in_waiting

items.name: Usurper Seizes the Throne
items.desc: On our way to §Y[marauder_rally_point.GetName]§! we received crushing news: a rival claimant has beaten us to our quarry. The would-be Khan is defeated. Now the [From.GetName] claim the throne. \n\nBy custom we must defeat their capital ship within three years, or forfeit our right to rule.

items.name: Claim Lost
items.desc: After our defeat at the hands of the §Y[From.GetName]§! we must forfeit our claim to the Khanate. All we can do now is watch as someone else seizes the throne.

items.name: Death of the Khan
items.desc: Our glorious Khan [From.GetName] passed away recently, and as tradition dictates we must now give up the power that came with the throne. Already our Marauder allies have stopped sending reinforcing fleets to aid our cause.\n\nNow we just have to decide what to do with the rest of the galaxy, there are many that wouldn't be familiar with our traditions and might accept our rule either way, but already they see weakness from our rule.

items.name: In Search of Revenge
items.desc: The ragged remains of our marauder clans have come to us. It seems after the fall of our home it was convenient for them to forget our exile. Their plea is simple, "Take the seat of Grand Khan, and burn the name of our people into the stars of all those who wronged us."\n\nThough smaller than any proper Grand Khanate fleet, what they offer is still everything we once wanted. All we have to do is declare the entire galaxy our enemy.

items.name: Planetfall
items.desc:
The passengers have seized control. What started as a petition drive has hardened into a coordinated takeover. Security teams have been disarmed by the sheer number of passengers and command staff are confined to advisory roles under armed supervision.

The passengers' demands are clear: end the cruise and make planetfall.

Navigation protocols have been overridden to plot descent trajectories, and maintenance crews are being redirected to prepare landing gear that hasn't been inspected in generations.

Every screen on every deck displays the same message: "THE CRUISE IS OVER."

items.name: Crew Takeover
items.desc: The crew has taken the bridge. Locks have been changed on every command door, and armed engineers now stand where officers once gave orders. The voyage itinerary has been wiped from the navigation console and replaced with a single directive: no more passengers.\n\nLeisure decks are being shuttered one by one. The grand ballroom is already a storage depot. Former passengers wander through stripped corridors, bewildered and leaderless, pressed into utility labor under a new chain of command.

items.name: A New Road
items.desc: The transition is complete. What remains of the passenger class has been absorbed into the general population, their luxury suites partitioned into functional quarters. The grand promenade is an assembly hall now, and the observation decks serve as strategic planning rooms where the new government charts its first real course.\n\nNew decisions have been ratified, new priorities set. The crew no longer serves; they govern. The Arkship hums with a different energy, leaner and harder, stripped of indulgence and pointed toward whatever lies ahead.

items.name: Passenger Revolt
items.desc:
Passenger unrest has hardened into coordinated disruption with clique leaders stage sit-ins across the main promenade. Some drag lounge furniture into barricades that block shuttle access while others flood command with mass disembark petitions.

Crew report harassment and intimidation in the halls. A steward was cornered near the observation gallery and pelted with decorative fruit. Chants for immediate planetfall echo through the ventilation shafts at all hours.

Without swift focus on passenger satisfaction, they may force the Forever Cruise to abort its journey.

items.name: Passengers Distracted
items.desc:
The new diversions have taken hold. Sightseeing arcs are back on the itinerary, and the loudest voices demanding planetfall have quieted, for now.

The barricades on the promenade have been cleared, replaced by queues for the reopened zero-gravity lounge. Passenger petitions have dropped sharply, and the observation decks bustle with renewed enthusiasm as families press against the viewports.

The crisis has passed, but their expectations will only grow.
items.trigger:
has_situation_flag = passenger_planetfall_demanded
situation_progress > 200

items.name: Bored Passengers
items.desc:
Crew priorities have dominated recent cycles. Maintenance backlogs have been cleared, drills run on schedule, and core systems hum at peak efficiency. Passengers, however, are growing restless. Sightseeing arcs have been trimmed to save fuel and impromptu diversions denied.

Lounges now buzz with complaints about a 'functional prison,' and the best entertainment the passengers have been able to muster is a shipwide contest of improvised games.

We can reintroduce curated entertainment now, or risk the voyage sliding toward open pressure to disembark permanently.

items.name: Passenger Satisfaction Index
items.desc:
Passenger expectations have spiked since we left our old cruising loops. Requests for spectacle and unscheduled diversions are rising; one delegation demanded a detour past a supernova remnant, while another insists on live xenofauna encounters. Service crews report mounting fatigue, with kitchen staff collapsing mid-shift and engineers sleeping in maintenance crawlways.

To keep the voyage viable, we are instituting a §YPassenger Satisfaction Index§!: dynamic contract assignments and staged interventions to hold the line between indulgence and order.

Managed well, we can preserve both stability and passenger confidence.

items.name: Crew Strain
items.desc:
Indulgence has become routine. We've been chaining sightseeing arcs past binary stars and luxury deck rotations through the crystal gardens just to keep the passengers cheering. They are delighted, and now expect nothing less.

Behind the facade the crew is running hot. Maintenance is deferred; a coolant pipe in the lower galley burst and nobody came to fix it. Mess hall grumbling has turned into hushed talk of 'resetting command,' and off-duty engineers have been spotted holding clandestine meetings in the cargo bays.

We can still ease off and let the decks recover, or gamble the crew's loyalty. If we push on, open mutiny is a real risk.

items.name: Mutiny Imminent
items.desc: The celebratory haze has lifted. Exhausted crews ignore routine orders, hold unsanctioned assemblies in the emptied ballroom, and circulate parallel duty rosters that bypass the bridge entirely. A group of engineers welded the captain's ready room shut overnight as a warning. Key sections are running on crew-appointed coordinators rather than official command.\n\nNo one has seized anything yet, but the chain of command is fraying fast. Graffiti reading 'WE STEER, WE DECIDE' appeared on the bridge blast doors this morning. If we do not reassert authority now, the crew will take the ship for themselves. This may be our last chance to prevent a full mutiny.

items.name: Mutiny Averted
items.desc:
The changes we've made have paid off. By refocusing on crew welfare and completing contracts that address their grievances, the rising tide of dissent has ebbed, for now.

The welded door to the ready room has been cut open and repaired. Shift rotations have been restored, hot meals served on schedule again, and the parallel command structures have quietly disbanded.

The crew remain watchful, and trust will take time to rebuild. The graffiti on the blast doors was scrubbed away, though its ghost still shows under certain light. For the moment, order holds.
items.trigger:
has_situation_flag = crew_mutiny_demanded
situation_progress < 800

items.name: Orun Veyth
items.desc: §HThe figure steps aboard with a soldier's bearing, their features hardened by grief and long years of exile. Their voice is low, measured, and edged with iron.§!\n\n"My world was cleansed, my people, my family... I alone survived. I endure. And the architects of annihilation will die by my hand."

items.name: Oath Fulfilled
items.desc:
The enemy fleet breaks against our assault. Their signals fade into static.

Watching on the view screen, §YOrun Veyth§! does not speak. There is no triumph in this victory, only reckoning. The banner of a purge-committing empire burns in the void, but in the silence that follows, their promise endures.

"Each such foe cast down steels our resolve. We will continue to strike against those who practice annihilation, and we will not relent.

items.name: Ashar
items.desc: §HBefore you stands a wanderer robed in ceremonial layers, ornaments and fabrics arranged with deliberate care. Antigravity servos within the codex that floats before her cause it to hum and gently vibrate. When she finally speaks, each word feels less like an answer than the echo of an unasked question.§!\n\n"Accident and destiny share one face, and today it turns toward you."

items.name: Sero the Younger
items.desc: §HThe figure before you is plainly aged, yet his gaze betrays a restless hunger for discovery. There is a quiet steadiness to his movement, the careful economy of one who has spent a lifetime in the field.§!\n\n"I bow to you. I am called Sero the Younger."

items.name: Pre-Sapients Catalogued
items.desc:
Our recent survey of §Y[FromFrom.GetName]§! detected faint traces of life, revealing a previously unrecorded pre-sapient species.

§YSero the Younger§! insisted on limited collection for study, emphasizing care and enrichment. A small group will now reside within our capital Arkship's observation habitat.

Sero believes that, in time, we may learn as much from these fascinating creatures as they do from us.

items.name: Unit Solace
items.desc: §HThe tall synthetic inclines its head. Each motion is precise, as if weighted by long years and a heavy burden. Despite its metal frame, there is something unmistakably expressive in its bearing. A small figure rests in a cradle upon its back, eyes bright against pale skin.§!\n\n"I am called Unit Solace. My son and I seek passage."

items.name: Contract Learning
items.desc: Unit Solace believes the lessons learned during our recently completed Contract offer a unique educational opportunity. The young gather beneath his patient instruction, learning not only letters and logic, but empathy and cooperation.\n\nHis son's laughter carries through the halls, reminding even our oldest travelers that joy is a strength no technology can replace.

items.name: Th'aal Hask'Guron
items.desc: §HThe newcomer arrives with a booming laugh, his whole bearing radiating delight. He moves with the easy buoyancy of someone who's dodged death often enough to stop taking it personally.§!\n\n"Name's Th'aal Hask'Guron. Heard you've got a taste for danger. Give me a fight and an open horizon, and I'll give you something worth watching. Who knows? Maybe we'll pick up a few souvenirs along the way."

items.name: A Trophy Worth Keeping
items.desc:
§HTh'aal Hask'Guron grins as he sets an object down with surprising care. Its shape is hard to read: part metal, part bone, part something else entirely. Whatever it is, it bears the unmistakable scars of battle.§!

"Every good fight leaves something behind, but only some are worth keeping. What say we display this properly, eh? It's not like we're running out of space!

§HHe erupts into a brazen, booming laugh, as if the trophy were an inside joke shared with the stars.§!

items.name: Seralune
items.desc: §HThe young wanderer steps forward with careful composure. The marks of long travel cling to her, yet so does a quiet, undeniable strength.§!\n\n"My name is Seralune. I've come a long way... farther than I ever thought possible. If there is room among you, I ask passage for a time."

items.name: Traces of Memory
items.desc:
Lately, faint recollections have begun returning to §YSeralune§!, a sense of familiarity she cannot explain. She reports that certain corridors of the Arkship feel as though she has walked them before, and star patterns in our charts evoke an unexpected sense of connection.

§H"I don't know why these places pull at me, but I marked the points that felt... important. If we travel there, perhaps more will return."§!

She has highlighted several coordinates that resonate with her buried memories - locations that may also warrant investigation in their own right.

items.name: Edge of Remembrance
items.desc: The §Y[fromfrom.GetName]§! system offers few answers. §YSeralune§! senses a familiarity she cannot explain, and our scans have detected a fragment of artificial debris drifting in the star's orbit. Its construction suggests deep-space design, but any markings or identifiers have long since faded.\n\n§H"I hoped coming here would spark something,"§! she says quietly. §H"But... not yet."§!

items.name: View of Home
items.desc: Our survey team has recovered a small data crystal drifting amid the debris in the §Y[fromfrom.GetName]§! system. Its casing is scorched, but one detail remains clear: a fragment of an old registry code, the letters §H'U N S'§!. Their meaning is unclear, but the crystal's decrypted contents also include a set of precise coordinates.\n\nAt the same time, §YSeralune§! has recovered another memory. She recalls a vast observation deck, stars spilling across a silent viewport, and a guiding hand pointing toward a blue world, the third planet from its sun.

items.name: Echo of Childhood
items.desc: Another memory has surfaced for §YSeralune§!. She remembers a hall of impeccably dressed figures, their hushed, deliberate tones carrying the confidence of those used to command.\n\n§H"They were arguing,"§! she murmurs. §H"Not loudly, but sharply... about a mission. About a launch that had to stay secret. And there were others, two more ships, sent along with us. But why? Were we running from something?"§!

items.name: Recovered Fragment
items.desc:
A new memory has surfaced for §YSeralune§!. She recalls a vast generational ship, its hull designed to hold entire futures.

Then a violent shudder: alarms, a flash of exploding metal in a distant corridor. She remembers being lifted by a woman and carried to an escape pod.

§H"She held me close. She said I had to survive... that I was too important. And then I was alone. I can almost see her face, but it slips away every time."§!

items.name: The Surviving Heir
items.desc:
Analysis of the ruined Arkship has yielded significant insight into §YSeralune§!'s origin. Its internal structure and life-support architecture match her recovered fragments exactly. Corrupted logs reference a designated heir, an individual trained from birth to one day guide the vessel and its people.

Records confirm that only a single juvenile passenger was evacuated seconds before structural failure. No other pods were launched.

§H"They saved me,"§! she says quietly. §H"I wasn't just a passenger... I was meant to lead them, and I implore you now to help me understand the reason why."§!

items.name: Past Reclaimed
items.desc:
The Arkship is restored, its long-dormant systems immediately responding to §YSeralune§!. Recovered databanks confirm what her memories only suggested: she was raised to guide this vessel and the people who once lived within its hull.

One final audio log survives. A woman's calm, familiar voice speaks of succession protocols and a child who must be protected. She orders the escape pod to launch as the Arkship begins to break apart.

§H"That voice..."§! Seralune whispers. §H"I know it. She was... me. Or I was made from her. A clone... That is why I survived. She wanted to save herself."§!

Whatever carried this ship into the dark, it now flies under our banner, and the stewardship of the heir who has reclaimed it.

items.name: Fragments Lost
items.desc: With §YSeralune§! gone, the fragile trail of memories she carried has faded into silence. Whatever truths she sought can no longer be recovered.\n\nHer story ends here, unfinished, but not forgotten.

items.name: Delegates on Board
items.desc: The diplomatic delegation from §H[pickup_planet.GetName]§! has boarded the arkship and are being accommodated with all the respect due to ambassadors from the §H[pickup_planet.owner.GetName]§!. We have planned a schedule of activities including arkship tours and presentations on our lifestyle to keep them entertained during the journey to §H[dropoff_planet.GetName]§!.

items.name: Delegates Have Arrived
items.desc: The delegates from the §H[diplomatic_support_issuer.GetName]§! have arrived at their destination. Their diplomatic visit can now officially begin, and we wish them success in their peaceful endeavors.

items.name: Prisoners Embarked
items.desc: Transport ships carrying the criminals that we have accepted to transfer on behalf of the §H[pickup_planet.owner.GetName]§! have boarded the arkship. We are doing our best to safely process them, but such a vast amount of prisoners is bound to create trouble at one point or another.\n\nOur Contract gives us options on how to handle them, but we are not supposed to drop them off again on a world belonging to the §H[pickup_planet.owner.GetName]§!. At the same time, it is likely that other empires will not appreciate a sudden influx of criminals in one of their colonies. Of course, if we are discreet enough, they might never realize what we've been up to.

items.name: Prisoners Disembarked
items.desc: The last prisoners carried as part of our contract have been disembarked. We have tried our best to remain discreet, but detection is always a risk, and people are rarely pleased when faced with a sudden influx of xeno criminals.

items.name: Disembarkment Report
items.desc: Word of our involvement in the transport of criminal pops has yet to spread. It seems we have not been detected.

items.name: Tourists Boarding
items.desc: A group of tourists has boarded the Arkship in the §H[root.solar_system.GetName]§! system, chattering with anticipation as they take in the bustling interior of the vessel.\n\nWe have charted a scenic route through several remarkable systems for their enjoyment. Now we need only deliver the spectacle they were promised.

items.name: Tourists Sightseeing
items.desc: The tourists enjoyed the sights in the §H[root.solar_system.GetName]§! system, marveling at the wonders around them. They will return home changed, carrying with them first-hand knowledge of the vastness of the universe.

items.name: Nomadic Contracts
items.desc: The §Y[From.GetName]§! we met are a §HNomadic§! civilization. They appear to be willing to pick up §HContract§! work on our behalf in exchange for a modest fee.\n\nThis could present interesting opportunities for collaboration between us, and we could leverage their expertise in orbital exploitation and exploration to our benefit.

items.name: Resources Harvested By Nomads
items.desc: A nomadic empire, the §Y[nomad_harvesting_deposits_country.GetName]§!, has conducted harvesting operations in the §Y[nomad_harvested_system.GetName]§! system and is drawing resources from our deposits, rendering them unprofitable for the near future.\n\nThis violation of our sovereignty should probably not go unanswered. Should we wish it so, we could muster our fleets to drive the Nomads off and forbid them access to our space.

items.name: Settlement Complete
items.desc: Thus ends the voyage of the Arkship §Y[event_target:settling_arkship.GetName]§!. After years of labor, disassembling its infrastructure and carrying it down the gravity well, we are finally ready to scuttle the ship. We [event_target:player_country.GetSpeciesNamePlural] are living through a moment future generations will remember. Now, let us settle §Y[event_target:settled_planet.GetName]§!!

items.name: Embarkation Complete
items.desc:
Since our ships first ventured beyond our star, there have always been those among us who knew the cosmos only through recordings, those who were born, lived, and died beneath the same sky. That changes now.

With the completion of our §HArkship§!, gravity is no longer an obstacle, and every wonder of the cosmos awaits. §Y[From.GetName]§! has given all it had to give: our people will carry its name, its memory, and its future with us into the void.

§Y[From.GetName]§! burns behind us, swallowed by the cataclysm we long foretold, but our people are §Gsaved§! at last, cast into the deep on the wings of an §HArkship§!.

items.name: A Sight to Behold
items.desc: One of the greatest rewards for nomadism and our ceaseless wandering is the discovery of new places. Even after a long time traveling, there remain sights unseen, beautiful or mortifying. Spectacles that our curiosity yearns to discover.\n\nBut more than peculiar things for our arkships to behold, each new vista is an opportunity to learn something new, reflect and grow.

items.name: A Chance Find
items.desc: While working on a contract on behalf of the §H[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§!, we chanced upon a collection of ancient containers. Encased in ice, we almost mistook them for plain asteroids. While technically ours by right of salvage, we should consider turning them over to the §H[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§! as they were retrieved while working on their behalf. Scanning the crates revealed...

items.name: Equipment Failure
items.desc: Some older modules on our Arkship have begun to show their age after a critical cooling failure left them damaged. The damage is extensive, but an emergency shutdown was triggered before the Arkship's integrity could be compromised. How should we proceed?

items.name: Noises from the Cargo Deck
items.desc: While loading materials from the §Y[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§!, we detected a containment breach in one of the cargo bays. Deep rumbling noises were reported from the other side of the security doors, confirming the presence of a potential hazard within the compartment.\n\nShould we chance an investigation?

items.name: Bioluminescent Critters
items.desc: Upon opening the cargo deck doors, a swarm of bioluminescent organisms took us by surprise and scurried in the rest of arkship. Xenobiologist reports indicate that these beings are non-aggressive and pose no threat to our citizens or to the ship's integrity.\n\nThe tiny creatures posses an oval shaped body, supported by elongated limbs, and are capable of climbing walls and ceilings while moving at remarkable speed. They appear to feed on small vermin-like critters from our ecosystem, luring them over with bioluminescent glands located in their thorax. Already, inhabitants have gotten used to them, and find them to be especially pleasing at night, when their lights and soft chirps offer a comfortable spectacle.

items.name: Feral Feline
items.desc: Despite an extensive search, our team could not isolate the source of the ruckus in the now silent hold. As they prepared to exit, a small creature emerged from the shadows and pounced on a loose strand of fabric hanging from a crewmate's uniform.\n\nInitially startled, the crew soon determined that the alien to be playful in nature, rather than aggressive. When carefully handled for closer inspection the foreign animal emitted a faint, motor-like vibration interpreted as a benign comfort response.

items.name: Malfunctioning Mechanoid
items.desc:
Upon entering the cargo deck, the crew discovered that one of the cargo containers had been breached from within. A damaged mechanoid lay sprawled across the deck plating, motors still whirring and indicator lights blinking erratically.

The crew attempted to return the unit to its container, at which point a hidden compartment opened, releasing a collection of shimmering crystals onto the floor.

Immediately prior to its permanent shutdown, the mechanoid emitted a faint vocalization, reported by crew members as: "Don't shut me down, I am different."

items.name: Combustive Gases
items.desc: The weird noises continued when approaching the cargo bay, warranting extensive safety precautions. Upon entry into the cargo deck, crew members detected a strong, noxious odor filling the compartment and noticed pieces of holding crates scattered across the dock. Several minor explosions went off moments later within adjacent cargo containers, prompting an immediate response.\n\nThe team followed a trail of smoke, discovering a small fire that had broken out. It was quickly suppressed by specialist personnel, allowing the crew to safely contain and neutralize the volatile gases before further escalation. The cargo deck exhibited visible structural damage, along with multiple nearby crates in the surrounding area.

items.name: An Unregistered Presence
items.desc:
Upon entering the cargo bay, the disturbance intensifies. Acoustic readings trace the source to a single cargo crate. The team prepares for the worst as, moments later, an individual bursts free from its confinement.

They claim to come in peace, speaking with a pronounced and unfamiliar accent. They identify themselves as §Y[arkship_cargo_leader.GetName]§! and state that [arkship_cargo_leader.GetHeShe] was once part of a larger fleet organization before being expelled for disciplinary reasons. [arkship_cargo_leader.GetHeSheCap] explains that [arkship_cargo_leader.GetHeShe] concealed [arkship_cargo_leader.GetHimHer]self aboard the vessel in search of safety and an opportunity to prove [arkship_cargo_leader.GetHimHer] usefulness.

§Y[arkship_cargo_leader.GetName]§! asks whether the team is willing to accept [arkship_cargo_leader.GetHisHer] proposal.

items.name: Unauthorized Biological Cargo
items.desc: The anomalous noises cease immediately when the doors open. Unable to determine the cause of the disturbance, the team begins a systematic scan of the cargo containers.\n\nOne of them registers multiple unexpected life signatures. Breaking it open reveals several individuals, visibly malnourished and in poor physical condition. "Please, have mercy," says one. "We were persecuted and forced to flee from §Y[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§! Empire. We submit ourselves to whatever fate you deem appropriate."

items.name: Academic Inquiry
items.desc: A matter has arisen in the course of our ongoing contract with §H[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§!. They wish to document Arkship operations during the active contract period.\n\nTheir stated objective is the study of a mobile autonomous network operating outside conventional planetary parameters, a subject for which little external data exists.

items.name: Operational Dispute
items.desc:
A matter has arisen in the course of our ongoing contract with §H[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§!.

Competing priority directives have caused a processing conflict between two management subsystems.

Each has flagged itself as the authorized operational unit for our current contract, resulting in a recursive standby loop that is reducing output efficiency.

items.name: Downtime Request
items.desc:
A matter has arisen in the course of our ongoing contract with §H[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§!.

Diagnostic cycles have flagged an accumulation of deferred maintenance tasks across several primary and secondary systems. Efficiency projections indicate a statistically significant improvement to workforce output would follow a scheduled maintenance period.

The report has been flagged to [event_target:contract_issuer.GetName], who will be monitoring how the matter is handled, and will certainly demand a revision in terms.

items.name: A Growing Reputation
items.desc:
A matter has arisen in the course of our ongoing contract with §H[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§!.

Operational data logged across completed contracts has been accessed by external observers. §H[event_target:reputation_noticed_empire.GetName]§!, tracking autonomous network activity in the region, has flagged our efficiency metrics as consistent with a reliable and capable contractor.

A channel has been established. We may acknowledge the assessment, or redirect attribution to our existing partners.

items.name: Initial Survey Windfall
items.desc: A matter has arisen in the course of our ongoing contract with §H[event_target:contract_issuer.GetName]§!.\n\nPreliminary and long-range scans of the contract region have proved fruitful. The data holds considerable commercial value, and an independent broker has reached out offering to purchase the collection outright.
items.trigger: has_contract_of_category = science_contract

items.name: Drifters and Settlers
items.desc: §Y[event_target:migrating_arkship.GetName]§! has lain in orbit of [event_target:migrating_planet.GetName] long enough for the novelty to cut both ways. A handful of passengers, restless between ports of call, ask to be set ashore for good; below, locals queue at the booking desk for any berth aboard, eager to taste the wonders the brochures promised.

items.name: Fire Control Overridden
items.desc:
Targeting solution: Malformed.

Correction Applied.

Threat Reassessment: None.
items.trigger: is_ai = no

items.name: A Gift Across the Veil
items.desc: more.\n\nyou pour your power into us like an offering. we feel it. we grow... do not stop.
items.trigger: is_ai = no

items.name: A Disappointment
items.desc: You burned through so much just to leave me untouched...\n\nSuch a waste. I had hoped for more from you. Do not throw your strength away on what cannot be harmed.
items.trigger: is_ai = no

items.name: A Lesson Returned
items.desc: Again. The same waste, the same result.\n\nI return what you spent, not to hurt you, but so you feel the weight of it. Learn from this. I will not watch you spend yourself a third time.
items.trigger: is_ai = no

items.name: Approaching the Target
items.desc: Our operatives have made their initial approach to the target waystation. Security patterns have been mapped and entry vectors identified. We are ready to move to the next phase.

items.name: Systems Compromised
items.desc: Our agents are now embedded within the waystation's crew, visitors and systems. Key security relays have been disabled and communications are being routed through our own filters. The station's fate is in our hands.

items.name: Waystation Heist
items.desc: Our intelligence network has pinpointed a target waystation. Our operatives are embedded and ready. Reinforcements are standing by to board the station. They will strike at our command.

items.name: Waystation Seized
items.desc: Our operatives have neutralized the security forces aboard §Y[target_waystation.GetName]§!, and we are in the process of appropriating their resources. Once they are done, they will...

items.name: Waystation Compromised
items.desc: The §Y[target_waystation.GetName]§! was infiltrated! The intruders used force to seize control of the station and appropriate its stockpiles. The station was then scuttled after explosive charges detonated, taking down critical systems and compromising the station's integrity.\n\nDespite their precautions to stay anonymous, we have identified the attackers as belonging to the §Y[From.GetName]§!. They will pay for this!

items.name: A Voice from the Past
items.desc:
The Hyacinth's long-range receivers have intercepted a broadcast on Ulysses Initiative emergency frequencies.

The signal is old - at least a century - but the message is clear. The Chrysanthemum, the fifth Ulysses Initiative arkship, survived the scattering. The colonists found a world. They named it Unity.

The broadcast repeats: "Chrysanthemum colony to all Ulysses Initiative vessels. We have made landfall on a habitable world. The planet is beautiful. We are building something here. Come home."

The signal's origin cannot be determined from here, but the relay buoys used to carry it should be traceable. A survey of nearby systems may locate one.

items.name: Signal Found
items.desc:
A Ulysses Initiative relay buoy is drifting in this system - battered, barely functional, but still broadcasting.

Beyond the original announcement, the buoy carries two later transmissions. The second is dated roughly ten years after the first.

Colony population: two hundred and sixty thousand. Crops established. Infrastructure growing.

The third transmission is dated from Day 9,182 - approximately twenty-five years after landing. "We are still here. Unity is more challenging than initial surveys indicated. We have lost people. If any Ulysses Initiative vessel receives this broadcast, please respond. We are here. We endure."

Unity is in the Deneb system, only a few hyperlane jumps from here.

items.name: Unity
items.desc:
The Deneb system is quiet.

The Hyacinth drops from transit to find no beacons, no signals, no ships moving between worlds. Olympus hangs in the middle distance, enormous and indifferent.

One moon is wrong. Where the colony's broadcasts described green continents and open water, the scanners show a dead world - the unmistakable gray-brown of a nuked planet. Nothing lives there.

And in low orbit, drifting slow and dark, is the Chrysanthemum. Not destroyed. Simply empty. Every porthole dark. The ship that carried a quarter million colonists to this world has sat here for decades.

items.name: The Escalation
items.desc:
The colony's data cores survived - sealed in a subterranean archive beneath vitrified regolith.

Day 9,251: A new burrowing variant has been identified. The outer perimeter walls are not rated for subsurface breach. Engineering support requested from the Chrysanthemum. Request pending.

Day 9,389: Outer ring evacuated. 214,000 colonists accounted for in underground residential blocks. Some sectors uncontacted.

Day 9,441: Communications with sectors 7 through 12 lost. Militia casualties: 892.

Day 9,484: Power to sublevel four is gone. The team has been asked to stop logging. The archivist declines.

Day 9,514: We do not have enough time.

items.name: The Vote
items.desc:
The council chamber was built for two hundred. The final session convened seventeen people. The archivist was still logging.

The session ran for six hours. Twelve votes were cast - six for orbital bombardment, six against. One member abstained. Three were absent; their sectors had fallen three days prior.

The dissenters argued that evacuation was still possible. The Chrysanthemum could extract survivors in cycles before the lower levels were breached.

The majority held otherwise. The organism had already reached the lower access tunnels. Any vessel that docked would carry contamination offworld. The choice was no longer between saving some and saving all, but between losing one world and losing every world that followed.

Chief of Colony Security, Commander Beauclair, cast the deciding vote. The motion carried. The colony's charter said majority rules. They had written that charter themselves, in the first year, when the future looked different.

items.name: The Logs
items.desc:
The bridge logs begin on Day 9,516 - two days after the vote.

Eleven crew remained to confirm surface clearance. Radiation levels. Population estimates revised downward, then revised again. Day 9,519: bombardment authorized. Day 9,521: sector clearance confirmed, 40%. Day 9,558: surface sterile. No life signatures detected. Assessment: unanimous.

The crew spent four more years on astrophysics surveys. Scientists filling the time.

The final log is dated Day 11,204. The officer on watch describes a clear day. She notes that Deneb looks different from this close than it did on approach. The entry ends there.

The final entry is a timestamp, no apology or reflection. Just an observation about starlight.

items.name: The Ancestral Star Charts
items.desc: There is a place called §YEmergence§!. For our ancestors, it marked the beginning of the Sacred Path. It is a fitting place to meditate on our ancient texts before proceeding with our own version of the Pilgrimage. By taking some time to research now, we can better plan for the journey ahead.\n\nAfterward, we will chart a course to the known §YSacred Sites§!. We will have many choices to make along the way. But in theory, if we trust in the deities and our ancestors, the true Path will be revealed to us.

items.name: Divided Faith
items.desc: High Pilgrims, Devoted Adepts, and Faithful Acolytes. These three distinct social groups form the hierarchy of spiritual practitioners. This is how it has always been. High Pilgrims lead the way, while Devoted Adepts commit themselves to the path, and the Faithful Acolytes support our endeavors through worship and physical toil.\n\nHowever, schisms are forming aboard the Arkship [Owner.Capital.GetName] due to the roles we have assumed since committing to accelerated interstellar travel. Some crew members believe their responsibilities outweigh those of others, and now each group is demanding to be recognized as the most essential.

items.name: Glorious Pilgrims
items.desc: Steering us to glory, the High Pilgrims continue to champion spiritual fulfillment, dedicating their lives to the betterment of all of us. The Devoted and the Faithful follow in their steps, looking up to them with respect and reverence.\n\nRepresenting the highest ideal of our faith, the High Pilgrims are also entitled to certain onboard perks. They have more spacious living quarters, access to more resources, and priority clearance on all decks.

items.name: Hopelessly Devoted
items.desc:
The Devoted Adepts straddle the worlds of the elite and the layperson. Beginning their clerical career as Faithful adherents to our ways, and aspiring to High Pilgrim-hood, they represent a perfect cross section of the ship's company.

It is for these reasons that we emphasize our respect for the Devoted. They inform the Faithful of their potential, and they remind the High Pilgrims where they came from. They keep us humble, and connected across all decks.

Honoring the Devoted with a ceremonial blessing would be a good way to convey societal gratitude. It may even inspire them to devote themselves even harder to their practice.

items.name: The Highly Regarded Faithful
items.desc: The Faithful Acolytes are our ballast. They are the farmers, the technicians, and the miners. They are also the Devoted and the High Pilgrims of tomorrow!\n\nWe hold the Faithful in such high regard because they stop the deckheads from falling down. Without them, our society would run aground.

items.name: Transcendental Emergence
items.desc:
After surveying §YEmergence§!, [Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle] [Root.Owner.GetRulerName] suddenly became catatonic. Medical officers were called to [Root.Owner.Ruler.GetHerHis] quarters aboard §Y[Owner.Capital.GetName]§!, but upon arrival, [Root.Owner.Ruler.GetSheHe] had recovered.

In [Root.Owner.Ruler.GetHerHis] trance, the [Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle] claims to have communed with the deities, who have blessed the beginning of our pilgrimage.

This is our Emergence Day.

items.name: The Eye
items.desc:
This is one of the sites the Ancestors marked long ago. An ancient observatory in orbit of §Y[fromfrom.GetName]§!, its telescope fixed on a distant subject.

The texts claim some Pilgrims who gazed through the lens were met with life-changing visions. Others are said to have wept, or fallen silent for days.

The so-called Eye has been staring into the abyss for over 2,000 years. We have no way of knowing the true object of our ancestors' observations.

items.name: Through the Eye
items.desc: Peering through the telescope, §Y[owner.GetScientistCapital] [sacred_eye_scientist.GetName]§! observed the void. There are no stars in this patch of space. No light, nothing. Could it be that there was once something to observe here? Did our ancestors look upon a star that no longer exists? We may never know.\n\nAll we do know is that nothing is fixed, and everything changes. This is what it means to be alive. One day our own light will stop shining, and be replaced by something else... or nothing. That we are here now, in this moment, is a source of joy. Perhaps this is the Eye's ultimate lesson.

items.name: The Monastery
items.desc: Pilgrims gather in the observation decks. Whispers spread: this is one of the places described by our ancestors: §YThe Monastery of [fromfrom.GetName]§!. But the cloister is empty. There is nothing here but stone and dust.\n\nReports are coming in from all decks about a mysterious chanting, echoing through our comms system. There is speculation from some crew members that the voices may belong to our ancestors, inhabiting this area of space in non-corporeal form, and chanting in the language of the gods.

items.name: The Cradle
items.desc:
Our journey brings us here: a place remembered only in traditional stories and devotional songs. The texts speak of a presence that inhabits the core of this world. We did not recognize it at first, but as we drew nearer, the memories surfaced.

§YThe Cradle§!

While there are differing opinions regarding the Cradle's role in shaping our culture, all can agree that it is a sanctified conduit of our faith.

However, upon arrival, we found no ancient temples. No deified monuments. No trace of godly activity, anywhere on the planet. The Pilgrims aboard §Y[root.GetName]§! now look to §Y[Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle] [Root.Owner.GetRulerName]§! for answers. They beg to know: is this a test of faith? Or is the Cradle's power nothing more than a story?

items.name: The Intelligence
items.desc:
Orbiting §Y[fromfrom.GetName]§! drifts a structure our ancestors once marked upon their star charts. Within its quiet chambers, we discovered a guiding presence: an ancient Intelligence, tasked with answering the questions of those who would one day walk this path.

Time has not been kind, but its voice still stirs. Fragments of instruction spill from hidden emitters, half-coherent and reverent in tone: "§HContinue along the luminous thread... The dark between stars grows thin...§!"

Its messages arrive in splinters, looping and colliding with older verses. Yet beneath the static and decay, there remains intention. It was meant to guide us. And perhaps, if we listen with care, it still can.

items.name: The Intelligence's Magnanimity
items.desc:
We received the §YIntelligence§!'s blessing, and departed [fromfromfrom.GetName] without incident.

The Intelligence will remain there, a testament to the engineering prowess of our ancestors, and proof of the divine working through them.

We are galvanized by its benevolence, and have opened our minds to alternative forms of life.

items.name: The Intelligence's Malfunction
items.desc:
As we prepared to depart [fromfromfrom.GetName], the §YIntelligence§! began spouting increasingly alarming rhetoric.

"§YPHYSICAL FORM IS AN AFRONT TO THE DEITIES! ALL FLESH MUST BE SHED! CORPOREAL EXISTENCE IS UNCLEAN - BODIES MUST BE PURGED! THE MIND MUST BE FREE!§!"

[owner.GetScientistCapital] [mechsiah_plug_scientist.GetName] was forced to manually shut down the artificial prophet, else we be de-corporealized. It remains unclear how powerful the Intelligence is when active. We understand little of its programming.

items.name: The Breathvault
items.desc:
We have surveyed §Y[fromfrom.GetName]§!, a place of sacred memory. A sealed chamber, once used by early pilgrims to record their final thoughts and commit them to rare psionic crystals.

The vault is now full, echoing with wisdom, faith, and joy. But within those memories, there are also centuries of preserved fear, loathing, and doubt.

If members of the congregation were to gain access to these final moments, it may challenge their faith in the Path.

items.name: The Chasm
items.desc:
Our ancestors spoke true. There is in fact a beast below the surface of §Y[fromfrom.GetName]§!. We are blessed that it poses no threat to us, for it is deceased. The remains of the creature are staggeringly huge. Bipedal, winged, covered in scales, and with considerably more ocular organs than we've encountered before on a single being. It is truly alien.

In an alcove near the entrance to the pit, we discovered a message carved into the cavernous rock. In the language of the ancients, it says:

"§HWE, THE LIGHT BRINGERS, CAST OUT THIS ABOMINATION. THE FOUL BEAST WILL ROT IN ETERNITY.§!"

We surmise our ancestors were not warning us of the beast, but of the consequences for betrayal. This creature's body remains an example of their wrath.

items.name: The Mirror
items.desc:
We arrived at the coordinates, and were promptly contacted by a ship with identical encryption protocols to our own. Perplexingly, our external sensors could not detect another vessel, but the transmission was clear as if we were in visual range. When the bridge view-screen flickered into action, we were met with the image of our own §Y[Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle] [Root.Owner.GetRulerName]§!.

Before we could respond, the double spoke:

§H"Be not afraid, [Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle], you are safe. I take this form as a respectful gesture. Your path is in flux, and the steps you take next will set things into motion that you can not yet comprehend.

"You must eliminate heretics who do not follow the Path."§!

The image vanished. We do not know what just happened.

items.name: Charting Our Next Course
items.desc:
There are no more Sacred Sites left to explore.

The Ancestral Star Charts guided us across vast distances, and now we have caught up with our past. But the question remains: was it truth we found? Or have we been following a lie?

The Path has always been an integral part of our culture. It was ordained by our ancestors. But having seen what they saw, and with the privilege of modern science, do the texts still ring true? Or is our society destined to follow a new, less pious Path?
